Write appends the compared points to a verification log (Dataset Curator columns + U_pred + U_cfd) that is retraining data and a training envelope for Prediction Confidence. ML screening prediction, not CFD: use it to compare options, then confirm anything that matters with a Wind Study (planning authorities do not accept surrogate results).  Wind Predictor              Run ONNX wind-field prediction end-to-end. Computes SDF, building height, Zrelative, U/Uref, direction features from geometry, assembles the 8-channel input tensor, runs ONNX inference, and outputs predicted wind speeds. Supports legacy 1ch (U), 2ch (U + k) and new 4ch (U + k + Uroof + kroof) models. ML screening prediction, not CFD: use it to compare options, then confirm anything that matters with a Wind Study (planning authorities do not accept surrogate results). Check a result with Prediction Confidence and Verify Prediction. Method: Kastner et al. (2026), SSRN preprint 6401886, doi:10.2139/ssrn.6401886.  Wind Predictor Cloud              Predict a pedestrian wind-speed field from buildings without running CFD, using the hosted Eddy3D model (Yel 1.0, a 512x512 image GAN). Rasterizes the buildings and the analysis plane into the model's input image, sends it to the API, and returns the predicted wind speeds plus a colored result mesh. Runs on Eddy3D's server: needs internet, no GPU and no model download, and the free server may need a minute to wake up. For a local GPU run over arbitrary points and multiple wind directions, use Wind Predictor with a model from ML Model instead. ML screening prediction, not CFD: use it to compare options, then confirm anything that matters with a Wind Study (planning authorities do not accept surrogate results). Method: Kastner & Dogan (2023), Building and Environment 242:110384, doi:10.1016/j.buildenv.2023.110384.  Wind Comfort Predictor ML              Calculate Pedestrian Wind Comfort using predicted wind fields from the ONNX model. ML screening prediction, not CFD: use it to compare options, then confirm anything that matters with a Wind Study (planning authorities do not accept surrogate results). Method: Kastner et al. (2026), SSRN preprint 6401886, doi:10.2139/ssrn.6401886.  Dataset Curator              Compute and export wind dataset features from analysis points and building geometry.  Dataset Reader              Read processed CSV datasets back into Grasshopper. Supports mag_U and all spatial features.  Interpolate UMag              Resample direction-specific wind-magnitude fields onto a new point grid (nearest-neighbour average, with direction-specific rotation). Prepares grids for GAN applications.  MRT Dataset Curator              Export the solved MRT field as a machine-learning dataset: one row per sensor per hour with spatial features, hourly climate drivers and the MRT/UTCI targets.

docs.title: Main Components
docs.text: CHT Air Cavity              A closed air cavity: solved as buoyant air (natural convection), coupled to the solids around it.  CHT Boundary              Boundary condition on one face of the analysis box: fixed surface temperature, convective film (h + air temperature), or adiabatic. Unassigned faces are adiabatic.  CHT Exterior Air              A volume of air that is meshed but never solved: the solids facing it get the surface film set here. Cheaper and steadier than solving a cavity, and the ISO 10211 convention.  CHT Material              Solid material for CHT heat transfer analysis. Catalog values (ISO 10456 / Incropera) seed the properties; wire a number to override one.  CHT Solid              A solid region of the CHT assembly: closed Brep/Mesh + material. The union of all solids and cavities must fill a rectangular box (the analysis domain).  CHT Case              Build a conjugate heat transfer case from solids, air cavities, exterior air and boundaries. Wire the Case output into the Run component (Containerized engine). Method: Kastner & Dogan (2020), SimAUD 2020 405-412, https://www.researchgate.net/publication/346039320_Solving_Thermal_Bridging_Problems_for_Architectural_Applications_with_OpenFOAM.  HAM Climate              Air conditions on one face of a HAM wall. One value per input is a constant; a list is a stepped schedule (one entry per step, hourly by default).  HAM Material              Porous material for a HAM wall: a hamFoam material model plus density, specific heat and conductivity. The five HAMSTAD benchmark models arrive with their published properties; the rest supply curves only, so wire rho, c and lambda1.  HAM Wall              Layered build-up for a HAM case, OUTSIDE layer first. Materials and thicknesses are read in parallel, so their counts must match.  HAM Case              Build a heat-and-moisture case for a layered wall. Wire the Case output into the Run component (Containerized engine — hamFoam ships only in the container). Pick a Preset to reproduce one of the two HAMSTAD benchmark tutorials.

docs.title: Main Components
docs.text: WRF Geo Data              Check and download the WPS static geographical data geogrid needs. Reports what is installed against the mandatory field list, and fetches the bundle that closes the gap.  WRF Met Data              Download the meteorological GRIB files that drive a WRF run. The file list and the Vtable are shown before you fetch anything, so a window can be checked first.  WRF Domain              Define a WRF domain and the parent grids nested around it. Domains are specified INNERMOST-FIRST: the grid you set here is the finest one, and each nest ratio adds a coarser parent around it. Outputs the project the WRF Namelist component writes, and the domain extents as rectangles centred on the innermost domain.  WRF Namelist              Write namelist.wps for a WRF project. The text is produced on every solve; the Write toggle saves it to /run_wps/namelist.wps.  WRF Progress              Progress of the WRF pipeline in the working directory, with an expected time to completion once wrf.exe is stepping. Toggle Live to re-poll once a second.  WRF Run              Run the WRF pipeline in the two launches it needs: the WPS half (geogrid, ungrib, metgrid), then run_wrf/namelist.input, built from that output, then the WRF half (real, wrf). Writes one script per launch into the project folder. The scripts and commands are always shown, even before you run, so a failing run can be reproduced by hand.  WRF Animate              Loop through a WRF run's history frames while Play is on. Wire Frame into the WRF Probe's Frame input; each tick advances one frame and recomputes the display.  WRF Map              Lat/lon graticule with labels, the run's own coastline from LANDMASK, and a site marker — in the same plane as the WRF Probe points and WRF Domain rectangles. Wire Labels + Label Points (and Site Label + Site Point) to a Text Tag to draw the annotations.  WRF Probe              Sample a surface field of a WRF run over the whole domain, one point per grid cell. Points are in metres about the domain centre, matching the WRF Domain rectangles. Wire Points + Values into the Scalar Field Viewer, or Points + Vectors into the Vector Field Viewer, for the display.  WRF ABL              Build an atmospheric boundary layer from a WRF site series. The output plugs into the same socket as Outdoor's ABL, so it drives the wind study, Outdoor+, FluidX3D and LBM alike. Note this is uniform in plan: one log-law profile at the site, not a spatially varying inflow.  WRF Weather              Read a WRF run at a site and build the weather an Eddy3D case needs. Feed the Weather output to Timing Parameters and urbanMicroclimateFoam runs on WRF instead of an EPW. Start HOY and Duration describe the window the run actually covers — wire them too, because every hour outside it is deliberately NaN and will stop OpenFOAM rather than quietly simulate a day of 0 degC.

docs.title: Main Components
docs.text: PALM Domain              Define the PALM-4U grid: cells, spacing and the site's latitude/longitude. The domain's lower-left corner sits at the Origin point in the Rhino model (world origin by default), with y pointing north. Feed the output to PALM Case and PALM Run.  PALM Land Cover              Fetch OpenStreetMap land cover over the PALM domain and classify it into PALM surface types. Feed the output into PALM Case's Land Cover input. Urban block polygons are skipped and reported — paint those by hand.  PALM Case              Write the PALM-4U case: the static driver (terrain, buildings, tree canopies and the ground surface mosaic, rasterized onto the domain grid) and the _p3d namelist that runs it. Geometry inputs take trees of meshes/Breps; branches are flattened — everything wired belongs to ONE scene. Ground not covered by any input takes the Ground Cover class. The viewport shows the domain, its boundary conditions and the rasterized surface the solver will actually see.  PALM Settings              Steer the PALM-4U run: duration, wind, temperature and outputs. Forcing is idealized (constant wind, cyclic boundaries). Comfort switches on radiation and the biometeorology module, whose PET/UTCI/MRT maps are PALM-4U's point.  PALM Progress              Progress of the PALM run in the case folder, from its RUN_CONTROL table. Toggle Live to re-poll once a second.  PALM Run              Run PALM-4U. Writes a launch script into the case PALM Case wrote, then starts the published PALM container. The script and command are always shown, even before you run, so a failing run can be reproduced by hand.  PALM Results              Read a PALM output field: one variable, one time frame, as values and a colored mesh over the domain. Variables and times available in the case are listed on every solve.

docs.title: Main Components
docs.text: Noise Area Emitter              A fixed AREA source of sound for Noise Run, to ask "what if": a car park, a courtyard, a loading yard, a market. Give it a closed curve (its z is the source height, m) and a sound power level dB(A) PER SQUARE METRE — or a data sheet's eight octave levels per square metre — and the hours it runs in the day (12 h), evening (4 h) and night (8 h). The area is cut into point sources that share it, so the total power is the area times the level, whatever the grid. No directivity, no reflection off the walls round it. For one unit use Noise Emitter, for a line Noise Line Emitter.  Noise Emitter              A fixed point source of sound for Noise Run, to ask "what if": a rooftop plant, a generator, a car park gate, an event stage. Give it a point (its z is the source height, m) and a sound power level dB(A) — or a data sheet's eight octave levels, 63 Hz to 8 kHz, which win — and the hours it runs in the day (12 h), evening (4 h) and night (8 h). It radiates equally in every direction, with no reflection off the wall or roof beside it. Wire it next to the road sources and compare two runs, with and without it.  Noise Line Emitter              A fixed LINE source of sound for Noise Run, to ask "what if": a conveyor, a rail spur, a row of loading bays, a queue. Give it a curve (its z is the source height, m) and a sound power level dB(A) PER METRE — or a data sheet's eight octave levels per metre — and the hours it runs in the day (12 h), evening (4 h) and night (8 h). It is cut into point sources like a road, with no directivity and no reflection off the wall beside it. For one unit at one place use Noise Emitter.  Noise Receivers              Where the levels are asked for: a ground grid inside a disc at pedestrian height (1.5 m; set 4 m to match an END strategic map), and a point in front of every facade at every storey of the buildings wired in. Facade levels are free-field, without the reflection off the facade they stand before, as CNOSSOS and the END define them.  Road Source              A road as a CNOSSOS-EU line source: its centreline, a daily traffic total, the heavy-vehicle share and a speed. One item per curve, or one value for all of them. Feed the sources to Noise Run.  The daily total is split 70/20/10 % over day (07-19), evening (19-23) and night (23-07), and heavies half-and-half between two-axle and multi-axle trucks — the neutral defaults when a count says no more.  Roads From OSM              Every driveable road around a site from OpenStreetMap, as Road Sources with STREET-TYPE DEFAULTS for traffic: a residential street a few hundred vehicles a day, a primary road fifteen thousand, a motorway sixty thousand. A posted maxspeed wins over the class speed; four lanes carry twice the two-lane default. These are placeholders for a count — override the roads that matter with Road Source. Roads are placed in metres east/north of the site, at z = 0.  Noise Run              Road-traffic noise after CNOSSOS-EU (Directive 2015/996, 2021/1226 coefficients): the emission of every road and the propagation to every receiver — divergence, air absorption, the ground effect on the mean plane, diffraction over roofs and crests — summed per octave band and period into Lday, Levening, Lnight and Lden. Lden (L_den) is the day-evening-night level of the EU Environmental Noise Directive 2002/49/EC: the long-term A-weighted level in dB(A) over a whole day, with the 4 h evening counted +5 dB and the 8 h night +10 dB (the day is 12 h), so night and evening noise weigh more than their hours.  PROTOTYPE LIMITS: homogeneous atmospheric conditions only (no favourable-propagation share, so distant levels run a little low); no facade reflections; no path around a corner (a receiver behind a block gets the over-the-roof path only, which reads low); one ground factor for the whole site; no rail, aircraft or industry. Not a compliance calculation.  Method: CNOSSOS-EU, Commission Directive (EU) 2015/996 Annex II (road emission §2.2, propagation §2.5), coefficients per Delegated Directive (EU) 2021/1226, https://eur-lex.europa.eu/eli/dir/2015/996/oj — pinned against NoiseModelling (Université Gustave Eiffel) on the ISO/TR 17534-4 cases.  Noise Map              Colours a run's receivers in the END 5 dB bands (yellow from 50-55, orange at 60, red at 65, blue above 80): a ground mesh of the grid, a vertical quad per facade receiver, and the points, values and colours behind them for custom tagging. Pick Lden or a single period. Lden (L_den) is the day-evening-night level of the EU Environmental Noise Directive 2002/49/EC: the long-term A-weighted level in dB(A) over a whole day, with the 4 h evening counted +5 dB and the 8 h night +10 dB (the day is 12 h), so night and evening noise weigh more than their hours.

docs.title: Main Components
docs.text: Cut Fill              Cut and fill between the existing ground and a proposed grading: where the proposed surface sits below the ground is CUT (red), where it sits above is FILL (blue), and the volumes come with the mesh. Compare design options on one depth scale (Depth Range), read the balance (Net: positive = material to bring in), and the bands say how deep the work goes.  Both surfaces are sampled at the centre of every raster cell inside the proposed surface's footprint; a cell's volume is depth × cell area, so halve the cell size where the grading is finer than the cells. Ground the proposed surface does not reach is not earthworks; a cell the existing ground misses is left out and counted. Depths within 5 mm of zero are unchanged.  Terrain Diagram              The diagrams a grading is read by, off one raster of the ground: elevation or slope bands as a coloured mesh, contours with major lines and their level labels, and spot levels with a downhill arrow at any points you wire. Set Range to hold one colour scale while the ground is edited or design options are compared, and Slope Bands to the gradients that matter (2 % drainage, 5 % and 8.33 % access ramps, 33 % mowing).  The ground is sampled once at the centre of every cell; slope is Horn's 3 x 3 gradient in percent (100 % = 45°), and reads low in the outermost ring of cells, where a neighbour is missing. Contour levels are multiples of the interval counted from elevation 0, so a line keeps its level when the ground changes.

docs.title: Eddy3D - Outdoor+
docs.text: The urban microclimate module of the Eddy3D plugin, using urbanMicroclimateFoam (uMFoam)

docs.title: Overview
docs.text:
urbanMicroclimateFoam (uMFoam) is an open-source solver built on OpenFOAM for modeling urban microclimates. It simulates coupled physical processes including:

  • Turbulent airflow
  • Heat and moisture transport in air
  • Radiative heat exchange (shortwave and longwave)
  • Heat and moisture storage in building materials (HAM model)
  • Urban vegetation heat balance

Learn more at the official repository: 🔗 urbanMicroclimateFoam GitHub

docs.title: 1. Install an OpenFOAM engine
docs.text:
Eddy3D runs OpenFOAM through one of these engines (pick one):

  • Docker or Podman (Windows & macOS, recommended): Install Docker Desktop or install Podman Desktop. Eddy3D pulls the same pre-configured OpenFOAM 12 image automatically with either engine — Auto-detect prefers Podman and falls back to Docker.
    • Docker has the bigger ecosystem and the most familiar tooling, but Docker Desktop requires a paid subscription for larger companies and runs its containers through a privileged background daemon.
    • Podman is free and open-source with no licensing restrictions, runs daemonless, and executes containers rootless by default for a smaller attack surface — a good default on shared or locked-down machines.
  • blueCFD-Core 2024 (Windows): Download blueCFD-Core. Install into a folder without spaces in the name (e.g. C:\blueCFD-Core\2024) — a location like C:\Program Files\... breaks the OpenFOAM toolchain and the UMF solver can never be built or found.
  • WSL (Windows): WSL installation guide.

docs.title: 2. Install the Eddy3D Plugin for Grasshopper (Rhino)
docs.text:
• Open Rhinoceros
  • Run the PackageManager command
  • Search for Eddy3D
  • Click Install and restart Rhino

docs.title: Verify Installation
docs.text:
Use the Check Installation component in Grasshopper:

  • Set Check = True
  • Set Install UrbanMicroclimateFoam = True if it’s a new install

The console will automatically install the necessary files.

docs.title: 1. Load Template
docs.text:
• Use the Templates component
  • Right-click > select UMCF.Templates.MicroclimateSimulation.gh

docs.title: 2. Add Weather File
docs.text:
• Connect an EPW file to the Weather component
  • This enables time settings in the Timing component

docs.title: Air Region
docs.text:
Use the Air Region component to set:

  • ABL Conditions: Wind speed, height, direction
  • Domain Dimensions:
  • Cell Size
  • Front Add, Back Add, Sides Add, Top Add
  • Refinement Box Add

docs.title: Solid Region (Buildings)
docs.text:
Inputs:

  • Building mesh geometry
  • Material (default: Hamstad5Brick)
  • Mesh refinement (optional)
  • Indoor temperature (°C)

docs.title: Vegetation Region
docs.text:
Inputs:

  • Vegetation mesh
  • Leaf Area Density (LAD)
  • Vegetation properties
  • Mesh refinement (optional)

Default vegetation values are found in constant/air/vegetationProperties.

docs.title: Simulation Settings
docs.text:
Configure with the Simulation Settings component:

  • Number of CPUs (e.g., 10 recommended)
  • maxFluidIteration (higher = better resolution)

docs.title: Write and Run the Case
docs.text:
Use the UMCF Case component to prepare files and view logs.

  1. Prepare Simulation – generate mesh
  2. Run Simulation – execute solver

Run both steps with the same processor mode (single/parallel).

After simulation: - View results with .foam in ParaView - 0 folder = initial conditions - Output folders based on controlDict: - startTime = 0, endTime = 43200, deltaT = 3600 (i.e., 12 hours)

docs.title: Visualize Results (in Rhino/Grasshopper)
docs.text:
Use a quad mesh plane at desired height in the Probing section.

Probe for: - Temperature (T) - Velocity (U) - Humidity (w)

Steps:

  1. Generate mesh plane
  2. Click Run
  3. Enable Probing to load results
  4. Use Hour Slider to view time-based results

docs.title: Output Types
docs.text:
• Velocity (U)
  • Temperature (T)
  • Humidity (w)

Visualizations are available both in Grasshopper and ParaView.

docs.title: Need Help?
docs.text: Visit the UMCF GitHub Issues page or reach out to your instructor/supervisor for support.

docs.title: Methods & citations
docs.text:
Eddy3D writes cases for solvers other people wrote — the physics belongs to the engines, and results cite the engine (OpenFOAM, urbanMicroclimateFoam, OpenLB, FluidX3D, Radiance, EnergyPlus; see the credits). What Eddy3D's own papers own is the workflow wrapped around those engines: how the mesh is built, how a year of weather becomes a handful of solves, how a facade pressure reaches an airflow network. A study that relies on one of these methods cites the paper next to the engine.

The preferred general citation for Eddy3D is Kastner & Dogan (2022), Building and Environment 212:108639, ResearchGate. The repository ships a machine-readable CITATION.cff (GitHub's Cite this repository button), and the full list is on the publications page.

docs.title: Where a citation reaches you
docs.text:
Each published method is cited in three places, all fed from one table in the code (MetaFOAM.Lib/Eddy3DCitations.cs), so they cannot drift apart:

  1. The component's description — the tooltip in Grasshopper ends with Method: …, and the component pages on this site mirror that text (the exporter renders them from the live components).
  2. This page — the map from paper to components to dictionaries below.
  3. The generated OpenFOAM dictionaries that implement a method carry a // Method: … line directly under the Eddy3D banner, so a case folder found in the wild names the paper next to the plugin version that wrote it. Line comments only — the parser strips them on re-read.
// ------------------------------------------------------------------------- //
// Generated by Eddy3D 1.10.0.827 — https://www.eddy3d.com
// ------------------------------------------------------------------------- //
// Method: Kastner & Dogan (2020), Journal of Building Performance Simulation 13(1):59-68, doi:10.1080/19401493.2019.1692906
/*--------------------------------*- C++ -*----------------------------------*\
  =========                 |
  \\      /  F ield         | OpenFOAM: The Open Source CFD Toolbox
...

docs.title: Published methods → components → dictionaries
docs.text: Paper Published method Components Generated dictionaries Kastner & Dogan (2020), J. Build. Perform. Simul. 13(1):59–68, ResearchGate — precursor: Kastner & Dogan (2018), eSim 2018, ResearchGate Cylindrical meshing. One cylindrical blockMesh serves every wind direction; the cylinder's side patches switch between inlet and outlet per direction, so a study of n directions meshes once instead of n times. Validated against wind-tunnel data; recommended from eight directions up. Cylinder Domain, Outdoor Case mesh/system/blockMeshDict; every case_NNN/0/* field file that carries the switched side patches Kastner & Dogan (2022), Build. Environ. 212:108639, ResearchGate — precursor: Kastner & Dogan (2019), Building Simulation 2019, ResearchGate Decoupled annual outdoor thermal comfort. Hourly wind directions are clustered (k-means) into a simulation budget; each RANS solve becomes a spatial lookup table; velocity amplification factors turn the lookup into an hourly wind-speed matrix; trees are Darcy–Forchheimer porous zones; MRT comes from a Radiance two-phase DDS shortwave chain plus view-factor longwave exchange; hourly UTCI closes the loop. Validated against on-site weather stations. Wind Rose Cluster, Velocity Amplification Factors (VAF), Tree, MRT, MRT Solve, UTCI (Simulation) case_NNN/constant/fvModels (tree porosity) Dogan, Kastner & Mermelstein (2021), Build. Environ. 196:107762, ResearchGate Surfer. Discretises every model surface, computes probe-to-surface view factors with a ray-cast occlusion test, simulates exterior surface temperatures in EnergyPlus, and assembles MRT from surface temperatures, sky temperature and a solar-gain ΔMRT (effective radiant field). RMSE 1.8 °C (surfaces) and 2.0 °C (MRT) against measurements at ~80× the speed of a full simulation. MRT View Factors, SurfaceTemp (EnergyPlus), MRT Solve, MRT — (Radiance and EnergyPlus inputs, not OpenFOAM) Dogan & Kastner (2021), Build. Simul. 14(4):1189–1200, ResearchGate — precursor: Dogan & Kastner (2018), IBPC 2018, ResearchGate Facade pressure coefficients for airflow networks. An automated OpenFOAM wind study writes the surface pressure coefficient Cp = (p − p∞)/(½ρU∞²) for arbitrary building shapes and context, probed on the facades and exported as the wind-pressure-coefficient arrays an EnergyPlus AirflowNetwork expects. Run Settings → Pressure Coefficient, Airflow Network Cp case_NNN/system/Cp; the pressureCoefficients function object in case_NNN/system/controlDict De Simone, Kastner & Dogan (2021), Building Simulation 2021, ResearchGate Airborne-pathogen passive scalar. An isothermal OpenFOAM ventilation case carries an airborne-pathogen tracer as a passive scalar injected from an emitter zone, so plan layouts and inlet/outlet positions can be compared for exposure. Benchmarked against a CFD test case and a tracer-gas restaurant study. Indoor Case, Viral Emitter system/controlDict (scalarTransport_viral), constant/fvModels (the source) Kastner & Dogan (2023), Build. Environ. 242:110384, ResearchGate GAN wind surrogate. An image-to-image GAN trained on RANS results predicts a pedestrian-level wind field from a rasterised building layout in a fraction of a second — the hosted Yel 1.0 model. Wind Predictor (Cloud) — Kastner, Chen, Manivasakan, Michalatos, Karadag & Dogan (2026), SSRN 6401886, doi:10.2139/ssrn.6401886 (not on ResearchGate yet) Physics-informed GAN with arbitrary input and output channels — the 8-channel ONNX family (Yel 2.0, Esen, Poyraz) that runs locally over arbitrary points and several wind directions. ML Model, Wind Predictor, Wind Comfort Predictor (ML) — Kastner & Dogan (2020), SimAUD 2020, 405–412, ResearchGate Thermal bridges with OpenFOAM. Conjugate heat transfer through layered assemblies solved with chtMultiRegionFoam, set up from Grasshopper geometry. CHT Case system/controlDict of the CHT case Rahimi, Alvarez, Stone, Berardi & Kastner (2025), Build. Environ. 285:113637, ResearchGate — precursor: Rahimi, Berardi, Stone & Kastner (2024), IBPC 2024, ResearchGate Validation, not a method. urbanMicroclimateFoam (heat, air, moisture, radiation, vegetation), run through Eddy3D Outdoor+, against weather stations on the Georgia Tech campus: temperature RMSE down to 1.03 °C, humidity RMSE 4.78 %, vegetation-driven cooling up to 2.1 °C. The physics stays Kubilay, Derome & Carmeliet's — cite the solver for results. Outdoor+ Case — (the dictionaries are the solver's)

docs.title: Related work that is not an Eddy3D feature
docs.text:
• Rahimi, Kastner & Berardi (2025), Building and Environment 276:112858, ResearchGate — convective heat transfer and humidity in unsteady microclimate CFD with a customised buoyantHumidityPimpleFoam. A solver study; Outdoor+ models humidity through urbanMicroclimateFoam's own HAM physics instead. Also: Rahimi, Kastner & Berardi (2024), How much computational complexity is necessary to model relevant aspects in microclimate urban physics?, IABP 2024, ResearchGate.
  • Karadag, Smyl & Kastner (2026), Sustainable Cities and Society 148:107614, doi:10.1016/j.scs.2026.107614 — the review the 11 | ML panel sits in: where surrogate wind models stand, and what they can and cannot replace. Not on ResearchGate yet.

docs.title: Applications of the annual comfort workflow
docs.text:
Studies that used Eddy3D rather than extended it — useful as worked examples of the decoupled workflow at neighbourhood and city scale:

  • Young, Kastner, Dogan, Chokhachian, Mokhtar & Reinhart (2021), Building and Environment 208:108577, ResearchGate — outdoor thermal comfort along cycling routes at varying levels of physical accuracy, against bike-ridership counts in Cambridge, MA.
  • Natanian, Kastner, Dogan & Auer (2020), Energy and Buildings 224:110283, ResearchGate — annual outdoor thermal comfort autonomy and energy balance across Mediterranean typologies, using the hourly wind factors.
  • Kastner & Dogan (2020), SimAUD 2020, 85–91, ResearchGate — predicting space usage on a university campus by multi-objective assessment of outdoor thermal comfort.

docs.title: Outdoor+ Solver Troubleshooting
docs.text: Field notes for runs of the Outdoor+ (urbanMicroclimateFoam) case that mesh fine but stop during the solve. For installation problems see Setup Troubleshooting; for the workflow itself see First Steps.

docs.title: Where to look first
docs.text:
Everything the solver prints lands in the case folder (the Working Directory of the Outdoor+ Case component, one sub-folder per case name):

  • the solve log — the last Solving for solid region <name> line before the error tells you which region diverged (buildings, terrain, or a vegetation region);
  • checkMesh_<region>.txt — one per meshed region, written at the end of meshing;
  • the *_dump fields (Ts_dump, pc_dump, ws_dump, Crel_dump) written into the last time folder when the solid solver gives up — load them in ParaView to see where the field ran away.

docs.title: This is going to crash (Ts)! … Cannot decrease time step further
docs.text:
The solid regions (buildings, terrain) are solved with an adaptive sub-time-step inside each hourly fluid step. After every solid iteration the solver checks that the solid temperature Ts stays within 0 K < Ts < 423.15 K (150 °C) and that the capillary pressure pc stays negative. If not, it prints This is going to crash (Ts)! (or (pc)!), reverts the fields, halves the time step and retries. When the time step reaches minDeltaT (the written case uses 1e-6 s) it aborts with Cannot decrease time step further.

The message says nothing about the cause, so always read the log: the last Solving for solid region ... line names the region (buildings or terrain) that diverged. Known causes, in the order to check:

docs.title: 1. A light hygroscopic wall material
docs.text:
Materials with a moisture model and a very low density/conductivity — CalciumSilicate (ρ 270 kg/m³, λ 0.06 W/mK) and Hamstad5Insulation (ρ 130) — diverge in the coupled heat-and-moisture solve as soon as the air field has converged and the surface starts receiving solar radiation (seen on an internal case, 2026-10). It is not a sufficient cause on its own: a flat-terrain courtyard case with a CalciumSilicate inner layer ran through sunrise without a single time-step halving.

Integer-wired Material inputs

The Material input of Building Material, Terrain Surface Material and Soil Material expects a material name. Older documents wire a Number Slider into it; the plugin then resolves the number by position in the dropdown list, so slider 1 silently means CalciumSilicate. Prefer the dropdown (right-click the input) or a panel with the name.

index name ρ (kg/m³) λ (W/mK) moisture model 0 AsphaltConcrete 2100 0.75 yes 1 CalciumSilicate 270 0.06 yes, strongly hygroscopic 2 Hamstad5Brick 1600 0.68 yes (plugin default) 3 Hamstad5Insulation 130 0.04 yes, strongly hygroscopic 4 Hamstad5Mortar 1900 0.82 yes 5 HamstadBrick 2005 0.5 yes 6 HamstadCase2 1600 0.68 yes 7 HamstadConcrete 2400 1.6 yes 8 HamstadPlaster 790 0.2 yes 9 Impermeable 2400 1.0 none — heat conduction and storage only 10 PorousAsphalt 2000 0.7 yes 11 SabaBrick 1608 0.73 yes 12 SabaBrickMod 1608 0.73 yes 13 Savonnieres (buildings) / Soil (terrain) 1830 / 1150 1.2 / 1.5 yes 14 Soil (buildings) / VanGenuchten (terrain) 1150 / 1500 1.5 / 1.0 yes

Remedy: use Impermeable for both wall layers (stable, models heat storage and conduction, no moisture in the wall), or a heavy hygroscopic material such as Hamstad5Brick or HamstadConcrete. To bisect, set every material (walls, terrain surface, soil) to Impermeable once; if that run finishes, bring the moisture models back one region at a time.

docs.title: 2. Inverted cells from the wall extrusion
docs.text:
The solid buildings and terrain are made by extruding the surface inwards (two layers, 0.1 m each by default, 10 cells per layer at expansion ratio 1.2). Wherever the surface has a feature narrower than roughly twice the wall thickness — a 20 cm ledge, a fin, a thin parapet, sliver triangles between unwelded faces — the offset prisms cross and checkMesh_buildings.txt reports negative cell volumes. The solver then fails on the very first solid step, at t of a few seconds, with the same message as above.

The plugin reads the checkMesh logs and raises a warning on Run when it finds negative volumes (since 1.14). Remedy: remove or thicken the thin features in Rhino, pass the façades through Gmsh Mesh, and re-mesh.

Small determinants are expected

checkMesh -allGeometry always reports many cells with small determinant (< 0.001) in the building and terrain regions. The thinnest extruded cell is about 4 mm thick under a face that is 1–3 m wide; that aspect ratio gives tiny determinants by construction and does not affect the one-dimensional conduction through the wall. Only negative volumes, incorrectly oriented faces or severely non-orthogonal faces in a solid region are a problem.

docs.title: 3. An air field that has not converged
docs.text: The air region is solved to steady state inside every hourly step, from whatever field it has. The first ~100 iterations of a cold start are a violent transient — the log shows Min/max T: pinned to 273.15 / 373.15 K and very large |U| — that has died out by iteration ~100 and converged by ~500. Max Fluid Iterations below 300 freezes that transient into hour 1 and hands the solid regions a garbage boundary condition. Keep it at 300 or more; 500–1000 for the first hour is cheap insurance.

docs.title: 4. Time-step controls
docs.text: Only after the three points above: Simulation Settings → Min Delta T (1e-6 s in the written case; a wired value overrides it) and Initial Solid Time Step Factor reduced, to give the solid solver more room. This delays a material-driven divergence rather than curing it.

docs.title: This is going to crash (pc)!
docs.text: Same mechanism, but the moisture equation overshoots pc ≥ 0 (saturation). Seen with the Soil and Hamstad models from a cold start; cases written by plugin 1.10 or later carry a floor on the moisture capacity (minCrel) that removed it in all tested cases. If it still appears, switch the affected region to Impermeable and report the case.

docs.title: Need help?
docs.text: Open a thread in the Eddy3D Discussions and attach the .gh, the tail of the solve log (from the last Solving for solid region line) and the checkMesh_*.txt files.

docs.title: Wind CFD: the RANS approach
docs.text:
The 02 | Outdoor workflow (Atmospheric Boundary Layer → Outdoor Case → Run → Probe) solves pedestrian-level wind with steady Reynolds-averaged Navier–Stokes (RANS) in OpenFOAM 12. Eddy3D writes the case — geometry, mesh controls, boundary conditions, turbulence model, numerics — and OpenFOAM solves it. The physics is OpenFOAM's; this page explains what Eddy3D chooses on your behalf, what you can change, and where the approach stops being trustworthy.

Install the engine before you run

Nothing on this page solves until an OpenFOAM engine is installed. Open Eddy3D Setup (ribbon 00 | Setup, or the standalone installer) and install the row (U)RANS CFD (OpenFOAM). It offers three routes:

  • Containerized — macOS and Windows, through Podman (preferred) or Docker. Pulls a digest-pinned OpenFOAM 12 image; needs the Container runtime (Podman · Docker) row first.
  • BlueCFD — Windows, native. Parallel runs also need a 64-bit MS-MPI; Eddy3D refuses a parallel blueCFD launch without one and says so.
  • WSL — Windows, OpenFOAM inside a Linux distribution.

The engine is chosen on Outdoor Case. Every template's description names the Setup row it needs under Needs.

docs.title: When steady RANS is the right tool
docs.text:
Eddy3D offers several ways to get a wind field. Steady RANS is the workhorse: it gives the time-averaged flow around buildings at a cost a design team can afford for 8–16 wind directions.

Question Use Engine Mean wind speed, wind comfort classes, facade Cp, mean pollutant concentration Steady RANS (this page) OpenFOAM, 02 | Outdoor Mean flow where the wake sheds periodically, or a time-averaged field you trust more than one steady solve URANS — same components, Run Settings → Solver Algorithm PIMPLE OpenFOAM, 02 | Outdoor Gusts, peak loads, turbulence statistics resolved in time Large-eddy simulation on a lattice-Boltzmann solver OpenLB or FluidX3D, 11 | LBM Air temperature, humidity and surface heat exchange coupled with the flow Coupled microclimate urbanMicroclimateFoam, 03 | Outdoor+ A first look in seconds, before any CFD Machine-learning screening — never a substitute for CFD Wind Predictor, 12 | ML

docs.title: Equations
docs.text:
OpenFOAM's incompressibleFluid solver module solves the steady, incompressible RANS equations with an eddy-viscosity closure:

∇·U = 0
∇·(U U) = −∇p + ∇·[(ν + ν_t)(∇U + ∇Uᵀ)]

U is the mean velocity, p the kinematic pressure, ν the molecular and ν_t the turbulent (eddy) viscosity, which the turbulence model supplies. Pressure–velocity coupling is SIMPLE. Whether the run is steady or transient is decided by the time-derivative scheme, which Run Settings writes for you (see Transient runs).

docs.title: Turbulence models
docs.text:
Run Settings → Turbulence Model. All four are OpenFOAM 12 RAS models.

Model Notes Realizable k-ε (default) Shih et al. 1995. The AIJ and COST 732 recommendation for pedestrian-level wind; robust on coarse urban meshes, and over-predicts turbulence at stagnation points less than standard k-ε. Standard k-ε Launder & Spalding 1974. Cheapest and most tolerant; over-produces turbulence at building corners and under-predicts recirculation. RNG k-ε Yakhot et al. 1992. Better in separated and swirling flow at the same cost. SST k-ω Menter 1994. Best near-wall behaviour, needs a finer mesh near walls. In OpenFOAM 12 its ω inlet is uniform, not a boundary-layer profile, so the approaching flow loses most of its turbulence before it reaches the buildings. Mean velocities stay good; anything driven by inflow turbulence (dispersion, gust estimates) does not. Prefer a k-ε model unless you need SST specifically.

docs.title: The atmospheric boundary layer (inflow)
docs.text:
The Atmospheric Boundary Layer component sets the inlet as the equilibrium neutral boundary layer of Richards & Hoxey (1993), which OpenFOAM's atmBoundaryLayer conditions implement:

u*        = κ · U_ref / ln((Z_ref + z0) / z0)
U(z)      = (u* / κ) · ln((z − z_g + z0) / z0)
k         = u*² / √C_μ                          (constant with height)
ε(z)      = u*³ / (κ · (z − z_g + z0))
κ = 0.41,  C_μ = 0.09
  • U_ref at Z_ref — the reference speed and its height (default 10 m).
  • z0 — aerodynamic roughness length of the terrain upstream. One value, or one per wind direction (z0 per Direction), for example from Land Cover Roughness, which derives z0 from OpenStreetMap land cover over the upstream fetch.
  • Station versus site. A weather station measures at 10 m over open terrain. Feeding that speed straight into an urban profile tells the model the urban 10 m wind equals the open-country one, which overstates pedestrian wind by up to about 2×. Wind Conditions (with Site Terrain set) applies the EN 1991-1-4 §4.3 terrain transfer (×0.54 for category IV, ×0.84 for III), and Velocity Amplification Factors applies the same factor to the hourly series. The default is "None": no transfer.

docs.title: Boundary conditions
docs.text:
Patch Velocity Pressure Turbulence Inlet ABL log profile (atmBoundaryLayerInletVelocity) zero gradient ABL k and ε Outlet inletOutlet fixed 0 inletOutlet Top and sides slip slip slip Ground no slip zero gradient rough wall function nutkAtmRoughWallFunction with the same z0 as the inlet Buildings no slip zero gradient nutUSpaldingWallFunction

Using the inlet's z0 on the ground keeps the approaching profile from changing along the empty fetch, the "horizontal homogeneity" condition. Check it with the ABL_Verification template: some decay is normal, a profile that changes shape completely is not.

docs.title: Domain
docs.text:
Two shapes, both on Outdoor Case:

  • Box Domain. Automatic extents follow COST 732 best practice: 5 H upstream, 15 H downstream and 5 H to the sides and top (H = tallest building). The inlet is one fixed face, so an 8-direction study builds and meshes one rotated box per direction.
  • Cylinder Domain. One mesh serves every direction. The side wall is split into segments, and each direction decides which segments are inlet and which are outlet (Kastner & Dogan 2020). An 8-direction study meshes once instead of eight times. Each direction is still solved from scratch.

Outdoor Case checks the frontal blockage against the 3 % limit of the ASCE/SEI CWE Prestandard. Model the surrounding buildings within about 240 m of the study area before trusting results near the edge of the context.

docs.title: Mesh
docs.text: blockMesh writes a uniform background mesh and snappyHexMesh refines it towards buildings, terrain and any refinement regions. Each refinement level halves the cell size and costs about eight times the cells in that region. Cell Size shows the size each level actually produces (for example L3 · 1.25 m), and the Wind Study banner estimates the cell count as a range before you mesh, because a single number would claim more precision than the estimate has. Height Bands refines by height above ground without any geometry: finest near pedestrian level, coarser above.

docs.title: Numerics
docs.text:
Run Settings → Numerics is a point on a triangle with three corners: Accuracy, Robustness and Speed. The default sits towards Robustness. It sets the convection schemes, under-relaxation, corrector counts and linear-solver tolerances together. A few other controls matter on their own:

  • Warm-up Iterations — run the first iterations with first-order upwind and heavy relaxation, then switch to the chosen numerics. The default (−1) picks this from the numerics point.
  • Potential Flow — initialise velocity and pressure with a quick potentialFoam solve instead of a uniform field. Measured on test cases, this and other "better initial fields" do not reliably converge faster; the effect changes sign between cases.
  • Velocity cap — every wind case carries an fvConstraints limit of |U| ≤ 100 m/s. It keeps a diverging start finite and logs when it bites. A run whose maximum |U| sits at the cap has diverged; it has not converged.
  • The pressure equation always uses the GAMG solver; the Laplacian scheme defaults to limited 0.5.

docs.title: Convergence
docs.text:
• Convergence (default 1e-4) stops the run once the initial residuals of p, U and k (plus ω for SST) are all below the tolerance. ε is never in that list. Its residual stalls around 10⁻² even when the field has settled, because of how the wall functions fix ε next to walls, so it would hold every k-ε run to the iteration limit.
  • Auto-stop on plateau ends a run cleanly once every residual has been flat for about 100 iterations. Some wind directions, often the oblique ones, settle into a small limit cycle instead of converging; their residuals never reach the tolerance however long they run.
  • Live Residuals shows the run's progress, rate and estimated time to finish. Field monitors (default on) also log the domain's maximum |U| every iteration. This is the earliest sign of a cold-start overshoot.
  • Flat residuals are not proof of a settled field. Eddy3D tests the residual history for stationarity (the KPSS test) and can run a grid-convergence study (Roache GCI) through the foamgci toolkit.

docs.title: Transient runs (URANS)
docs.text: Choose PIMPLE as Solver Algorithm on Run Settings to make the same case transient. The controls change meaning: you set Duration and Time Step in seconds, a Max Courant number, and an Averaging Window for the time-averaged fields. Iteration counts, the residual stop and the plateau stop do not apply to a transient run and are not written. The component says so on the canvas, because treating 1000 iterations as 1000 seconds would give a wrong answer that looks right.

docs.title: From a solved case to results
docs.text:
• Probe samples velocity (or any field: Cp, a pollutant, TKE) at points, usually a grid about 1.5–2 m above ground. Wind Field Viewer and Streamlines draw it.
  • Velocity Amplification Factors turns each direction's U / U_ref into an hourly field by scaling with the weather file's hourly speed and direction. This is the annual wind every comfort assessment reads. Its optional TKE input gives a gust estimate for gust-referenced criteria.
  • Wind Comfort classifies that annual field against Lawson, Davenport, NEN 8100 or Wellington criteria, for the year, a season or a month.
  • With Pressure Coefficient on, Run Settings writes facade Cp. Airflow Network Cp exports it to EnergyPlus.

docs.title: Validation
docs.text:
Eddy3D checks that the cases it writes let OpenFOAM reproduce measured data. The benchmarks run through the same case writer as the canvas. Headline results (2026-09-27, OpenFOAM 12; the full tables and their caveats are in the repository's VALIDATION.md):

Benchmark Result AIJ Case I — surface-mounted cube, three closures Velocity hit rate q 0.77–0.81, correlation R ≥ 0.99 for every closure; SST loses its inflow turbulence (see above) CODASC street canyon, wind perpendicular to the street Concentration FAC2 0.90–0.96, |FB| ≤ 0.21 on 1400 points; the leeward-wall profile is too flat AIJ Case H — 1:1:2 building, point source Outer flow right (q 0.91 above the roof); the wake is 1.9× too long and peak concentrations 2.6–4.3× too high CEDVAL A1-5 — isolated block Recirculation length 3.26 H

These are typical RANS strengths and weaknesses. Mean speeds away from the wake are reliable; wake lengths and concentrations in the wake are not.

docs.title: Limitations
docs.text:
• Steady RANS gives the mean, not the gust. Gust-referenced criteria rely on a gust estimate from the modelled turbulence, not on resolved gusts. For peak values use LES (11 | LBM).
  • Wakes are typically too long and recirculation too weak with k-ε closures. Results directly behind buildings deserve the least trust.
  • Not every direction converges to a tolerance. Some, especially oblique ones, end in a limit cycle. Check the residuals and the field monitors before reading a direction's result.
  • This is not a structural-load tool. Eddy3D results are for pedestrian comfort, ventilation and dispersion screening. They do not demonstrate compliance with a wind-load standard.
  • The physics belongs to OpenFOAM. Cite OpenFOAM, the turbulence model, and the Eddy3D method papers you relied on (see Methods & Citations).

docs.title: Setup Troubleshooting Notes
docs.text: Field notes from getting Eddy3D running on a fresh Windows machine, covering a few snags that aren't obvious from the Setup dialog alone. These are community notes rather than official guidance — for the authoritative install flow see Downloads and Outdoor+ First Steps.

docs.title: Before you run Setup
docs.text:
• Skim the development docs before running Eddy3D's Setup component, so you know what each capability needs.
  • Of the container engines, Podman is preferable (daemonless, rootless, no licensing restrictions). If you're new to Podman on Windows, the Podman for Windows tutorial walks through the install.
  • Launch your container engine (Podman or Docker) before opening Rhino/Grasshopper. Setup doesn't always start the engine automatically — if it isn't already running, start it by hand first, or the capability checks below will fail to detect it.

docs.title: Install the latest beta
docs.text: Use the Rhino Package Manager (run the PackageManager command) to install Eddy3D, and check "Include pre-releases" to get the latest beta build rather than the last stable release.

docs.title: Installing capabilities: use "Pull", not "Install"
docs.text:
For each capability, click the arrow to expand its detailed instructions, and click Pull rather than Install — Pull fetches a prebuilt image into Docker/Podman, which is faster and more reliable than building it locally.

You likely don't need every capability

Check which simulation modules your workflow actually needs (Outdoor, Outdoor+, Indoor, and so on) before pulling all of them — most projects only need a handful of the capabilities listed.

If you click Install instead

Clicking Install can leave the process stuck, repeating 0 B written in the log with no progress:

If this happens, stop the install and use Pull instead.

docs.title: Missing WSL
docs.text:
If Setup warns that WSL (Windows Subsystem for Linux) is missing, you can install it from the capability panel (via the Install Engine component) or by hand:

To install it by hand, open an administrator Command Prompt and run:

wsl --install

Reboot when prompted. There's also a video walkthrough of installing WSL if you'd rather follow along.

To confirm WSL is installed: open File Explorer, select This PC, and look for a Linux entry in the sidebar.

docs.title: LBM CFD (FluidX3D) blocked by Windows
docs.text:
On some Windows machines — often ones under an organization's IT policy — FluidX3D.Core.dll gets blocked by an Application Control policy, and LBM CFD (FluidX3D) fails detection:

If you hit this, it's a local machine policy issue rather than an Eddy3D bug: check the Troubleshooting guide link in the Setup dialog, or ask your IT administrator about an Application Control exception. FluidX3D isn't required for most outdoor or indoor CFD workflows, so it's safe to leave for later while you continue with the other capabilities.

docs.title: Main Components
docs.text: Convert Units              Convert values between the units Eddy3D works in — any unit into any other of the same kind, a single value or a whole hourly list. Temperature (°C, K, °F), speed (m/s, km/h, mph, kn), length, area, volume, pressure (Pa, hPa, inHg, psi), radiation (W/m², Btu/h·ft², kWh/m²), energy and power (kWh, Btu, kW, TR), mass, air flow (m³/s, cfm), rain rate, illuminance, humidity ratio (g/kg, gr/lb), enthalpy, U-value and conductivity, angle and time. EPW and every Eddy3D comfort input are in SI, OpenFOAM temperature fields are Kelvin: wire the values in, pick From and To.  Download Weather              Pick an EPW weather file from a bundled catalog of 60,867 climate files — every TMYx station on climate.onebuilding.org plus the EnergyPlus store (IWEC, TMY3, CWEC, SWERA, …) — with your own folders and Morph Weather results listed alongside them; its second list, Built for this site, holds the sources that build a file for your site (Open-Meteo, PVGIS, NASA POWER, Copernicus CDS, NSRDB). Click the Station widget and choose Weather file (catalog)… for a searchable table with a map, or type a name, WMO id or direct URL. The catalog is searched offline; only the chosen file is downloaded, once, into the weather cache. The catalog browser's unit setting (SI or Imperial) changes only what is displayed — the Message strip, the match list and the Info text; the EPW file and every number this component outputs stay SI, so wire them to other components as before.  Morph Settings              Engine settings for Morph Weather: the method (Future Weather Generator or the World Bank CCKP anomalies), climate products, spatial interpolation, uncertainty case and solar methods. Every value left empty stays on the Future Weather Generator's own default; the CCKP methods ignore the generator-only settings.  Morph Weather              Morph a present-day EPW into future-climate EPWs with the Future Weather Generator (future-weather-generator.adai.pt), then feed the result to any Eddy3D workflow. Needs Java 17+ and the generator's .jar, which Eddy3D does not ship: download the distribution you need (CMIP6 Global, CORDEX-CMIP5 Europe, …) into ~/Eddy3D/FWG. The tool is licensed CC BY-NC-SA 4.0 — noncommercial use, attribution required. Alternatively set Morph Settings' Method to a CCKP entry: the World Bank Climate Change Knowledge Portal's CMIP6 ensemble (0.25°, no key, no Java, no jar) is read for the site's grid cell and applied to the file as monthly shifts and stretches.  Compare Weather              Puts two weather files of one site side by side before one of them drives a study: a station's typical year (an EPW from the climate browser) against a reanalysis year (ERA5, Open-Meteo, NASA POWER), or the same place from two providers. Dry-bulb temperature, relative humidity and wind speed as means, global horizontal radiation and precipitation as sums, for the year and each month.  An EPW's missing-value codes are left out, so a typical-year file without a rain column says it carries none instead of reading as a dry climate. It measures the difference; it does not pick a file. For the wind's DIRECTIONS use Compare Wind Climates.  Compare Wind Climates              Puts two wind climates of one site side by side — a station record (ISD, EPW) against ERA5, or two stations — before one of them drives a study. Wire the Climate output of two Wind Climate components built with the same Sectors.  Rose Overlap is the share of the direction distribution the two have in common (1 = the same rose); Speed Ratio is B's mean speed over A's, over the non-calm hours. The report says which of the two differs and lists every sector. It measures the disagreement; it does not pick a source.  Deconstruct Weather              Deconstruct a Weather object into hourly time series values. More outputs: zoom in and click + beside the outputs to pick any EPW column, derived series (solar angles, sun vector, absolute humidity) or monthly statistic; − removes one. OutdoorPlus  Monthly Climate Chart              Visualize monthly dry-bulb temperature and relative humidity from Eddy3D Weather as two aligned min/mean/max charts.  Weather              Read an EPW file and create a Weather object for the simulation. OutdoorPlus  Wind Climate              Long-term directional wind statistics for pedestrian comfort: for every direction sector (36 × 10° by default) and season (year + Dec-Feb, Mar-May, Jun-Aug, Sep-Nov, named for the hemisphere), the sector probability, the calm share and a Weibull c, k fitted by maximum likelihood to the non-calm hours of a MULTI-YEAR record — ERA5 via Open-Meteo (any coordinate, no key), the nearest NOAA ISD or GHCNh station, local EPW files or a CSV — or the City of London Annex A table. A typical year cannot carry a safety criterion: Lawson's 15 m/s for 0.022 % of the year is about two hours, and a TMY holds two hours of one composite year. Wire the Wind Climate output into Pedestrian Wind Comfort (with VAF's Speed Ratios) to classify from P(U > u) = Σ p·exp(−(u/(r·c))^k); the report says whether the record is long enough to measure the safety tail. Downloads run off the canvas and are cached per year in WeatherCache/WindRecords inside the Eddy3D folder of your local app data.Sources: ERA5 (Hersbach et al. 2020, Copernicus C3S) via Open-Meteo; NOAA NCEI Integrated Surface Database (ISD-Lite) and its successor GHCNh; City of London Wind Microclimate Guidelines (2019), Annex A.  Geometry Repair              Check building geometry and repair it for snappyHexMesh: weld split vertices, remove degenerate and duplicate faces (and the shared walls of touching solids), orient every closed piece outward, optionally fill small holes and drop specks, then optionally rebuild it as a closed, manifold voxel WRAP — overlapping buildings fuse into one solid, courtyards open to the sky stay open, gaps narrower than about the wrap cell close. Runs in-process (no Python service). The case components already run the safe part automatically before meshing; use this to see what is wrong, to fill holes, or to wrap.  Land Cover Roughness              Fetch land-cover polygons around a location from OpenStreetMap (open data, Overpass API) — plus surface car parks, pedestrian areas and bare ground — and classify each into an aerodynamic roughness length via the Davenport-Wieringa terrain classification, with the terrain elevation around the site (AWS Terrain Tiles, open data). Outputs ready-made ground roughness zones draped on a terrain mesh for the wind case.  Site Context              One click from a location to the site's context: buildings with heights, bare-earth terrain, tree crowns, land-cover ground zones with their roughness, and the inlet z0 per wind direction — fetched in the background from open data and placed in a local frame centred on the location (Rhino model units). Sources: OpenStreetMap buildings (ODbL; height from the height tag or building:levels x 3 m, else the Fallback Height — never guessed silently: every building's height KIND is in the report), GEDTM30 bare-earth DTM (CC BY 4.0), the Meta/WRI 1 m canopy height map plus OSM street trees (CC BY 4.0 / ODbL), and ESA WorldCover 2021 (CC BY 4.0). Buildings come from GlobalBuildingAtlas LoD1 (TUM, CC BY-NC 4.0 — heights PREDICTED by a model, every one labelled so) or from OpenStreetMap (ODbL — the height tag or building:levels x 3 m, else the Fallback Height), chosen on Building Source. Results are cached on disk, so a reopened document shows its context without a new fetch; pressing Fetch again, or Refresh from the sources on the right-click menu, downloads anew.  Site Picker              Pick a site on a satellite map: search an address or place (Nominatim / Photon, OpenStreetMap data), click or drag the pin, then "Use this location". The map window stays in front of Rhino and Grasshopper while it is open. Latitude and Longitude (WGS84 degrees) go into LiDAR Site, Site Context or any component that takes a site. The pick is saved with the document. The last 20 places you searched for or used are kept on this machine (~/Eddy3D/site-picker-recent.json): Recent in the map window, and "Recent sites" in this component's right-click menu sets one without opening the map. Imagery: Esri World Imagery; map: © OpenStreetMap contributors. Needs an internet connection.  Watertight              Combine a multi-part building mesh into a single watertight, CFD-ready solid via the bundled Python mesh service (trimesh/manifold3d/pymeshfix). The server auto-starts locally on the first run (uv-managed Python environment; first start installs it, 1-2 minutes) and is reused afterwards.  Wind Compass              Visualize a wind direction on a compass circle. Direction is meteorological degrees (0=N, 90=E, 180=S, 270=W); outputs the flow vector and the 16-point cardinal name.  Wind Rose Cluster              Cluster annual wind conditions into a budget of representative directions using k-means over hourly wind vectors (speed x direction): frequent, strong conditions attract the budget, and each cluster reports an observed direction/speed pair plus its frequency. Without wired speeds, clusters directions alone (unit vectors). Method: Kastner & Dogan (2022), Building and Environment 212:108639, doi:10.1016/j.buildenv.2021.108639; Kastner & Dogan (2019), Building Simulation 2019, Rome 621-628, doi:10.26868/25222708.2019.210458.  City Surface              Build ONE watertight surface of terrain, buildings (LoD 1.2 boxes to LoD 2.2 roofs) and surface layers (water, roads, green) for urban CFD. Ground comes from points (wired, or class 2 of a LAS/XYZ cloud) and every footprint and layer outline is carried into its triangulation, so buildings stand IN the terrain with walls down to the ground on every side instead of boxes sunk through a plate. A roof is the footprint's Height above its median ground, or else the Roof Percentile of the roof points (class 6) inside it, or — with neither, typically a house the survey saw only as the tree canopy over it — a flat box at the median height of its five nearest reconstructed buildings (the Report counts them). Overlapping footprints are separated (the earlier one wins); flattened layers sit at one level. Outputs are split by part so each can be its own patch. Method: Pađen et al. (2022), Frontiers in Built Environment 8:899332, doi:10.3389/fbuil.2022.899332; Biljecki et al. (2016), Computers, Environment and Urban Systems 59, 25-37, doi:10.1016/j.compenvurbsys.2016.04.005.  LiDAR Site              Fetch open LiDAR and building footprints for a site from its latitude and longitude, for City Surface: the footprints over a square of the given Size, the point cloud (the terrain) over a larger square, Terrain Size — the ground a CFD domain stands on reaches further than the buildings that matter. The Netherlands: AHN (Het Waterschapshuis, CC-BY 4.0) from its official sheets — a sheet is ~5 GB and is downloaded once into the cache, then every site in it is read from there — with BAG footprints (Kadaster, CC0). The United States: USGS 3DEP (public domain), only the point-cloud nodes over the site, with GlobalBuildingAtlas footprints (TUM, CC BY-NC 4.0; OpenStreetMap if it cannot be read). France (IGN LiDAR HD, Licence Ouverte), Switzerland (swissSURFACE3D, swisstopo), Bavaria (CC BY 4.0), Scotland (National LiDAR Programme, OGL), Estonia (Maa- ja Ruumiamet), Denmark (Danmarks Højdemodel), Spain (PNOA 2022-25: Aragon, Extremadura, the Canaries) and Slovenia (GURS CLSS), the last three from the open-lidar-data mirror: the 1 km tiles over the site, 65-250 MB each (Slovenia's 2024 flight up to 1 GB), cached once, with the same footprints. Everything comes out in metres around the site centre: wire Point Cloud, Footprints and Domain into City Surface. Tree Crowns are read from the cloud's own vegetation returns (one closed mesh per cluster, for the Tree component); Trees, Barriers and Furniture are for looking at and for a render (round trees; with Roads on, OpenStreetMap fences, walls, hedges and street furniture); Layer Outlines, Layer Names, Layer Roughness and Flatten are OpenStreetMap land cover (ODbL) with its Davenport z0, in the footprints' frame — wire them into the City Surface inputs of the same names. Rivers, streams and canals mapped as lines come with them as water ribbons (the OpenStreetMap width tag, else river 20 m, canal 8 m, stream 3 m).  Analysis Period              Define an analysis period (from/to day of year, start/end hour of day) and output the hour-of-year indices it covers, for filtering annual results.  Calendar              Interactively select a month, day, and hour for annual analysis. Click the controls on the component to change the date and time.  Hour of Year              Convert a start date/time and optional end date/time into hour-of-year values (1–8760) for indexing annual hourly data.  Translate Date To Hours              Translate a Ladybug analysis period to hours of the year.  STL Exporter              Export geometry to STL format for OpenFOAM or other CFD tools. Supports meshes and Breps (auto-meshed); binary or ASCII, single or multiple files.  Safety Toggle              A boolean toggle that is always FALSE when a file is opened. Useful for preventing automatic execution of heavy work. When Run is connected to several component inputs, they run one Grasshopper solution at a time in canvas order. Double-click to toggle.  Settle Data              Hold the last output while the left mouse button is pressed, then publish the newest value when the button is released. Useful between an MD Slider and an expensive component.

docs.title: Main Components
docs.text: Atmospheric Boundary Layer              Define atmospheric boundary layer inflow conditions for Eddy3D.  Manual Inflow Profile              Define inflow boundary conditions from a manually entered vertical profile (z/zR, U/UR, k/UR^2) instead of the parametric ABL log-law. Writes fixedProfile inlet conditions for U, k and epsilon. epsilon is derived from the profile as epsilon(z) = Cmu^0.5 * k(z) * d(U)/dz.  Uniform Flow              Create a uniform (constant velocity) inflow boundary condition for Eddy3D.  Wind Conditions              Bin a year of EPW wind into direction sectors — frequency, speed histogram, mean speed and a Weibull fit per sector — with the station's origin (provider, id, period, coordinates, elevation) and the site's location in one record. Optionally transfers the station's speeds to the site's terrain per EN 1991-1-4 (the anemometer stands in open country; the site does not). Wire the record into the ABL component's Wind Directions: it supplies directions AND speeds, travels into the study manifest and the Study Report, and lets VAF scale the hourly series by the same factor.  Cell Size              Compute the snappyHexMesh refinement level needed to reach a target cell size (each level halves the cell size).  Cylinder Domain              Define a cylindrical simulation domain for Eddy3D. One cylindrical mesh serves all wind directions; the cylinder side faces switch between inlet and outlet per direction. The auto radius and height size the domain under the blockage limits of ASCE/SEI CWE Prestandard AC 6-8b (to 2% frontal, 16% lateral and vertical, against limits of 3/17/17%), which the case component verifies. Model surrounding buildings within ~240 m of the study area (ASCE 49 proximity guidance) before trusting results near the context edge. Method: Kastner & Dogan (2020), Journal of Building Performance Simulation 13(1):59-68, doi:10.1080/19401493.2019.1692906; Kastner & Dogan (2018), eSim 2018 (IBPSA-Canada), Montréal, https://www.researchgate.net/publication/325023244_Streamlining_meshing_methodologies_for_annual_urban_CFD_simulations.  Height Bands              Refine the mesh in BANDS OF HEIGHT above the ground — level 3 within 4 m, level 2 within 10 m, level 1 within 24 m — everywhere on the site, not only near buildings. This is how the pedestrian layer gets resolved across open plazas and streets that no building refinement reaches. The bands follow the case's ground surfaces (terrain, ground ring and roughness zones), so on a sloped site they stay the same height above the ground; only a meshing dict with no ground surface gets the flat disk Centre and Radius describe. Wire Extras into the case component's Extras input beside any Refinement Region.  Mesh Settings              Configure mesh refinement, layers, and grading for Eddy3D.  Refinement Region              Define a custom snappyHexMesh refinement region (a box, solid or surface) — refines the cells inside/near the geometry to the chosen level. Wire Extras into a case component so the region is written every time the case is written; or wire a written Case in and press Apply to edit the dictionaries in place (which a later re-write undoes).  Brep Grid Points              Generate centered surface samples on the actual faces of Brep, surface, or mesh geometry.  Data Coverage              What Eddy3D can fetch for a site before anything is fetched: one line per layer — buildings, roof shapes, terrain, fine terrain, point cloud, tree crowns, land cover, climate, natural hazards — with its provider, detail, licence and whether it covers this site. Worldwide providers always do; LiDAR (AHN in the Netherlands, USGS 3DEP in the United States) by position; the weather catalogue by its nearest station. Use it to plan the site model and see where you will have to bring your own data (a LAS/LAZ file, a survey, an EPW).  Ground Roughness              Assign a multi-face ground plate to the wind tunnel: each face gets its own aerodynamic roughness length z0 and becomes its own ground patch (nutkAtmRoughWallFunction). Feed into the wind case component's Ground Roughness input.  Pollutant Source              Define a pollutant emission source for the wind study: a closed volume (stack tip, traffic corridor box, exhaust vent) releasing a named species at a mass rate. Wire into the Eddy3D Case component's Sources input; the species is transported as a passive scalar with turbulent diffusivity (Sct) on every direction case, and the concentration field (kg/m3) is read back by probing the species name.  Tree              Represents a tree as a porous zone for wind blocking (Darcy-Forchheimer). Feed into the wind case component. Method: Kastner & Dogan (2022), Building and Environment 212:108639, doi:10.1016/j.buildenv.2021.108639.  Custom Function Object              Define a custom OpenFOAM function object the solver runs at runtime — fieldAverage, yPlus, wallShearStress, forces, surfaceFieldValue, a coded FO, etc. Wire Extras into a case component so it is written every time the case is written; or wire a written Case in and press Apply to edit controlDict in place (which a later re-write undoes).  Outdoor Case              Create, write, and manage an Eddy3D outdoor wind simulation case. Method: Kastner & Dogan (2022), Building and Environment 212:108639, doi:10.1016/j.buildenv.2021.108639; Kastner & Dogan (2020), Journal of Building Performance Simulation 13(1):59-68, doi:10.1080/19401493.2019.1692906.  Run Settings              Configure solver run controls for Eddy3D. PIMPLE (transient) writes Co below 1, three pressure correctors, turbulence on every outer corrector and unbounded convection. Method: Wolf Dynamics (2021), OpenFOAM advanced training, online session, July 2021 GT-79, GT-97, GT-100, https://www.wolfdynamics.com/training/turbulence/OF2021/turbulence_20221_OF8_guided_tutorials.pdf.  Remote Run              Run a written wind study on another machine over SSH (a workstation, server or cloud VM with Eddy3D's CLI and a container engine). Submit packages the study's static part, copies it to /- under the remote home and starts `E3D run` detached; while it runs the component polls every minute and shows each direction's convergence; Fetch copies the solved study back over the local one. SSH uses key login only and never prompts: connect once in a terminal first. The remote must be Linux, macOS or WSL.  Run              Mesh and run an OpenFOAM case on the selected engine (wind / indoor / UMF).  SLURM Runner              Write SLURM batch (sbatch) files to run a wind study on an HPC cluster.  Write Run Scripts              Writes meshing and simulation scripts (.bat / .sh) into a Scripts/ folder under the wind study, so the workflow can be launched manually outside Grasshopper. The scripts match what the Run component executes. Write the study to disk first (Wind Case 'Write').

docs.title: Main Components
docs.text: Air Region              Create an air region for the UMF case. OutdoorPlus  Box Domain              Define simulation domain extents and refinement padding. OutdoorPlus  Building Material              Select a building material from the list and override its properties.  Building Mesh Settings              Configure mesh refinement for building regions.  Building Region              Build a solid building region for the UMF case: from the façade surface meshes, two material wall layers (outer + inner) are extruded inward to model heat and moisture transport through the building envelope.  Create Address              Create a MetaFOAM Address for entries and settings.  Create Entry Key              Create a MetaFOAM EntryKey from key segments.  Create Setting              Create a Setting from a list of entries.  Entry from a Key and Value              Create an Entry from an address, key, and value.  Gmsh Mesh              Creates a STL mesh from geometry using the gmsh application. Useful to create healthy mesh topologies for building elements.  Advanced Terrain Mesh              Generate a multi-resolution terrain mesh from input geometry with a solid base. OutdoorPlus  Grass              Define grass patches and parameters for the terrain. OutdoorPlus  Grass Material              Create a soil-backed grass surface material for the urbanMicroclimateFoam terrain heat, radiation, and evapotranspiration model. OutdoorPlus  Soil Material              Define soil material properties for terrain layers. OutdoorPlus  Terrain Mesh Settings              Configure mesh settings for terrain and underground regions. OutdoorPlus  Terrain Region              Create a terrain region with materials and depth settings. OutdoorPlus  Terrain Surface Material              Select a terrain surface material from the list and override its properties. OutdoorPlus  Water Surface              Coupled evaporating water surface for urbanMicroclimateFoam. The water geometry becomes a named air patch that exchanges sensible heat and moisture with the air; water motion and a moving free surface are not solved. Requires an UMF build that includes the simpleWater model.  Vegetation Mesh Settings              Configure mesh refinement for vegetation regions. OutdoorPlus  Vegetation Properties              Define vegetation property coefficients for canopy modeling. Shows the recommended coefficients (Leaf Length, rsMin, kc) by default; right-click to show all coefficients (Cd, C, nEvapSides). OutdoorPlus  Vegetation Region              Create a vegetation region from tree crown solids. Pick a Tree Type preset for a typical leaf area density and foliage drag coefficient, or choose Custom and wire your own LAD. The output drives BOTH the Outdoor+ (OpenFOAM/UMF) case and the LBM Run component's Vegetation input, with consistent canopy drag.  Library sources — LAD (crown-average, m²/m³): Sjöman et al. (2021) Arboricult. Urban For. 47(6), plant area index of 64 urban species; Klingberg et al. (2017) Urban For. Urban Green. 26, Gothenburg leaf area mapping; ENVI-met Albero plant database conventions; Zhang et al. (2018) Atmosphere 9(5):198 and Beijing For. Univ. J. (2017) ENVI-met validations for subtropical evergreens. Cd (per frontal leaf area, 0.1–0.3): Katul et al. (2004) Boundary-Layer Meteorol. 113; Mayhead (1973) Agric. Meteorol. 12, conifer wind-tunnel drag; Gillies et al. (2002) J. Geophys. Res. 107(D24), drag vs. wind speed and crown streamlining. Note: NIST TN 2039 (2019) reports Cd ≈ 2.8 against total projected area per volume — a different normalization; do not mix it with the Cd·LAD convention used here. OutdoorPlus  Case Run              Prepare and run a UMF case. OutdoorPlus  Outdoor+ Case              Create, read, and manage an Outdoor+ (UMF microclimate) case. Validated in: Rahimi et al. (2025), Building and Environment 285:113637, doi:10.1016/j.buildenv.2025.113637; Rahimi et al. (2024), IBPC 2024, https://www.researchgate.net/publication/384972164_Assessing_the_Complexity_Required_for_Enhancing_Eddy3D_Validation_of_urbanMicroclimateFoam_for_Urban_Heat_Island_Mitigation. OutdoorPlus  Simulation Mesh Settings              Configure snappyHexMesh settings for the simulation. OutdoorPlus  Simulation Settings              Configure simulation control settings for UMF. OutdoorPlus  Timing Parameters              Define simulation timing and optional weather-driven time series. OutdoorPlus  ViewFactors              Configure the view-factor discretization for radiation modeling. OutdoorPlus  Check Geometry              Tests for buildings and trees for Eddy3D-OutdoorPlus simulation.  Deconstruct Entry              Deconstructs an Entry instance.  Deconstruct FileContainer              Deconstructs a FileContainer instance.  Deconstruct Region              Deconstruct a MetaFOAM Region instance.  Deconstruct Setting              Deconstruct a Setting instance into its entries.  Relative Humidity              Convert specific humidity (w) and temperature (T) to relative humidity (%) — reads the UMF fields w and T, so it lives with Outdoor+, not with the weather inputs.
