docs.title: City Surface - [source code]
docs.text: Build ONE watertight surface of terrain, buildings (LoD 1.2 boxes to LoD 2.2 roofs) and surface layers (water, roads, green) for urban CFD. Ground comes from points (wired, or class 2 of a LAS/XYZ cloud) and every footprint and layer outline is carried into its triangulation, so buildings stand IN the terrain with walls down to the ground on every side instead of boxes sunk through a plate. A roof is the footprint's Height above its median ground, or else the Roof Percentile of the roof points (class 6) inside it, or — with neither, typically a house the survey saw only as the tree canopy over it — a flat box at the median height of its five nearest reconstructed buildings (the Report counts them). Overlapping footprints are separated (the earlier one wins); flattened layers sit at one level. Outputs are split by part so each can be its own patch. Method: Pađen et al. (2022), Frontiers in Built Environment 8:899332, doi:10.3389/fbuil.2022.899332; Biljecki et al. (2016), Computers, Environment and Urban Systems 59, 25-37, doi:10.1016/j.compenvurbsys.2016.04.005.

docs.title: Input
docs.text: Name Nickname Description Type Point Cloud Cloud LAS, LAZ or text x y z [class] files. Class 2 is read as ground, class 6 as roof; a file without classes is all ground. Only points inside the Domain are kept. LiDAR Site's Point Cloud output. Text Footprints Bldg Closed building footprints (plan view; z is ignored). LiDAR Site's Footprints output. Curve Domain Closed planar outline of the area to build (plan view). Everything is clipped to it. LiDAR Site's Domain output. Curve Layer Outlines Layer Closed outlines of surface layers imprinted into the terrain (water, roads, green...). LiDAR Site's Layer Outlines output. Curve Layer Names Names Name per layer outline (by index, the last repeats). Outlines with the same name form one output. LiDAR Site's Layer Names output. Text Layer Roughness z0 Aerodynamic roughness length z0 [m] per layer outline (by index, the last repeats), carried to the Layer Roughness output — one value per Layers mesh, for Ground Roughness. LiDAR Site's Layer Roughness output. Number Flatten Flat Per layer outline (the last repeats): set it to one level, the Layer Percentile of the ground under it (water). An outline whose ground falls more than 2 m across it (a river mapped as an area) follows the ground instead. LiDAR Site's Flatten output. Boolean Roof Hints Hints Optional roof hints per footprint, aligned with Footprints (LiDAR Site's Roof Hints): 'gable;4;90;across' — shape (flat/gable/hip/shed or an OSM roof:shape word); roof height m; ridge direction °; 'across' for the ridge on the short side. A hint is used only where the LiDAR has too few roof points to fit a roof; a fit always wins, and a fit that disagrees with its hint is counted in the Report. Text LoD Roof detail. LoD 1.2: one flat roof per footprint (Roof Percentile of its points). LoD 1.3: one flat roof per height level (a tower on a podium is two; a pitched roof stays one). LoD 2.0: ONE standard roof per building — flat, shed, gable or hip, whichever fits its roof points best (flat when within 15 %) — on the footprint's oriented box, clipped to the footprint: the cleanest choice where the LiDAR is sparse or trees overhang. LoD 2.1: roof planes like 2.2, but details from 4 m only: smaller parts are merged (unless they stand 4 m above their neighbours — a shaft is not a detail), and a pitched plane whose points are thinner than 3 m on the map (a wall, an eave line) is dropped. LoD 2.2: roof planes fitted to the roof points (pitched roofs, ridges, steps between levels), details from 2 m. At every 2.x level a footprint with a Height, or without enough points for a plane, stays LoD 1.2. Text Engine Eng Who thins the ground raster and scores the roof planes. Auto: the OpenCL GPU when there is one, else the CPU. GPU: the OpenCL GPU; a fallback to the CPU is reported, never silent. CPU: every core. The surface is the same either way — the GPU reproduces the CPU's cell means, medians and plane choices; the sequential triangulation stays on the CPU. Text Run Build the surface. Resets when the run starts; a wired toggle held true re-runs when the inputs change. Boolean

docs.title: Output
docs.text: Name Nickname Description Type Terrain The ground outside buildings and layers (open at the domain outline). Mesh Buildings Bldg Roofs and every wall, down to the ground and between buildings. Mesh Layers Layer One mesh per layer name. Mesh Layer Names Names The name of each Layers mesh. Text Surface All of it as one welded mesh. Mesh Roof Heights RoofZ Roof elevation per footprint (by index); NaN where a footprint was skipped. Number Report What was built, skipped and approximated. Text Layer Roughness z0 z0 [m] of each Layers mesh (by index, the first Layer Roughness given for its name; none given: nothing). With Layers and Layer Names, the Faces, Roughness Lengths and Names of Ground Roughness. Number Tree Crowns Crowns Tree crowns from the cloud's own vegetation returns (classes 3-5; unclassified points beside buildings when the cloud has a building class), one closed mesh per cluster of 4 m columns from 0.41 x tree height to the top, none inside a footprint, none under 2 m. Plug into the Tree component's Geometry, one Tree per crown. Empty when the cloud has no vegetation (the Report says why); kept with the cached surface. Mesh Low Vegetation Low The vegetation the crowns leave out — hedges, shrubs, young trees from 0.5 m up — one closed mesh per cluster of 2 m columns that stand on the ground and rise to the tallest return, none under a crown, none inside a footprint. Plug into the Tree component's Geometry with a shrub species (Hedge / shrub) - one zone per mesh there, and a site has hundreds of these (the Report counts them); Outdoor+ Vegetation Region takes them as one region. Read only from a cloud that classifies vegetation (ASPRS 3-5): where the trees are unclassified points beside buildings, a low one would also be a car or a fence, so none is read. Not here: lawn under 0.5 m (the surface layers' ground cover) and what stands inside a tree's 4 m crown cell (the trunk space - the Report counts it). With Tree Crowns these are the trees, and the hedges and shrubs outside their cells; the Report says what was read and what was not. Mesh Trees The same vegetation as individual trees, ONE mesh: a round crown on a short trunk each, standing where the canopy of the cloud's vegetation returns peaks (1 m raster, 3 m and taller, none inside a footprint, at most the 20,000 tallest). For looking at and for a render, not for a solver: Tree Crowns are the porous zones the Tree component takes. Empty when the cloud has no vegetation (the Report says why); kept with the cached surface. Mesh Full Terrain Ground The WHOLE ground as one welded mesh over the whole Domain: no layer is cut out of it and no footprint is either. It is the surface's own triangulation with every triangle at the height of the ground at its corners, so where Terrain or a Layers mesh exists the two agree exactly, a flattened pond is as level here as there, and under a building it is the plane through the ground the walls stand on at the footprint's corners (not the roof). Terrain stays the ground OUTSIDE buildings and layers; this is the ground they all stand on, to look at, to drape something on or to read heights from. Not drawn in this component's preview (it lies under the other parts); kept with the cached surface. Mesh Bridges The bridge decks as closed slabs, from the cloud's bridge returns (ASPRS class 17): one plane through the returns, sides smoothed, 1 m thick, wherever the ground is more than 2 m under the deck (where it comes up to the deck, the bridge rests on it and Terrain has it). Not part of Surface, which is 2.5D and cannot pass under anything; Site Look's Bridges. Empty when the cloud has no bridge class; kept with the cached surface. Mesh

docs.title: Comfort Heat Map - [source code]
docs.text: 365 × 24 heat maps of one probe's UTCI or PET — sun and wind, wind without sun, sun without wind, neither — from the same MRT, wind and weather inputs as UTCI (Simulation). Sun is removed by setting MRT to the air temperature and wind by holding 0.5 m/s, exactly as the Site Report's scenarios do. Export writes SVG, PDF and PNG.

docs.title: Input
docs.text: Name Nickname Description Type MRT M The MRT component's Result (preferred), or a DataTree of annual MRT values — {probe}(8760) or {hour}(probes), both accepted. Generic Data Wind Speed V Wind speed as for UTCI (Simulation): an AnnualWindField, one value per probe, or a tree. Defaults to calm (0.5 m/s) when unconnected. Generic Data Air Temperature T Annual hourly ambient air temperature (8760 values, °C). Number Relative Humidity RH Annual hourly relative humidity (8760 values, %). Number Probe Index of the probe to map (0-based, in the MRT Result's probe order). Integer Metric UTCI, or PET on the temperate or humid assessment scale. PET uses the defaults of PET (Simulation): 35 years, average sex, 1.75 m, 75 kg, standing, 0.9 clo, 80 W, 1013.25 hPa. Text Folder Where Export writes the files. Defaults to ~/Eddy3D/Charts. Text Export E Write the four maps as SVG, PDF and PNG into Folder. Boolean

docs.title: Output
docs.text: Name Nickname Description Type Scenarios S The four scenario names, in the order of the Values branches. Text Values V The metric (°C) at every hour of the probe's year, one branch per scenario {scenario}(hours). Number Comfort % % Share of hours in the no-thermal-stress class, per scenario. Number Files F The SVG, PDF and PNG paths Export wrote. Text

docs.title: Comfort Hours - [source code]
docs.text: Bin an hourly point-specific series (e.g. UTCI) into a comfort range or the UTCI thermal-stress categories, per analysis period, and report hours/percent in each band. Feed it a point-specific DataTree (e.g. the UTCI component's output) and, optionally, one Analysis Period per branch (see the Analysis Period / Analysis Period To Hours components); an unwired period covers the whole series as one implicit Annual period.

docs.title: Input
docs.text: Name Nickname Description Type Values Hourly point-specific series to bin (DataTree, one branch per point, e.g. UTCI 8760h). Number Analysis Periods Periods Hour-of-year lists (DataTree, one branch per period, 1-based hours). Unwired = one Annual period covering the whole series. Integer Period Names Names Optional label per analysis-period branch, in branch order. Defaults to "Period N" (or "Annual" when Analysis Periods is unwired). Text Mode Custom Range bins Low-High; UTCI Categories bins into the 11 UTCI thermal-stress categories instead (Low/High are ignored). Text Low Band lower bound, inclusive. Ignored in UTCI Categories mode. Number High Band upper bound, exclusive. Ignored in UTCI Categories mode. Number

docs.title: Output
docs.text: Name Nickname Description Type Point Index of the point/probe (0-based, branch order of Values). Integer Period Analysis-period name this row was evaluated over. Text % In Band Pct Percent of evaluated hours falling in the band/category. Number Hours In Band InBand Count of evaluated hours falling in the band/category. Integer Hours Evaluated Evaluated Count of hours evaluated for this point/period (present, non-NaN samples). Integer Label Band label (Custom Range) or UTCI category name (UTCI Categories). Text

docs.title: Compare Weather - [source code]
docs.text: Puts two weather files of one site side by side before one of them drives a study: a station's typical year (an EPW from the climate browser) against a reanalysis year (ERA5, Open-Meteo, NASA POWER), or the same place from two providers. Dry-bulb temperature, relative humidity and wind speed as means, global horizontal radiation and precipitation as sums, for the year and each month. An EPW's missing-value codes are left out, so a typical-year file without a rain column says it carries none instead of reading as a dry climate. It measures the difference; it does not pick a file. For the wind's DIRECTIONS use Compare Wind Climates.

docs.title: Input
docs.text: Name Nickname Description Type Weather A A An EPW file path, or a Weather object — usually the station's typical year. Generic Data Weather B B The EPW file path or Weather object to hold against it — usually a reanalysis year at the site. Generic Data

docs.title: Output
docs.text: Name Nickname Description Type Quantities Names The quantities compared, with their units. Text Annual A A Each quantity over the year in file A (mean, or sum for radiation and precipitation). Number Annual B B The same in file B. Number Monthly Difference Diff B minus A for each month, one branch per quantity. Number Distance Dist Distance between the two files' stated locations (km). Number Report The summary and the monthly tables (Markdown). Text

docs.title: Compare Wind Climates - [source code]
docs.text: Puts two wind climates of one site side by side — a station record (ISD, EPW) against ERA5, or two stations — before one of them drives a study. Wire the Climate output of two Wind Climate components built with the same Sectors. Rose Overlap is the share of the direction distribution the two have in common (1 = the same rose); Speed Ratio is B's mean speed over A's, over the non-calm hours. The report says which of the two differs and lists every sector. It measures the disagreement; it does not pick a source.

docs.title: Input
docs.text: Name Nickname Description Type Climate A A A Wind Climate — usually the station record. Generic Data Climate B B The Wind Climate to hold against it — usually ERA5 at the site. Generic Data

docs.title: Output
docs.text: Name Nickname Description Type Rose Overlap Overlap Shared share of the two direction distributions, 0-1. Number Speed Ratio Ratio Mean speed of B over A, non-calm hours. Number Agree True when the overlap is at least 0.85 and the mean speeds are within 15 % (round thresholds, not a standard). Boolean Directions Dir Sector centres (degrees from north). Number Difference Diff Probability of B minus A in each sector (percentage points). Number Report The verdict and the sector table (Markdown). Text

docs.title: Convert Units - [source code]
docs.text: Convert values between the units Eddy3D works in — any unit into any other of the same kind, a single value or a whole hourly list. Temperature (°C, K, °F), speed (m/s, km/h, mph, kn), length, area, volume, pressure (Pa, hPa, inHg, psi), radiation (W/m², Btu/h·ft², kWh/m²), energy and power (kWh, Btu, kW, TR), mass, air flow (m³/s, cfm), rain rate, illuminance, humidity ratio (g/kg, gr/lb), enthalpy, U-value and conductivity, angle and time. EPW and every Eddy3D comfort input are in SI, OpenFOAM temperature fields are Kelvin: wire the values in, pick From and To.

docs.title: Input
docs.text: Name Nickname Description Type Values Val Values to convert, in the From unit — a single value or a list (e.g. the 8760 hourly dry-bulb values of an EPW). NaN passes through. Number From The unit the Values are in. The From unit decides what is converted (a speed, a pressure, a temperature …). A wired text ("K", "°F", "mph", "m3/h", "Celsius") works too. Text To The unit to convert into — it has to measure the same thing as From, or the component says so. Text

docs.title: Output
docs.text: Name Nickname Description Type Values Val The converted values, in the To unit — same order and length as the input. Number

docs.title: Cull Ground Mesh - [source code]
docs.text: Cut building footprints out of a ground mesh to make an analysis ground mesh. The ground is quad-remeshed to Target Face Count (or taken as wired when that is 0), then every vertex under a building is removed together with the faces that use it.

docs.title: Input
docs.text: Name Nickname Description Type Building Mesh Bldgs Building meshes (joined internally). A ground vertex is culled when the vertical line through it pierces one of these faces, so the roofs are what matter; open-bottomed footprint extrusions are fine. Mesh Ground Mesh Ground Ground mesh(es) to cull. Remeshed to Target Face Count first, or culled exactly as wired when that is 0. Mesh Target Face Count Target Quad count QuadRemesh aims for before culling. 0 skips the remesh and culls the ground mesh as wired, so a hand-built grid keeps its faces. Default: 50000. Integer Triangulate Tri Shrink quads at the cut edge into triangles instead of dropping them, so the cut-out hugs the footprint. Off removes every face that touched a culled vertex. Does not triangulate the rest of the mesh. Default: true. Boolean

docs.title: Output
docs.text: Name Nickname Description Type Culled Mesh Mesh Ground mesh with building footprints removed. Mesh

docs.title: Custom Function Object - [source code]
docs.text: Define a custom OpenFOAM function object the solver runs at runtime — fieldAverage, yPlus, wallShearStress, forces, surfaceFieldValue, a coded FO, etc. Wire Extras into a case component so it is written every time the case is written; or wire a written Case in and press Apply to edit controlDict in place (which a later re-write undoes).

docs.title: Input
docs.text: Name Nickname Description Type Case Optional. An already-written case to edit in place — any Eddy3D OpenFOAM case (wind, Outdoor+ microclimate, indoor, CHT) or a loaded study. Leave it empty and wire the Extras output into the case component instead, which is the durable route: a function object applied here is erased the next time the case is written. Generic Data Name Function object key (a valid OpenFOAM word, e.g. "fieldAverage1"). Text Definition Def The function object body — the contents between its braces, as text (from a panel) or a Foamonary. Example: type fieldAverage; libs ("libfieldFunctionObjects.so"); fields ( U p ); The component wraps it as Name { ... } inside controlDict functions. Generic Data Region Optional OpenFOAM region for a MULTI-region solver (Outdoor+ microclimate: air, buildings, vegetation, terrain; CHT: one per solid/cavity). Those solvers scope every function object by region and nest its output under postProcessing//, so an unscoped one never runs. Leave empty for single-region cases (wind, indoor). Text Bake Apply Write the function object into the wired Case's already-written controlDict (idempotent). Momentary button. Not needed for the Extras route, which writes it with the case. Boolean

docs.title: Output
docs.text: Name Nickname Description Type Status What was written, and where. Text Extras The function object as case data. Wire this into a case component's Extras input so it is written into controlDict every time the case is written — including after a re-write, which is what editing controlDict in place cannot survive. Generic Data

docs.title: Cut Fill - [source code]
docs.text: Cut and fill between the existing ground and a proposed grading: where the proposed surface sits below the ground is CUT (red), where it sits above is FILL (blue), and the volumes come with the mesh. Compare design options on one depth scale (Depth Range), read the balance (Net: positive = material to bring in), and the bands say how deep the work goes. Both surfaces are sampled at the centre of every raster cell inside the proposed surface's footprint; a cell's volume is depth × cell area, so halve the cell size where the grading is finer than the cells. Ground the proposed surface does not reach is not earthworks; a cell the existing ground misses is left out and counted. Depths within 5 mm of zero are unchanged.

docs.title: Input
docs.text: Name Nickname Description Type Existing The existing ground — a mesh, Brep or surface (branches are flattened). Geometry Proposed The proposed grading — meshes, Breps or surfaces; their plan footprint is what gets rastered (branches are flattened). Geometry Cell Size Cell Raster cell size (m). Each cell is sampled once at its centre; use half the size of the smallest grading feature. Number Bands Depth band edges (m, ascending). Each band holds the cut and the fill between its edge and the previous one; the last band is open. Default 0.25, 0.5, 1, 2. Number Depth Range Range Depth (m) at the ends of the colour scale, the same for cut and fill, so design options compare on one scale. 0 = the deepest cut or highest fill of this result. Number

docs.title: Output
docs.text: Name Nickname Description Type Mesh The proposed surface as cells coloured by depth: red cut, blue fill, grey unchanged. Mesh Cells Centre of every rastered cell both surfaces cover, on the proposed surface. Point Depths Proposed minus existing at each of Cells (m): positive fill, negative cut. Number Cut Cut volume (m³). Number Fill Fill volume (m³). Number Net Fill minus cut (m³): positive is material to bring in, negative to take away. Number Bands One line per depth band: label, cut m³, cut m², fill m³, fill m² (tab-separated). Text Summary Totals, extremes and the bands as text. Text

docs.title: Cylinder Domain - [source code]
docs.text: Define a cylindrical simulation domain for Eddy3D. One cylindrical mesh serves all wind directions; the cylinder side faces switch between inlet and outlet per direction. The auto radius and height size the domain under the blockage limits of ASCE/SEI CWE Prestandard AC 6-8b (to 2% frontal, 16% lateral and vertical, against limits of 3/17/17%), which the case component verifies. Model surrounding buildings within ~240 m of the study area (ASCE 49 proximity guidance) before trusting results near the context edge. Method: Kastner & Dogan (2020), Journal of Building Performance Simulation 13(1):59-68, doi:10.1080/19401493.2019.1692906; Kastner & Dogan (2018), eSim 2018 (IBPSA-Canada), Montréal, https://www.researchgate.net/publication/325023244_Streamlining_meshing_methodologies_for_annual_urban_CFD_simulations.

docs.title: Input
docs.text: Name Nickname Description Type Core Cell Size Cell Cell size of the inner core blocks in meters. Default: 25. Number Inner Core Size Inner Half-size of the square inner core in meters. -1 = auto from the building footprint. Number Outer Radius Radius Outer radius of the cylindrical domain in meters. -1 = auto from the building height. Number Height Height of the cylindrical domain in meters. -1 = auto from the building height. Number Radial Multiplier RadMult Cell growth factor from the core toward the perimeter. Default: 2. Number Core Divisions Divs Cells per core block (and per perimeter segment, tangentially). Refines the core without changing the block layout that Core Cell Size sets; the preview core grid densifies to match. Default: 1. Integer Refinement Box Extension Refine Padding of the refinement box around the geometry (m). -1 = auto: 33% of the building footprint. Number Radial Grading Grade Far-field cell coarsening across the perimeter ring (outer cell size / inner cell size). 1 = uniform; >1 keeps fine cells at the buildings but grows the outer cells. The default 7 coarsens the far field aggressively (far fewer cells downwind); lower it (1-3) for a gentler, more uniform ring. Default: 7. Number Core Roundness Round Rounds the O-grid inner core from a square (0) toward a circle (1). Higher values even out the radial gap to the outer boundary, cutting the corner non-orthogonality of the square core. 0 keeps the classic square core. 0.65 is the checkMesh-sweep optimum (lowest max non-orthogonality across mesh resolutions; skewness stays well within limits). Default: 0.65. Number Vertical Grading GradeZ Vertical cell expansion ratio (top cell size / bottom cell size). 1 = uniform; >1 keeps fine cells near the ground and coarsens aloft (typical for an ABL). A checkMesh sweep showed non-orthogonality/skewness are unaffected by this; the only cost is background aspect ratio. The default 35 strongly refines the near-ground layer; ease it down if convergence struggles. Default: 35. Number

docs.title: Output
docs.text: Name Nickname Description Type Domain Parameters Domain Cylindrical domain parameters (-1 entries mean auto-sized from the building geometry); plug into the wind case Domain input. Generic Data

docs.title: Daily Light Integral - [source code]
docs.text: Daily Light Integral per point in mol/m²/day — the photosynthetically active photons (400-700 nm) landing on each point per day, averaged over the analysed period. Shares Solar Irradiation's geometry: beam plus isotropic sky plus a ground term, no interreflection. The ground albedo here is a PAR albedo and is much lower than the broadband one. Vegetation is deliberately not accepted — see the Canopy note in the docs.

docs.title: Input
docs.text: Name Nickname Description Type Context C Shading geometry: buildings, terrain. A tree crown here blocks the beam COMPLETELY — the Canopy component's transmittance is broadband and cannot be applied to PAR. Geometry Points P Analysis points. Point Normals N Per-point surface normals. Without them every point is treated as HORIZONTAL, which is right for a planting bed or a green roof and wrong for a facade. Vector Weather W Weather record from Download Weather or Open Weather. Both the sun's position and the direct/diffuse irradiance for each hour come from this one file. Generic Data HOY H Hours of the year to analyse [1-8760]. Left empty, every DAYLIGHT hour of the year is analysed, which gives the annual mean and the full monthly breakdown. Integer Timestep T Sun samples per hour. 1 is hourly; 10 gives a 6-minute step. The irradiance is still the file's HOURLY value — a finer step refines WHERE the beam lands, not the weather itself. Integer Sky View SVF Optional sky view fraction per point, from Sky Exposure. Without it the sky is treated as fully open, which overstates diffuse in any real courtyard — and a courtyard is where this metric is usually asked. Number Ground PAR Reflectance GR PAR albedo of the ground for the reflected term. NOT the broadband albedo: vegetation absorbs PAR and reflects near-infrared, so grass is near 0.05 in PAR against ~0.23 broadband. Only tilted surfaces see any of it. Number Offset O Distance to lift each point off its surface before tracing. Number North Nth Counter-clockwise degrees from the model's +Y axis to true north (Ladybug's convention). The sun is rotated, not the model. Number Conversion Cv How broadband shortwave becomes PAR photons — a PAR energy fraction times a quanta-per-joule factor. Logan & Faust (default): 0.45 x 4.48 µmol/J = 0.00726 mol/Wh, the pair behind the published US daily-light-integral maps, calibrated against global horizontal irradiance. Ecological: 0.50 x 4.60 µmol/J, the generic convention used in flux-tower work. Runs about 14% higher. Neither is universal — both assume a daylight spectrum on an unfiltered surface. Text Engine Eng Who traces the rays. Auto: the OpenCL GPU when there is one, else the CPU. GPU: the OpenCL GPU; a fallback to the CPU is reported, never silent. CPU: the SIMD BVH on every core. Text

docs.title: Output
docs.text: Name Nickname Description Type DLI Mean daily light integral per point over the analysed period, mol/m²/day. Number Colors Col Colour ramp over the mean DLI. Colour Result Res The whole solve as one item — the monthly breakdown included. Wire Deconstruct DLI to expand it; twelve months over a large grid is the tree this output exists to avoid putting on the canvas. Generic Data Report R Range, days analysed, rays and the assumptions used. Text

docs.title: Data Coverage - [source code]

docs.title: Input

The (max) fields are peaks over the whole run — what a design is checked against — and are tracked every solver step, so they never miss a peak between snapshots. Pin it when comparing two options — otherwise each rescales to its own maximum and the worse one can look identical to the better one. Domain Cutoff Hide cells at or below this value. For a depth field it is in MILLIMETRES, and it is what stops a site-wide film of numerically-zero water from painting the whole model and hiding the ponding that matters. 10 mm is a sensible floor for ponding. docs.title: Design Storm - [source code]
docs.text: Builds a design-storm hyetograph from an IDF (Intensity-Duration-Frequency) curve, with an optional climate allowance. Feed it to Stormwater Run. Give it EITHER the three coefficients of an i = a/(t+b)^c fit, OR a published depth-duration table (the form NOAA Atlas 14, KOSTRA and FEH actually distribute). The alternating-block and Chicago patterns reproduce the IDF depth at every sub-duration, which is what makes the result a design event rather than a shape. Drainage Depth takes the share the piped drainage carries off the storm before it reaches the surface model: the total depth of the storm the sewers were designed for (2-year, 24-hour in the source study), removed in proportion from every block, after the climate allowance. It is a volume allowance, not a pipe network. Method: Shrestha et al. (2026), Urban Systems Lab, urban-flood-modeling-workflows, https://github.com/UrbanSystemsLab/urban-flood-modeling-workflows.

docs.title: Input
docs.text: Name Nickname Description Type Return Period T Design return period in years — the 1-in-T event. Local guidance sets this; 10, 30, 50 and 100 are the usual choices, with the higher values reserved for infrastructure whose failure matters most. Reported on the result; it does not itself change the rainfall, which comes from the curve you supply. Number Duration Dur Storm duration in MINUTES. Worth sweeping rather than guessing: a small, sealed catchment usually peaks under a short intense burst, a large or absorbent one under a longer storm, and the critical duration is whichever produces the worst result here. Number IDF Coefficients abc Three numbers a, b, c of an intensity fit i = a / (t + b)^c, with t in minutes and i in mm/h. Ignored when a depth-duration table is wired. Number Durations Dmin Durations (minutes) of a published depth-duration table — the form NOAA Atlas 14, KOSTRA and FEH distribute. Pair with Depths; wiring these overrides the coefficients. Number Depths Dmm Total rainfall depths (mm) matching Durations, for the return period being designed against. Interpolated in log-log space so intermediate durations stay on the published curve. Number Pattern How the depth is distributed through the storm. Alternating Block (default): peak centred, and every sub-duration matches the IDF curve. Chicago: the same increments arranged around an earlier peak — the harsher test for a design leaning on depression storage. Uniform: constant intensity. Simplest, and understates peak ponding for the same total depth. Text Block Length Block Length of each hyetograph block in minutes. A real modelling choice, not a discretisation detail: the finer it is, the higher the peak block. 5 minutes is the usual default for urban work. Number Climate Allowance Climate A published percentage uplift on design rainfall. These are ALLOWANCES, not projections — nothing here downscales a climate model — and the source travels onto the Summary output so a report can cite it. Guidance is revised; check a value more than a couple of years old against your own regulator. Text Drainage Depth Drain Total rainfall depth (mm) the piped drainage is assumed to carry off this storm, so it never reaches the surface. Usually the depth of the storm the sewers were designed for, read off the same rainfall statistics (the source study uses the 2-year, 24-hour depth). It comes off after the climate allowance, in proportion from every block: each is scaled by 1 − drainage/total, and a storm no deeper than the drainage reaches the surface as nothing. A volume allowance, not a pipe network — it does not know where the inlets are. 0 (the default) models no drainage. Number

docs.title: Output
docs.text: Name Nickname Description Type Storm The design storm, for Stormwater Run. Generic Data Intensities I Rainfall intensity of each block (mm/h), in order. Number Total Depth Depth Total rainfall over the storm (mm) that reaches the surface model — after the drainage allowance, when one is set. Number Summary The storm in words, including the climate allowance and its source. Text

docs.title: Download Weather - [source code]
docs.text: Pick an EPW weather file from a bundled catalog of 60,867 climate files — every TMYx station on climate.onebuilding.org plus the EnergyPlus store (IWEC, TMY3, CWEC, SWERA, …) — with your own folders and Morph Weather results listed alongside them; its second list, Built for this site, holds the sources that build a file for your site (Open-Meteo, PVGIS, NASA POWER, Copernicus CDS, NSRDB). Click the Station widget and choose Weather file (catalog)… for a searchable table with a map, or type a name, WMO id or direct URL. The catalog is searched offline; only the chosen file is downloaded, once, into the weather cache. The catalog browser's unit setting (SI or Imperial) changes only what is displayed — the Message strip, the match list and the Info text; the EPW file and every number this component outputs stay SI, so wire them to other components as before.

docs.title: Input
docs.text: Name Nickname Description Type Station Which climate file to use. Click the widget and choose Weather file (catalog)… to pick from the catalog with a map and a spec sheet; the value stored is the file's own name (e.g. DEU_BE_Berlin-Tempelhof.AP.103840_TMYx.2009-2023). A station name, WMO id, country or dataset year still works as a search — the best match nearest the site wins — and a direct EPW or ZIP URL is downloaded as-is. Choose Open-Meteo (ERA5) — or type Open-Meteo 2019 — to build a file for the SITE (wire Latitude/Longitude, or set the Earth Anchor Point) from ERA5 reanalysis: one actual year, last year unless one is given, on the 0.25° cell. The same menu builds PVGIS (a typical year), NASA POWER (an actual year, from 2001) and ERA5 via Copernicus CDS (an actual year with measured radiation; it needs your own free CDS token, in the ECMWF_DATASTORES_KEY environment variable or ~/.cdsapirc, and the dataset licence accepted on the CDS website) and NSRDB (GOES TMY, a typical year, or GOES aggregated, an actual year from 1998, both PSM v4 on a 4 km cell over the western hemisphere; a release of Eddy3D ships a shared NLR API key for it, which your own (a free key from developer.nlr.gov, with your name and email) replaces: NSRDB_API_KEY, NSRDB_FULL_NAME and NSRDB_EMAIL, or ~/.nsrdbrc). Credits: weather data by Open-Meteo.com (CC BY 4.0); PVGIS, European Commission Joint Research Centre; NASA Langley POWER Project; Copernicus Climate Change Service (ERA5); National Solar Radiation Database (NLR). Terms: THIRD-PARTY-NOTICES.md. Text Latitude Lat Site latitude in decimal degrees (north positive). With a site, the browser lists the nearest stations first, every row states its distance, and the map shows both. Optional, and only as a pair with Longitude: a lone latitude is not a site. Left empty, the document's Earth Anchor Point is the site when one is set; otherwise the catalog is listed in publisher order. Number Longitude Lon Site longitude in decimal degrees (east positive). See Latitude. Number Folders Dirs Extra folders of .epw files to list beside the online catalogs — a studio library, measured AMY years, or a Morph Weather output folder (whose files are labelled with their scenario and horizon). Scanned recursively; each file's own LOCATION header supplies its position. Text

docs.title: Output
docs.text: Name Nickname Description Type EPW File EPW Path to the downloaded EPW weather file. Text Logs L Execution log. Text Stations Stn The catalog entries that matched, nearest the site first. One line per file: name, dataset, source and distance. Text Station S What the chosen file is: station, period, publisher, WMO id, position, elevation, time zone, ASHRAE climate zone and the design conditions its publisher states. Text Extra Files X The .stat and .ddy files that came with the EPW, when the publisher ships them — design days and the climate summary. Empty for a file that has none. Text Site Latitude Lat Latitude of the SITE in decimal degrees (north positive): the Latitude/Longitude inputs when BOTH are given, else the document's Earth Anchor Point (which also replaces a half-given pair); empty when neither gives a full site — half a site is not a site. NOT the weather station's position — that is Deconstruct Weather's Latitude, and a station can sit tens of km from the site (an airfield, usually, whose open land cover is the wrong answer). Wire it into Land Cover Roughness's Latitude so land cover and terrain are fetched where the model is. Available as soon as the site is known, before any file is downloaded. Number Site Longitude Lon Longitude of the SITE in decimal degrees (east positive), from the same source as Site Latitude — never the weather station's. Wire it into Land Cover Roughness's Longitude. Number

docs.title: Flex Legend - [source code]
docs.text: Create a metric-aware color legend and an optional colored mesh from point/value samples. Supports wind, solar, sun-hours, temperature and other environmental data.

docs.title: Input
docs.text: Name Nickname Description Type Values Optional scalar values, one per Point. They also define Range when Range is empty. Number Points Pts Optional sample points. Supply one Value per point to create a colored cell mesh. Point Range R Optional value range the legend spans. Wire a viewer's resolved Range output, construct a domain manually, or leave empty to derive it from Values. Domain Metric Type Metric Metric preset controlling the legend title and units. Custom produces unitless labels. Text Color Map CM Color ramp — pick the same map as the Vector Field Viewer. Text Normals Optional orientation normal per Point. Supply one normal for all cells or one per point. Empty = orient every cell parallel to the legend Plane. Vector Title Optional legend title override, drawn above the bar. Empty = the Metric Type's name ("Sample Count" / " (sum)" for the Count/Sum hexbin aggregates). Text Contours Contour presentation. Off keeps one colored cell per sample. Bands re-meshes the samples into flat-filled contour bands; Lines adds isolines over the cells; Bands + Lines gives the classic contour map; Lines Only draws isolines alone. Text Plane Pl Placement plane: the bar rises along the plane's Y axis from its origin, labels sit to the +X side. Default: world XY at the origin. Plane Location L Optional anchor point overriding the Plane's origin — e.g. a corner of the domain box (plus an offset) to place the legend outside the wind tunnel. The Plane input keeps controlling the bar's orientation. Point Case Optional wind case (or its Domain Box output, or any geometry): places the legend just outside the domain's +X side at ground level, next to the wind tunnel, and scales it to the domain when Size is empty. Location still overrides the position; the Plane input still controls orientation. Generic Data Size S Bar height in model units (bar width and label offsets scale from it). Empty = 30% of the plotted Points' longest bounding-box dimension, then the Case bounds when no Points exist, then 10 units when neither has a usable extent. Number Steps N Number of labeled intervals along the bar (N+1 tick labels at exact fractions of the range). Empty = automatic ticks at round speed values (… 3.1, 3.2 … rather than 3.134). Integer Units Optional unit override for the selected Metric Type (for example lux, dB or kg/m²). Text Label Style LS How the tick labels draw in the viewport. Text is plain 3d text that bakes and exports the way it looks; Bubbles are the classic screen-sized text dots. Text Offset Distance to lift each generated mesh cell along its normalized surface normal. Default: 0.5 model units (0.5 m in Eddy3D's standard metre workflow). Number Cell Radius Radius Radius of each colored point cell in model units. Empty = inferred from point spacing. Number Bands Number of contour bands (and therefore isolines) across the Range. Empty = bands at round values, matching the legend's automatic ticks. Integer Smoothing Smooth Laplacian smoothing passes applied to the Values before contouring, for rounder isolines. This CHANGES the plotted numbers (the Values output is untouched) and is reported as a Remark. Default: 0 = contour the data as measured. Integer Aggregate Agg How the samples inside one hexagon become the value it draws. Count maps sampling density rather than the measured quantity. Text Bin Size Bin Hexagon size (centre to corner, in model units) for the Hexbins styles. Empty = about 40 hexagons across the sampled area, never finer than the sample spacing. Number Highlight Top Top Circle the N highest-valued hexagons and output those circles. 0 = none. Integer Boundary Optional closed, planar boundary (a district or site outline): hexagons whose centre falls outside it are dropped, and the outline is drawn dashed over the map. Curve Analysis Mesh AMesh Optional mesh carrying the field, with one Value per mesh vertex or per mesh face. Use it for facades, terrain and any sample set whose connectivity cannot be inferred from the Points alone. Empty = derive topology from Points. Mesh Max Edge MaxEdge Longest triangle edge kept when Points have to be tessellated — this is what leaves courtyards and building footprints as holes instead of bridging them. Empty = 1.8x the detected sample spacing. Ignored for a regular sample grid. Number Outlines Optional geometry drawn as solid lines over the map, so the bands and lines stay readable against the buildings that cast them. Curves (footprints) are draped onto the field and lifted by Offset; Breps and Meshes (City Surface's Buildings, LiDAR Site's masses) draw as their edge wireframes where they are, so the buildings read in 3D above their footprints. Geometry

Point Legend Values LV Tick label text with metric units, aligned with Legend Points. Text Field Mesh Mesh Vertex-colored mesh created from Points and Values (one polygonal cell per sample), oriented by the corresponding Normals and lifted by Offset. Mesh Colors Color per finite input value, aligned with Points. Colour Resolved Range Domain Range used to color both the legend and field mesh. Domain Contours Isoline polylines at each band edge, empty unless a line-drawing Contours style is selected. Curve Contour Values CValues Field value of each contour curve, aligned with Contours. Number Bin Centers Centers Centre of each drawn hexagon, empty unless a Hexbins style is selected. Point Bin Values BinValues Aggregated value per hexagon, aligned with Bin Centers. Number Highlights Circles around the Highlight Top hexagons, highest first. Curve

docs.title: FluidX3D Live View - [source code]
docs.text: Watch a FluidX3D wind solve live in the viewport: colors an analysis mesh with the velocity magnitude of the newest frame while the GPU solver runs, updating as each frame lands. Source 'VTK frames' reads the exported frames (also the final field of a completed run); Source 'Live server' reads the solver's memory-mapped slice once a second (Run Settings → Live) and sends a changed Buildings mesh to the running solver. Wire either the Run component's Case or Folder output into Case, and supply the mesh to read the wind on (e.g. a pedestrian-level plane).

docs.title: Input
docs.text: Name Nickname Description Type Case C FluidX3D run — accepts either the Run component's Case (VTK) or Folder output. Text Mesh M Analysis mesh to color, sampled at its vertices. A flat mesh that dips below Live Height over terrain follows the ground at that height. Mesh Live L Keep watching the case for new frames and repaint as they land. Boolean Max Speed Max Top of the color scale in m/s. 0 = auto: grows with the largest speed seen this session, so colors stay comparable across frames instead of rescaling on every export. Number Avg Window Avg Trailing time-average window in simulated seconds (VTK frames only). 0 = show the newest frame as-is (instantaneous LES fields look gusty/patchy by nature); > 0 = average all exported frames within the last N simulated seconds, which converges toward the mean field the other engines report. Updates live as new frames land either way. Number Source Src Where the frames come from. 'VTK frames': the exported u-.vtk files of a one-shot or interactive run (minutes apart on an integrated GPU). 'Live server': the memory-mapped slice of a run started with Live on Run Settings — a frame a second, one horizontal plane at Live Height, nothing written to disk. Text Buildings B Live server only: the buildings as they are NOW, in world coordinates (the same mesh LBM Run was given, moved or edited). Whenever it changes, the running solver re-voxelises it in place — the flow continues from where it was, no restart. Leave empty to keep the run's geometry. Mesh Appearance Look What the colours show. Velocity: wind speed in m/s against Max Speed. Speedup: wind speed divided by the case's ABL reference speed at reference height (the Run's u_ref), against Max Speedup — 1 is the undisturbed wind, above it the flow is accelerated. '+ LIC': the same colours with a line integral convolution of sparse noise over them — thin white strands gliding along the frame's velocity vectors (the window's mean when Avg Window is set). VTK frames only: the live server publishes speeds without a direction. Text Max Speedup MaxSU Top of the colour scale when Appearance is Speedup (0 = 1.5). Number Video Render every exported VTK frame through the active Rhino viewport into /video/live-view.mp4 (PNG frames stay beside it). Needs ffmpeg on PATH; the status says where to get it otherwise. Boolean

docs.title: Output
docs.text: Name Nickname Description Type Mesh M The analysis mesh, vertex-colored by velocity magnitude (bake to keep the colors). Mesh Speeds V Velocity magnitude per mesh vertex, m/s (aligned with the mesh's vertex order). Number Time t Physical time of the displayed frame, in simulated seconds. Number Status S Frame / watcher status. Text Histogram Hist Speed histogram of the displayed frame: 20 equal bins over 0-Max Speed, one line per bin, and the share of mesh vertices above 5 m/s. Text

docs.title: FluidX3D Run Settings - [source code]
docs.text: Solver controls for the FluidX3D GPU engine (memory, simulated time, export interval, an interactive real-time window, and an optional fixed lattice spacing). Memory 0 = detected from this machine's GPU.

docs.title: Input
docs.text: Name Nickname Description Type Memory M GPU memory budget (MB), or 0 for auto. Auto detects this machine's GPU memory and takes 75% of a discrete card's VRAM / 30% of unified memory (Apple Silicon, integrated), and says so in a Remark. With Grid Spacing set this is only a cap; with Grid Spacing 0 it SIZES the lattice, so a big auto budget means a big, slow run. Integer Sim Time T Physical simulated time (s) of an Interactive run, or of a plain solve with per-interval frames; a plain solve with Warmup, Averaging or Settle set runs warm-up + averaging instead (below). Number Export Interval E VTK export interval (s, simulated time). Number Ground Z Z Ground plane Z (model units). Number Source Dir S Optional override for the FluidX3D source folder. Leave empty to use the default install path. Text Interactive I Open FluidX3D's native real-time GPU window (live render, on-the-fly camera + mode keys) while continuing periodic VTK export for Eddy3D Live View and probes. Windows: full support; macOS: requires XQuartz (X11). Boolean Grid Spacing dx Lattice spacing in meters, or 0 for auto. Auto lets FluidX3D size the lattice to the Memory budget (the spacing is whatever the domain happens to get). A value fixes the discretization: ceil(L/dx) cells per axis, Memory becomes a check. Cell count grows with 1/dx^3 — halving dx costs 8x VRAM and ~16x time. Number Live Run FluidX3D as a LIVE SERVER: after voxelising, the solver keeps running until stopped and streams one horizontal wind-speed slice (at Live Height) into a memory-mapped file that FluidX3D Live View (Source = Live server) repaints once a second. A changed Buildings mesh on Live View is re-voxelised in place — the flow continues, no restart. No VTK frames are written in this mode (Sim Time and Export Interval are not used); stop it from LBM Run's menu. Boolean Live Height LiveH Height above the ground of the live slice, in metres (pedestrian level 1.75 m). Fixed for the run: the server streams this one slice. Number Synthetic Turbulence Turb Perturb the inflow face with zero-mean synthetic turbulence at the log law's own intensity (I_u = 1/ln((z+z0)/z0), 18 % at z = z0 x 240), so the LES is fed fluctuations instead of a steady profile. On AIJ Case A this took the wake's bias from +0.64 to +0.07 and the reattachment length from 1.3 H to 0.6 H (tunnel 0.4-0.75 H); costs ~45 % more time on a discrete GPU. Off = the steady log law (the validation control: EDDY3D_VALIDATION_INFLOW = control; on = synthetic; FluidX3D has no jitter arm). Boolean Warmup W Warm-up seconds discarded before the time mean. Setting this, Averaging or Settle switches a plain solve from Sim Time with per-interval frames to warm-up + averaging through the solver's own time mean (the final u-.vtk IS the mean). 0 with Averaging or Settle set = auto: 2 flow-throughs of the domain at Uref, at least 60 s. Never used by a Live or Interactive run. Number Averaging A Averaging window seconds of the time mean (see Warmup). 0 with Warmup or Settle set = auto: 4 flow-throughs of the domain at Uref, at least 120 s. Number Integral Length Lint Eddy (integral) length of the Synthetic Turbulence in metres: the base wavelength of the inflow modes. 0 = the mixing length 0.41 x the ABL reference height. The written case's status reports the resolved length, the inlet intensity at z_ref and U(z_ref). Number Settle Stop the run early once its running mean has settled: the mean field's change between two consecutive flow-throughs under 3 % (two pairs in a row), never before Warmup + Averaging have passed. The solver is given 4x the averaging window and stopped by LBM Run as soon as it settles; a running-mean frame lands per flow-through meanwhile. Off = run exactly the window. Boolean Open Faces Open Make the faces other than the inlet OPEN instead of pinning every face to the log-law velocity: side and top faces become free-slip (zero normal velocity; the tangential velocity and the density are the interior's next to the face) and outflow faces a pressure outlet (velocity from the interior, density 1) — the symmetry and outflow conditions AIJ and COST 732 prescribe. Upstream FluidX3D has neither, so the setup refreshes the face cells from the interior every 16 steps. On by default (AIJ Case A: no worse, the synthetic arm slightly better; stable and mass-conserving on axis and oblique wind). Off = the legacy imposed faces. Boolean Wall Function Wall Give the flat ground a rough-wall log-law wall function (z0 from the ABL) instead of a plain no-slip wall, the way OpenLB's wall model does: every step the solver sets the first cell above the ground to the log law through the wind 3 cells above it, and lets the ground take that log law's drag (it alters one function of FluidX3D's kernel.cpp for the run). Without it the lowest ~4 cells read LOW: on an empty domain with 1 m cells, 34 % low at 1.5 m; with it, within 10 % from 0.5 to 2.5 m. Buildings, roofs and terrain stay no-slip. Off = the bounce-back ground. Boolean

docs.title: Geometry Repair - [source code]
docs.text: Check building geometry and repair it for snappyHexMesh: weld split vertices, remove degenerate and duplicate faces (and the shared walls of touching solids), orient every closed piece outward, optionally fill small holes and drop specks, then optionally rebuild it as a closed, manifold voxel WRAP — overlapping buildings fuse into one solid, courtyards open to the sky stay open, gaps narrower than about the wrap cell close. Runs in-process (no Python service). The case components already run the safe part automatically before meshing; use this to see what is wrong, to fill holes, or to wrap.

docs.title: Input
docs.text: Name Nickname Description Type Mesh M Geometry to check and repair (all inputs are merged). Breps: mesh them first. Mesh Weld Tolerance Tol Corners closer than this are merged into one (model units). 0 merges exact duplicates only. Default 0.001 (1 mm in metres, Rhino's default tolerance). Number Max Hole Size Hole Close holes whose rim fits in this size (diagonal of the rim's bounds). 0 leaves every hole open. Number Min Piece Size Min Drop disconnected pieces smaller than this (diagonal of their bounds). 0 keeps every piece. Number Wrap Replace the result by its closed voxel wrap: Off, If Leaky (only when the repaired mesh is still not watertight) or Always (also fuses overlapping buildings into one solid). Text Wrap Cell Size Cell Voxel size of the wrap. Features and gaps narrower than about this close; each block is wrapped in its own grid, coarsened (and said so) above 24M voxels. Use about half the snappyHexMesh cell at the building surface. Number Smoothing Smooth Taubin smoothing passes over the wrap's staircase (0 = none). Each corner stays within 0.3 cells of where it was; a pass that would fold a face is undone. Integer Run Check and repair (and wrap). Resets when the run starts; a wired toggle held true re-runs when the geometry changes. Boolean

docs.title: Output
docs.text: Name Nickname Description Type Mesh M The repaired (or wrapped) mesh. Mesh Watertight WT True when the result is closed, manifold and consistently oriented. Boolean Report R What was found before, what was changed, and what remains. Text Open Edges Open Open (boundary) edges of the INPUT: the rims of holes and gaps. Line Non-Manifold Edges NM Edges of the INPUT shared by three or more faces (fins, touching solids, internal walls). Line Bad Faces Bad Degenerate and duplicate faces of the INPUT. Mesh

docs.title: Height Bands - [source code]
docs.text: Refine the mesh in BANDS OF HEIGHT above the ground — level 3 within 4 m, level 2 within 10 m, level 1 within 24 m — everywhere on the site, not only near buildings. This is how the pedestrian layer gets resolved across open plazas and streets that no building refinement reaches. The bands follow the case's ground surfaces (terrain, ground ring and roughness zones), so on a sloped site they stay the same height above the ground; only a meshing dict with no ground surface gets the flat disk Centre and Radius describe. Wire Extras into the case component's Extras input beside any Refinement Region.

docs.title: Input
docs.text: Name Nickname Description Type Heights H Band upper edges above ground (m), e.g. 4, 10, 24. Each gets the level at the same position in Levels; levels must not INCREASE with height. Number Levels L snappyHexMesh refinement level per band, aligned with Heights, e.g. 3, 2, 1 (each level halves the cell size). A single value applies to every band. Integer Centre C Optional centre of the ground disk (its Z is the ground level), used only when the case has no ground surface to follow. Default: the origin at Z = 0. Point Radius R Radius (m) of the ground disk, used only when the case has no ground surface to follow (the bands then cover the whole ground). Beyond the rim, cells are refined by their distance to the rim instead of to the ground. Number Name Region key (a valid OpenFOAM word). Text

docs.title: Indoor Case - [source code]
docs.text: Build an indoor ventilation case (room + inlets + outlets + sinks + sources) for OpenFOAM 12. Isothermal by default. Wiring a Wall Temp, an Indoor Wall with a temperature or heat load, or a Heat Source switches it to the buoyant solver (foamRun -solver fluid: gravity, an energy equation and a temperature-dependent density), so temperature differences drive the flow — plumes, downdraughts, stratification, stack effect. The solve is steady unless Transient gives the buoyant solver a duration to integrate over; Write Interval sets how often it keeps a snapshot, uniformly or dense-then-sparse. Steady or transient, the solve runs on every core but one when Wind Run's Parallel is on. Method: De Simone, Kastner & Dogan (2021), Building Simulation 2021, Bruges, doi:10.26868/25222708.2021.30632.

docs.title: Input
docs.text: Name Nickname Description Type Case Name Name Case name (no spaces). Leave empty for an auto-generated name (same convention as Outdoor). Text Working Directory Dir Working directory (default ~/Eddy3D/Indoor). Text Room R Closed room Brep. Brep Cell Size C Mesh cell size (m). Number Inlets I Inlet surface(s): Brep or Indoor Inlet component(s). Generic Data Outlets O Outlet surface(s): Brep or Indoor Outlet component(s). Generic Data Inlet Speed U Fallback supply speed (m/s) over each raw-Brep inlet AS DRAWN: that inlet delivers Speed × its area. Ignored for Indoor Inlet components, which carry their own Speed or Flow Rate. Number Sinks S Momentum sinks (Indoor Sink). Generic Data Sources Src Emitters: Momentum / Heat / CO2 / Viral Source components. Generic Data Wall Temp WT Optional wall temperature (°C) for every room face no Indoor Wall covers. Setting it switches the case to the buoyant solver on its own; no Heat Source is needed. A value of 150 or more is read as Kelvin, as definitions saved before this input was °C expect. Number Walls W Optional Indoor Wall components with a Surface: each gets its own patch and temperature. Room faces not covered by one keep the case-wide Wall Temp. Generic Data Age of Air AoA Solve the mean age of air (OpenFOAM 'age' function object) during the run. Age [s] is the time since the air at each point entered the room — the ventilation map: low = well flushed, high = trapped in a corner the supply never reaches. Unlike an air-change rate, which is one number for the whole room, it says WHERE the ventilation fails. Adds a cheap scalar transport solved alongside the flow at every iteration; probe the 'age' field to read it. With it the case also writes, under postProcessing/ for Read Results, the flux-weighted age of the air leaving through the outlet (exhaustAge — the reference Ventilation Effectiveness divides by). Whenever the case has Age of Air OR a CO2/viral emitter it writes the flow it carried (supplyFlow, exhaustFlow, m³/s on the isothermal and the buoyant path), and every CO2/viral emitter gets its flux-weighted exhaust value (exhaustCO2, exhaustViral, per m³ of air) and the MESHED volume of its zone (viralSourceVolume_0, m³ — Infection Risk's Emitter Volume), with or without this. Optional; default is off. Boolean Transient t Optional simulated time in SECONDS. Leave empty for the steady solve, which answers where a room settles. Set it to follow how the room gets there — a warm-up, a cool-down, a plume that never settles: the buoyant solver then integrates in time under a Courant limit and keeps 20 snapshots over the run unless Write Interval says otherwise. Buoyant cases only (it needs a Wall Temp, an Indoor Wall with a temperature or heat load, or a Heat Source), and far more expensive than the steady solve. Number Extras Optional user additions from the Refinement Region and Custom Function Object components. Applied every time the case is written, so they survive a re-write. The indoor mesh dict is built programmatically and has no refinementRegions block of its own — one is created for a user region. Generic Data Location In Mesh Loc Optional point inside the room's AIR (snappyHexMesh's locationInMesh): the mesh keeps only the region connected to it. Leave empty to have one chosen — the room centre when that is open air, otherwise the point of the main air volume furthest from every surface. Set it when the room has several disconnected air volumes and the one to mesh is not the largest. Point Engine OpenFOAM execution environment for this case: BlueCFD, WSL, or Containerized (Docker/Podman). Read by the Run component. Text Initial Temp T0 Optional room air temperature (°C) at the START of the solve — 0/T's internal field — separate from every boundary: wall temperatures, the supply, heat sources and the outlet's backflow keep their own values. Start a room warm and ventilate it through ambient boundaries to watch it cool by the flow alone. Buoyant cases only (it needs a Wall Temp, an Indoor Wall with a temperature or heat load, or a Heat Source); most meaningful with Transient, since a steady solve settles to the same room wherever it starts. Empty = 20 °C. A value of 150 or more is read as Kelvin. Number Write Interval dt Optional seconds between the snapshots a Transient run keeps. One number: a uniform interval (empty = 20 snapshots over the run). Several numbers: the run is split into that many EQUAL phases and each phase writes at its own interval — [1, 5, 20] on a 300 s run keeps a snapshot every 1 s to 100 s, every 5 s to 200 s and every 20 s to 300 s, dense where the room changes fastest. Each snapshot is the full set of fields on disk, so a 1 s interval over a long run costs disk and time. Ignored without Transient. Number Write W Click to write the case to disk. Resets automatically so it never re-writes on recompute. Boolean Clear X Click to delete the case folder. Resets automatically so it never re-deletes on recompute. Boolean

docs.title: Output
docs.text: Name Nickname Description Type Case C The indoor case (for the Run component). Generic Data Logs L Build / write logs. Text

docs.title: Indoor Comfort Map - [source code]
docs.text: Per-point thermal comfort from probed indoor CFD fields: PMV/PPD (EN ISO 7730), operative temperature, ISO 7730 draught rate (from k when probed, else Tu = 40 %), head-to-ankle temperature difference (ISO 7730 PD and ASHRAE 55 PPD), ADPI (ASHRAE 113, cooling) and the share of points meeting ISO 7730 categories A/B/C, EN 16798-1 I-IV and ASHRAE 55. Probe the same points for T, U, k (and T again at head and ankle height). Temperatures in kelvin — what OpenFOAM writes — are converted automatically. Not assessed: radiant asymmetry, floor temperature, and ASHRAE 55's SET method for points above 0.2 m/s (reported separately). Formulas pinned against pythermalcomfort (Tartarini & Schiavon 2020) and ISO 7730 Annex D.

docs.title: Input
docs.text: Name Nickname Description Type Air Temperature Ta Air temperature at each occupant point, at body height (0.6 m seated / 1.1 m standing): the Probe's T (kelvin is converted) or °C. Generic Data Air Speed V Mean air speed at the same points: the Probe's U vectors (their magnitude is used) or speeds in m/s. Generic Data Turbulent Kinetic Energy k Probed k (m²/s²) at the same points, for the draught rate's turbulence intensity Tu = 100·√(2k/3)/v. Unwired: ISO 7730's default Tu = 40 %. Generic Data Radiant Temperature Tr Mean radiant temperature (°C or K): one value for the room or one per point. Unwired: equal to the air temperature (walls at air temperature — say so in a report). Generic Data Relative Humidity RH Relative humidity (%), one value or one per point. Number Head Temperature Th Air temperature at head height (1.1 m seated / 1.7 m standing), one per point. With Ankle Temperature it drives the vertical-difference criterion; also used as the draught (neck) temperature. Generic Data Ankle Temperature Tf Air temperature at ankle height (0.1 m), one per point. Generic Data Metabolic Rate M Metabolic rate (met). Number Clothing Clo Clothing insulation (clo). Number Posture Pos Seated or standing: sets which heights the head/ankle probes represent and the ASHRAE 55 gradient span. Text Control Temperature Tc ADPI control temperature (°C). Unwired: the mean of the air temperatures. Number

docs.title: Output
docs.text: Name Nickname Description Type PMV Predicted Mean Vote per point (EN ISO 7730). Number PPD Predicted Percentage Dissatisfied per point (%). Number Operative Temperature To Operative temperature per point (°C, ISO 7726). Number Draught Rate DR ISO 7730 draught rate per point (%). Number Vertical PD PD ISO 7730 percentage dissatisfied from the head-ankle difference per point (%); empty without head/ankle input. Number Effective Draft Temperature EDT ASHRAE 113 effective draft temperature per point (K). Number ISO 7730 Category ISO Best ISO 7730 category met per point (A/B/C/Outside). Text EN 16798-1 Category EN Best EN 16798-1 category met per point (I-IV/Outside). Text ASHRAE 55 A55 Per point: Compliant, NotCompliant, or ElevatedAirSpeed (above 0.2 m/s — the SET method applies, not assessed here). Text Summary Sum Occupied-zone statistics. Text Comfort Map Map The whole map, for the Ventilation & Comfort Report. Generic Data

The air enters perpendicular to the surface, into the room, whichever way the surface faces.

Number Temperature T Inlet air temperature (°C). Applied when the case is thermal (Indoor Case has a Wall Temp, an Indoor Wall with a temperature or heat load, or a Heat Source); an isothermal case has no temperature field, and Indoor Case warns when a value other than 20 °C is dropped. Number Flow Rate Q Optional supply flow in LITRES PER SECOND (L/s) through this opening — the unit a diffuser schedule is written in (1 L/s = 3.6 m³/h). Replaces Speed when given. Number

docs.title: Infection Risk - [source code]
docs.text: Airborne infection risk by the Wells–Riley model, and the ASHRAE 241-2023 equivalent clean airflow check. Well-mixed: P = 1 − exp(−dose), with the room concentration rising from zero under outdoor air + air cleaning + deposition (0.24 /h) + viral inactivation (0.63 /h) (Buonanno, Stabile & Morawska 2020). Spatial: the Indoor Case's viral tracer, probed at the breathing zone, rescaled to quanta/m³ by what the case measured leaving the room (Exhaust Tracer × Carried Flow), or — without those — by the Viral Emitter's rate × MESHED zone volume; given both, the second cross-checks the first. Ventilation-only, as the CFD removes nothing else. The case writes the tracer per m³ of air, the carried flow in m³/s and each emitter's meshed zone volume on both the isothermal and the buoyant path, so the same wiring holds for both — wire a FINISHED solve: the cross-check tests the inputs, not convergence. ASHRAE 241: Table 5-1's ECAi per person × occupants (×2 for group vocalization, §5.1.3) against the achieved outdoor air + air cleaning (Eq. 6-1; in-duct cleaning = recirculated flow × single-pass efficiency, Eq. 7-1). CAVEATS: quanta emission rates are uncertain by orders of magnitude and depend on activity (breathing, speaking, singing) — compare designs rather than quote absolute risks; Wells–Riley covers long-range airborne transmission only; ASHRAE 241 also requires a building readiness plan and tested equipment, which this check does not cover.

docs.title: Input
docs.text: Name Nickname Description Type Room Volume V Air volume of the room (m³). Number Outdoor Air OA The DESIGN outdoor (supply) airflow to the room, in L/s: the ASHRAE 241 achieved ECA and the well-mixed risk. The spatial map's tracer scaling uses Carried Flow instead (the flow the solved case really carried, which snapping makes differ from the design), and falls back to this only when Carried Flow is not wired. Below 0.1 L/s per occupant — a twenty-fifth of ASHRAE 62.1's 2.5 L/s — it is warned as a flow typed in m³/s (0.5 m³/s is 500 L/s). 0 is accepted: ASHRAE 241 lets Air Cleaning supply the whole ECA. Number Air Cleaning ACS Equivalent clean airflow from air cleaning (L/s): in-duct filters = recirculated flow × single-pass efficiency (MERV-A 11 or better, ASHRAE 241 §4.2.3), in-room cleaners = tested CADR. Number Space Type Space ASHRAE 241-2023 Table 5-1 occupancy category (a bare name such as 'Classroom' also works). Text Occupants N People in the breathing zone (ASHRAE 241 P_Z). Integer Group Vocalization Voc Singing, chanting or loud group speech: doubles the required ECA (ASHRAE 241 §5.1.3). Boolean Infectors I Infectious occupants present. Number Quanta Rate q Quanta emitted per infector per hour. ILLUSTRATIVE default — it spans orders of magnitude with activity (Buonanno et al. 2020); set it for the scenario. Number Breathing Rate p Inhalation rate of a susceptible (m³/h): 0.49 resting, 0.54 standing, 1.38 light exercise. Number Exposure t Exposure duration (h). Number Viral Tracer C Probed 'viral' tracer at breathing-zone points (optional — the spatial map). Generic Data Emitter Rate IR The Viral Emitter's Injection Rate (SPECIFIC, 1/s — per m³ of its zone). With Emitter Volume it scales the map when no solved Exhaust Tracer and Carried Flow are wired, and cross-checks them when they are. Several Viral Emitters: the cross-check compares Ce × Qc with the SUM r × Vz over all of them — with equal rates give this one rate and, as Emitter Volume, the sum of their zones' volumes (viralSourceVolume_0 + _1 + …). Number Emitter Volume Vz The MESHED volume of the Viral Emitter's zone, in m³, as the case writes it: Read Results with Dataset 'viralSourceVolume_0' (postProcessing/viralSourceVolume_0 — one per emitter, numbered like the solver's viralSource_0, whose "selected N cell(s) with volume V" it reproduces), its Values wired here — the LAST value is used. NOT the drawn box's volume: the rate is per m³ of the zone and boxToCell selects cells by centre, so the zone is whatever cells the box caught (the reference room's 1.8 m³ box meshed 1.4496 m³; typed as 1.8 the cross-check reads 0.805). Several Viral Emitters: the sum r × Vz over all of them is what the cross-check needs (see Emitter Rate). Number Exhaust Tracer Ce The FLUX-weighted mean of 'viral' in the air leaving the room, as the Indoor case writes it: Read Results with Dataset 'exhaustViral' (postProcessing/exhaustViral), its Values wired here — the LAST value, the final written time, is used (0 there means the case is not solved yet: a Warning). With Carried Flow it scales the map — Ce × Qc is the emission the case measured leaving — and Emitter Rate × Emitter Volume, when given, is checked against it. Not a point probed at the outlet: the exhaust carries the flux-weighted mean (the balance closes at 1.000 with it, 0.983 with the area average). Number Carried Flow Qc The flow the case CARRIED out of the room, as a VOLUME flow in m³/s (not a kg/s mass flow: nothing here can tell one from the other, and a mass flow reads about 15 % low): Read Results with Dataset 'exhaustFlow' (postProcessing/exhaustFlow, m³/s on the isothermal and the buoyant path), its Values wired straight in — the LAST value is used. Used ONLY for the spatial map: with the Exhaust Tracer it scales the tracer to quanta (Ce × Qc) and is what the emitter is cross-checked against. Outdoor Air stays the design flow of the ASHRAE 241 check and the well-mixed risk; a Carried Flow outside 0.03–30 × Outdoor Air (snapping and recirculation stay inside it: 5–10 % outdoor air is 10–20 ×) is warned as the L/s ↔ m³/s slip it is. The inlet's supplyFlow (negative, read as its magnitude) works too, but prefer exhaustFlow: on the buoyant path the supply is the colder, denser air and carries a smaller volume than leaves (0.5000 against 0.5008 m³/s at 300 W; about 2 % at a 3 kW heater, estimated). Unwired: Outdoor Air stands in for it, with a Remark. Number

Number Steady Probability Pss Same, with the room at steady state throughout (%) — an upper bound. Number Expected Cases Cases Susceptibles (occupants − infectors) × P. Number Point Probability Pi Per breathing-zone point, from the viral tracer (%). Number Required ECA ECAreq ASHRAE 241 V_ECAi (L/s). Number Achieved ECA ECA Outdoor air + air cleaning (L/s). Number ASHRAE 241 Pass Pass Achieved ≥ required. Boolean Summary Sum Readable summary. Text Infection Risk Risk The assessment, for the Ventilation & Comfort Report. Generic Data
