docs.title: LBM Case - [source code]
docs.text: Build a lattice-Boltzmann wind case from the ABL, the geometry and a settings object, and write it to disk. Wire 'LBM Run Settings' for OpenLB or 'FluidX3D Run Settings' for FluidX3D (nothing = OpenLB). Feed the Case output to LBM Run, then to Probe, LBM Field or FluidX3D Live View — the same Case → Run → Probe chain as the OpenFOAM wind study.

docs.title: Input
docs.text: Name Nickname Description Type Case Name Name Case folder name below Working Directory. Letters, numbers, hyphens, and underscores only. Empty = a generated name (like swift-otter-fjord-lantern), kept with the document and shared with the other studies in it, as on the Outdoor Case. Text Working Directory Dir Parent directory for named LBM cases (optional; default ~/Eddy3D/Cases/LBM, or ~/Eddy3D/Cases/FluidX3D for the GPU engine). Must not contain spaces when running in a container (the case becomes a bind-mount source); the Native runtime has no such restriction. Text ABL ABL inflow from the 'ABL Flow' component — the SAME boundary condition the OpenFOAM engines use (reference speed, reference height, roughness length, direction). Uses the first wind direction (one direction per case). Generic Data Domain Simulation domain (optional). Accepts the Box Domain component's output — its Front/Back/Side/Top extensions override the auto margins (Cell Size and refinement are OpenFOAM meshing concepts and are ignored; lattice spacing comes from the settings) — or a plain Box, used verbatim as the domain extents. Generic Data Buildings B Building geometry. Mesh Terrain T Terrain / ground context meshes (optional; merged with the buildings). Mesh Vegetation Veg Tree crowns (optional; OpenLB only): closed solid meshes, or the Outdoor+ 'Vegetation Region' object — the SAME trees can drive the UMF case and this engine. Simulated as porous canopy cells that slow the wind without blocking it. Vegetation Region objects carry their own Cd x LAD; plain meshes use the Vegetation Drag setting. FluidX3D has no canopy model and ignores this input. Generic Data Pollutants Src Pollutant emitters (optional; OpenLB CPU only): the Outdoor 'Pollutant Source' objects — the SAME sources the OpenFOAM wind study takes. Each species becomes a passive scalar carried by the LES wind and diffused by its turbulence (Sc_t from the source); LBM Field reads the time-averaged concentration in kg/m³. At most four species. Generic Data Engine Eng Which lattice-Boltzmann engine builds the case. OpenLB: CPU/GPU wind with vegetation and pollutants (wire 'LBM Run Settings'). FluidX3D: GPU wind, no canopy or scalar model (wire 'FluidX3D Run Settings'). A Settings object that belongs to the other engine is an error, not a switch. Auto follows the Settings object (nothing wired = OpenLB) and is what documents saved before this input behave as. Text Settings S 'LBM Run Settings' (OpenLB) or 'FluidX3D Run Settings' (FluidX3D) — it must match Engine. Optional; nothing means the chosen engine's defaults (OpenLB under Auto). Generic Data Write W Write the case to disk (STL + case files + launch script) without running it. Boolean Clear Delete this named case folder and all of its contents — for FluidX3D also the results left in the shared source tree. Boolean

docs.title: Output
docs.text: Name Nickname Description Type Logs L Case status / write log. Text Case C The LBM case: wire into LBM Run to launch it, and into Probe / LBM Field / FluidX3D Live View to read it (text sockets receive the case directory). Generic Data Domain D Resolved simulation domain in world coordinates (wind-aligned for OpenLB, world-aligned for FluidX3D). Updates live with the inputs — no Write needed; the standard preview renders it in the viewport. Box Folder F Case root folder: the OpenLB case directory, or the FluidX3D case root holding the source tree beside the VTK export directory that Case points at. Text

docs.title: LBM Field - [source code]
docs.text: Read the time-averaged pedestrian wind field from an LBM case directory. Outputs world-frame points and velocity vectors — plug both into the Vector Field Viewer.

docs.title: Input
docs.text: Name Nickname Description Type Case C LBM case directory (the 'Case' output of the LBM Run component). Text Refresh R Re-read the results (toggle while a run is in progress). Boolean

docs.title: Output
docs.text: Name Nickname Description Type Points P Probe points (world frame). Point Velocity V Time-averaged velocity per point (m/s, world frame). Vector Speed S Speed magnitude per point (m/s). Number Status St Read status. Text Spread Sd Per-point standard deviation of the speed across the perturbed-inflow ensemble members (m/s). Empty for a single run. High spread — typically in wakes and shear layers — means the local result is sensitive to inflow uncertainty; give comfort verdicts there extra margin. Number Species Sp Pollutant species the case transports (from the LBM Case Pollutants input), one per Concentration branch. Empty when the case has no pollutant sources. Text Concentration Conc Time-averaged pollutant concentration per point (kg/m³): branch {i} is Species item i, index-aligned with Points. Number Temperature Rise dT Time-averaged air temperature rise over the ambient per point (K), index-aligned with Points. Empty for an isothermal case (no heat flux on LBM Run Settings). Number

docs.title: LBM Live View - [source code]
docs.text: Watch an OpenLB wind solve live in the viewport: colors an analysis mesh with the wind speed of the newest probe snapshot while the solver runs, repainting as each snapshot lands. The solver writes the instantaneous field during warm-up, the running average after, and the final average at the end. Also shows the final field of a completed run. Wire the LBM Run component's Case output into Case, and a mesh lying on the probe layer (the horizontal plane the solver samples: Probe Height on LBM Run Settings, 1.5 m above the ground by default) into Mesh. A vertex is read by interpolating the probes around it; vertices off the layer stay grey. Record keeps every snapshot that lands (results/snapshots/), and Frame plays the recording back: -1 shows the newest snapshot, 0 the first recorded one. Animate a slider on Frame for a replay; Window Start/End show the MEAN over a frame range instead; Video renders every recorded frame through the active viewport into an MP4 (ffmpeg on PATH).

docs.title: Input
docs.text: Name Nickname Description Type Case LBM case directory: the 'Case' output of the LBM Run component. Text Mesh Analysis mesh to color, read at its vertices. It must lie on the probe layer: a horizontal plane at pedestrian height covering the area you want to watch. Mesh Max Speed Max Top of the color scale in m/s. 0 = auto: grows with the largest speed seen this session, so colors stay comparable across snapshots instead of rescaling on every one. Number Frame Recorded frame to show (0 = the first recorded snapshot); -1 = the newest snapshot of the run. Beyond the last frame shows the last. Integer Record Keep every snapshot that lands, so the run can be played back with Frame (results/snapshots/). Boolean Live Keep watching the case for new snapshots and repaint as they land. Boolean Appearance Look What the colours show. Velocity: wind speed in m/s against Max Speed. Speedup: wind speed divided by the case's reference inflow speed at reference height (U_ref from LBM Run's case), against Max Speedup — 1 is the undisturbed wind, above it the flow is accelerated. '+ LIC': the same colours with a line integral convolution of sparse noise over them — thin white strands gliding along the probes' velocity vectors (the mean of a playback window's frames when one is set); a picture of the flow, not a quantity. Text Max Speedup MaxSU Top of the colour scale when Appearance is Speedup (0 = 1.5). Number Window Start WinA First recorded frame of a playback window (0 = the first recorded snapshot); -1 = off. With Window End set too, the mesh shows the MEAN speed over the window instead of a single frame. Integer Window End WinB Last recorded frame of the playback window (inclusive); -1 = off. Integer Video Render every recorded frame through the active Rhino viewport into results/video/live-view.mp4 (PNG frames stay beside it). Needs ffmpeg on PATH; the status says where to get it otherwise. Boolean

docs.title: Output
docs.text: Name Nickname Description Type Mesh The analysis mesh, vertex-colored by wind speed (bake to keep the colors). Mesh Speeds Wind speed per mesh vertex, m/s (aligned with the mesh's vertex order; null off the probe layer). Number Time Simulated time of the displayed snapshot, in seconds (unset when the file carries none). Number Status Snapshot / watcher status. Text Frames Snapshots in the recording. Integer Histogram Hist Speed histogram of the displayed frame: 20 equal bins over 0-Max Speed, one line per bin, and the share of probed vertices above 5 m/s. Text

docs.title: LBM Run - [source code]
docs.text: Launch a lattice-Boltzmann case from the LBM Case component (OpenLB in a container or natively, or FluidX3D on the GPU — whichever the case was built with). Writes the case first if it has not been written, then starts the solver in a terminal window (untick 'Show solver window' in the right-click menu to run it in the background) and follows it: a progress bar with the time left, live warnings, and a refresh of everything downstream when the run moves on or finishes. A case already solving is followed, never started twice. Right-click to stop the run, list what is running on this machine, or open its log. Read results with Probe (points), LBM Field (the probe layer) or FluidX3D Live View.

docs.title: Input
docs.text: Name Nickname Description Type Case C The LBM case from the LBM Case component. Generic Data Run R Write the case (if needed) and launch the solver. Boolean

docs.title: Output
docs.text: Name Nickname Description Type Logs L Run log / status. Text Case C Case directory the readers resolve against (the OpenLB case, or the FluidX3D VTK export directory) — plug into Probe, LBM Field or FluidX3D Live View. Text Domain D Resolved simulation domain in world coordinates, as on the LBM Case component. Box Folder F Case root folder: the OpenLB case directory, or the FluidX3D case root holding the source tree beside the VTK export directory that Case points at. Text Progress 0 to 1 of the simulated window (an ensemble: of all its members). Number Done True once the run finished and wrote its results. Boolean Remaining Left Estimated seconds until the run finishes, from how fast it has been progressing. Empty until the progress has moved twice. Number Simulated Time SimT Simulated time [s] at each progress report of the run so far — the x axis for Max Speed. Number Max Speed MaxU Peak velocity [m/s] in the domain at each Simulated Time (OpenLB; FluidX3D does not report it). A run heading for instability climbs here long before it fails. Number

docs.title: LBM Run Settings - [source code]
docs.text: Solver controls for the container-based LBM wind engine (grid spacing, warmup and averaging windows, probe layer, GPU, container runtime).

docs.title: Input
docs.text: Name Nickname Description Type Grid Spacing dx Lattice spacing in meters. Cell count grows with 1/dx^3 — halving dx costs 8x memory and ~16x time. Number Warmup W Physical seconds of simulated wind discarded before averaging starts. 0 = auto: two domain flow-throughs (length / reference speed), at least 60 s — fixed seconds quietly under-run large domains. Number Averaging A Physical seconds of simulated wind averaged into the reported field. 0 = auto: four domain flow-throughs, at least 120 s. Number Probe Height Hp Height above ground of the pedestrian-level result layer (m). Number Probe Spacing Sp Spacing of the result grid (m). 0 = auto: follows Grid Spacing (one probe per lattice cell), coarsened by powers of two if that would put more than 200,000 probes on the canvas. Sampling FINER than the grid does not resolve more — neighbouring probes then interpolate inside the same lattice cells. Number GPU Run the CUDA build of the solver image (needs an NVIDIA GPU + container toolkit; Windows/Linux only — macOS containers have no CUDA). Boolean Runtime Rt How the solver runs. Auto prefers Podman, falls back to Docker, then to a native install; Docker and Podman run the same OCI image. Native runs a host-installed eddy3dWind executable with NO container at all — the Windows path when neither Podman nor Docker Desktop is an option. Native is CPU (OpenMP) only; the CUDA build ships as a container image. Text Image Img Container image override. Empty = docker.io/pkastner/openlb-wind:1.9.3-r6@sha256:40a0b26464c5b434fc0d5368fe0792897427158266da8c1eabb7ff3982e4e195. Text Jitter Jit Slowly vary the inflow direction by a few degrees (deterministic). Seeds resolved unsteadiness a steady analytic inflow lacks, so exposed upstream areas stop reading unrealistically calm. Off = perfectly steady inflow. The validation runs' EDDY3D_VALIDATION_INFLOW arms on this component: control = Turb off + Jitter off; jitter = Turb off + Jitter on (4 degrees there, the amplitude below defaults to 5); synthetic = Turb on. Boolean Jitter Amplitude Jd Direction variation in degrees when Jitter is on. Number Vegetation Drag Veg Crown density for PLAIN meshes wired into the LBM Run component's Vegetation input, as Cd x leaf area density (1/m): 0.1 sparse, 0.25 typical, 0.5 dense. Vegetation Region objects carry their own Cd x LAD and ignore this. Number Perturbed Inflow UQ Run a perturbed-inflow ensemble instead of a single solve: members re-run the case with the inflow speed varied +/-10% and direction +/-6 deg (realistic measurement uncertainty); LBM Field then reports the mean plus a per-point spread that flags wake regions where the result is inflow-sensitive. Runtime scales with Ensemble. Boolean Ensemble N Member count when Perturbed Inflow is on (3 = nominal + speed pair, 5 adds the direction pair, up to 9). Integer Vegetation Density VegD Crown density preset for PLAIN vegetation meshes (sets Vegetation Drag = Cd x LAD). Custom uses the Vegetation Drag input. Vegetation Region objects carry their own Cd x LAD and ignore both. Text Ground Gnd How the solver treats the ground (OpenLB). None is the no-slip bounce-back: it lets the log-law inflow collapse in the lowest cells (measured at 1 m cells: -53 % at 1.5 m after 100 m). Power law and Spalding are OpenLB's wall-modelled ground and hold the profile; they are smooth-wall models. Rough adds the rough-wall log law with the ABL's z0, so the ground shear follows the roughness like OpenFOAM's rough wall function. Costs about 2.5x the run time. Text Displacement Height d Zero-plane displacement of the log-law inflow (m): the profile starts at d and is zero below it, for an approach flow over an urban or forest canopy the domain does not model (d is roughly 0.7 x the canopy height). 0 = the plain log law. Must stay below the ABL's reference height. Number Outlet Sponge Sponge Fraction of the domain length in front of the outlet that becomes an absorbing sponge layer relaxing the flow to the inflow profile (OpenLB; 0 = the plain pressure outlet). The pressure outlet bends the profile over the last ~20 % of the domain (measured, 200 m domain: +16 % at 5.5 m, -21 % at 30.5 m at the outlet); a 0.1 sponge keeps the field ahead of it within ~3 %. Treat the sponge zone itself as padding, not as results. At most 0.5. Number Synthetic Turbulence Turb Turbulent inflow (OpenLB): OpenLB's vortex method adds random eddies to the log-law inlet, sized ~0.4 x the reference height, with the intensity of the log law (I_u = 1/ln(z/z0)), refreshed once per eddy passage. Replaces Jitter. On AIJ Case A it cut the wake's bias from +0.88 to +0.59 and the reattachment length from 2.0 H to 1.3 H against the steady inflow at H/20, and beat the jitter at both resolutions tried (docs/VALIDATION.md 10b), so it is the default, on the CPU and the CUDA solver alike. Off = the steady profile (the validation control). The strip names the arm: synthetic, jitter or steady, as EDDY3D_VALIDATION_INFLOW does. Boolean Wind Schedule Sched Time-varying wind (OpenLB), one line or item per point: time (s), wind speed at the ABL's reference height (m/s), wind direction (deg, from, clockwise from north) - e.g. hourly weather replayed in minutes. Linear between points, held beyond the ends; the time-averaged result covers the averaging window. Every direction must stay within 45 degrees of the ABL direction (with Jitter): set the ABL to the mean direction. Empty = a steady wind. Text Settle Stop the run early once its running average has settled: the change of the probe-layer mean between consecutive snapshots (mean |du| in % of the mean speed) at or under this value for two snapshots in a row. 0 = run the whole averaging window; 3 is a sensible value, and the window then stays the upper bound. Single runs only (an ensemble's members solve one after another). Number Ground Heat Flux Qg Sensible heat flux from the ground into the air (W/m², OpenLB): 0 = isothermal. Roughly 100-300 on a sunny afternoon over paving, negative at night. The air warms and rises (Boussinesq); LBM Field reads the Temperature Rise. Number Building Heat Flux Qb Sensible heat flux from every building surface into the air (W/m²), as Ground Heat Flux. Number Air Temperature Ta Ambient (inflow) air temperature (°C) the temperature rise is measured from; sets the expansion coefficient 1/T of the buoyancy. Number Refine Resolve a box around the buildings at half the Grid Spacing (OpenLB): half their height upwind, one height on the sides, six heights downwind so the wakes stay inside (a box face across a wake loses it), up to twice their height; coupled to the rest of the lattice by OpenLB's Rohde scheme. Each refined cell costs 16 coarse ones (8 cells x 2 steps): it pays when the box is a small part of a large domain. Not with pollutants or heat fluxes yet. Boolean Integral Length Lint Eddy (integral) length of the Synthetic Turbulence in metres: the size of the vortices seeded on the inlet. 0 = derived, max(2 x Grid Spacing, 0.41 x the ABL reference height). The written case's status reports the resolved length, the inlet intensity at z_ref and U(z_ref). Number Instant Snapshots Inst Write every in-progress probe snapshot as the INSTANTANEOUS field for the whole run instead of the running mean once averaging starts. Needed for Live View's playback window; the solver image must carry the ProbeSnapshotField key (an older image ignores it and keeps writing means). Boolean

docs.title: Output
docs.text: Name Nickname Description Type Settings S LBM run settings for the 'LBM Run' component. Generic Data

docs.title: Land Cover Roughness - [source code]
docs.text: Fetch land-cover polygons around a location from OpenStreetMap (open data, Overpass API) — plus surface car parks, pedestrian areas and bare ground — and classify each into an aerodynamic roughness length via the Davenport-Wieringa terrain classification, with the terrain elevation around the site (AWS Terrain Tiles, open data). Outputs ready-made ground roughness zones draped on a terrain mesh for the wind case.

docs.title: Input
docs.text: Name Nickname Description Type Latitude Lat Latitude of the SITE (the point the Anchor plane maps to), decimal degrees WGS84 — wire Download Weather's Site Latitude, or read it off a map. Not an EPW header or Deconstruct Weather's Latitude: those give the weather STATION, usually an airport kilometres away. Number Longitude Lon Longitude of the SITE, decimal degrees WGS84 (east positive) — wire Download Weather's Site Longitude, or read it off a map. Not an EPW header or Deconstruct Weather's Longitude: those give the weather STATION. Number Radius R Half-size (m) of the square query window around the location. Optional; default is 500. Number Terrain Radius TR Half-size (m) of the terrain mesh window. Make it cover the WHOLE CFD domain floor (domain radius plus margins) — the land-cover zones only cover Radius, and the terrain must continue beyond them. Keep it at least Radius: land cover beyond the terrain has no ground to become a zone on and is left out (with a Warning). Optional; default is 2 x Radius. Number Anchor Plane Model-space plane the lat/lon location maps to (polygons are placed on it, X = east, Y = north). Optional; default is the world XY origin. Plane Refinement Level RefLvl Snappy surface refinement level for the zone patches. Optional; default -1 = follow the case's ground level (Mesh Settings' ground refinement, prism layers included), so the land-cover floor is meshed like the ground around it. A document saved before this default keeps the level it was saved with (2). Integer Color By How the preview and the Colored Mesh output colour the ground. 'Land use' paints each zone by what it is (water, grass & parks, forest, paved, residential, ...); 'Roughness' paints it by z0 on a FIXED logarithmic scale anchored on the eight Davenport classes (0.0002 m pale yellow to 2 m dark brown), so a z0 has the same colour in every document and component. Terrain no zone covers is grey in both. Display only: the zones, their z0 and the written case are identical either way. Text Fetch Press to query OpenStreetMap (the land cover, then the paved and bare-soil surfaces) AND download the terrain tiles, in the background — the canvas stays live. Responses are cached on disk, so later solves and document opens read them offline. One press is one attempt: a Fetch held true by a wired toggle does not retry a failed download on every recompute — press again, or flip the toggle off and on. Right-click the component to cancel, or to force a refresh. Boolean

docs.title: Output
docs.text: Name Nickname Description Type Ground Zones Zones Ground roughness zones, clipped to the query window; plug into the wind case's Ground Roughness input. Where polygons overlap, the SMALLEST wins, so a lake inside a park keeps water's z0. With a terrain, each zone is the terrain faces whose centres lie inside its outline, and the wind case re-cuts the terrain along the same outlines at write time, so the zone patches and the remaining ground always tile. A polygon that owns no terrain face (covered by smaller zones, smaller than a terrain cell, or beyond a terrain smaller than the query window) is left out of all four zone outputs, and a message counts it. Without a terrain the zones are flat plates on the anchor plane. Ground Zones, Boundaries, Roughness Lengths and Land Cover are index-aligned. Generic Data Boundaries Crvs Closed land-cover outline per zone (index-aligned with Ground Zones), in model space. Draped on the terrain when there is one: every vertex, and every point where the outline crosses a terrain grid line or cell diagonal, lies on the surface the case meshes. Flat on the anchor plane otherwise. Curve Roughness Lengths z0 Roughness length z0 (m) per zone, index-aligned with Ground Zones. Number Land Cover Class Davenport class and source OSM tag per zone (e.g. 'closed (landuse=forest)'), index-aligned with Ground Zones. Text Terrain T The FULL terrain mesh around the site (AWS Terrain Tiles / SRTM-3DEP merge), placed on the anchor plane with elevation RELATIVE to the site (the location sits at the anchor origin); plug into the wind case Terrain input. The wind case splits the zone areas out of it at write time, so the meshed ground and the zone patches always tile without coincident surfaces. Not previewed by this component (its coloured zones cover the same surface). Mesh Site Elevation Elev Absolute elevation (m above sea level) of the location — the datum the Terrain mesh's z=0 corresponds to. Number Colored Mesh Color The ground as ONE vertex-coloured mesh for display and export: every zone piece in its Color By colour, plus the terrain no zone covers in grey — the tiling the wind case writes. Without a terrain, the flat zone plates. Not previewed by this component, which draws the same colours lit; wire it into a Mesh param or bake it. It is a copy: editing it changes nothing in the case. Mesh

docs.title: Land Cover Runoff - [source code]
docs.text: Fetches land-cover polygons around a lat/lon from OpenStreetMap (open data, no key) and classifies each into a Curve Number and an overland Manning's n. This is the same Overpass query the Land Cover Roughness component makes, read for runoff instead of for wind — so wiring both on one site costs one fetch, not two. Unmapped tags are skipped rather than guessed at.

docs.title: Input
docs.text: Name Nickname Description Type Latitude Lat Site latitude in decimal degrees. Number Longitude Lon Site longitude in decimal degrees. Number Radius Half-width in metres of the square window fetched around the site. Keep it close to the terrain's own extent: Overpass returns the FULL geometry of anything touching the window, and a large one drags in metro-scale polygons. Number Soil Group Soil Hydrologic soil group underneath. It shifts every Curve Number: the same lawn sheds far more on clay than on sand, so this is the single input here with the largest effect on the answer. B is the usual default when nothing local is known. Text Anchor Model-space point the lat/lon maps to. Default is the origin. Point

docs.title: Output
docs.text: Name Nickname Description Type Zones Runoff zones for Stormwater Grid, largest first: Grid stamps them in list order with the last one winning, so a polygon nested in another (a lake in a park) keeps its own surface. Put hand-drawn Runoff Zones AFTER these to override them. Generic Data Outlines Curves The classified polygons, so they can be edited or rebuilt by hand. Curve Classes What each polygon was classified as. Text Curve Numbers CN Curve Number assigned to each polygon, for the chosen soil group. Number

docs.title: Layer Runoff - [source code]
docs.text: Runoff zones from the ground layers a site model already has: wire LiDAR Site's Layer Outlines and Layer Kinds, and every outline becomes a zone with the Curve Number and overland Manning's n of what the ground there is (grass, park, forest, residential, paved…). The rain then falls on the same polygons the wind study's roughness and City Surface's layers were built from, with no second fetch. A kind takes the hydrology of its typical OpenStreetMap tag, for the chosen soil group. Roads, paved areas and paths read as paved (CN 98). An outline whose name is not a ground kind (a roughness class such as roughly_open) is skipped and counted: wire Layer Kinds, not Layer Names. Put hand-drawn Runoff Zones after these to override them.

docs.title: Input
docs.text: Name Nickname Description Type Layer Outlines Layer The ground layers' closed outlines: LiDAR Site's Layer Outlines, most specific first, as City Surface takes them. Curve Layer Kinds Kinds What the ground of each outline is (water, grass, park, forest, residential, roads, paved…): LiDAR Site's Layer Kinds, one per outline. Text Soil Group Soil Hydrologic soil group under the site: it decides the Curve Number of every pervious kind. Text

docs.title: Output
docs.text: Name Nickname Description Type Zones Runoff zones for Stormwater Grid, least specific first: Grid stamps them in list order with the last one winning, so a pond in a park keeps its own surface. Put hand-drawn Runoff Zones AFTER these to override them. Generic Data Classes The hydrologic class each zone was given. Text Curve Numbers CN Curve Number of each zone, for the chosen soil group. Number

docs.title: LiDAR Site - [source code]
docs.text: Fetch open LiDAR and building footprints for a site from its latitude and longitude, for City Surface: the footprints over a square of the given Size, the point cloud (the terrain) over a larger square, Terrain Size — the ground a CFD domain stands on reaches further than the buildings that matter. The Netherlands: AHN (Het Waterschapshuis, CC-BY 4.0) from its official sheets — a sheet is ~5 GB and is downloaded once into the cache, then every site in it is read from there — with BAG footprints (Kadaster, CC0). The United States: USGS 3DEP (public domain), only the point-cloud nodes over the site, with GlobalBuildingAtlas footprints (TUM, CC BY-NC 4.0; OpenStreetMap if it cannot be read). France (IGN LiDAR HD, Licence Ouverte), Switzerland (swissSURFACE3D, swisstopo), Bavaria (CC BY 4.0), Scotland (National LiDAR Programme, OGL), Estonia (Maa- ja Ruumiamet), Denmark (Danmarks Højdemodel), Spain (PNOA 2022-25: Aragon, Extremadura, the Canaries) and Slovenia (GURS CLSS), the last three from the open-lidar-data mirror: the 1 km tiles over the site, 65-250 MB each (Slovenia's 2024 flight up to 1 GB), cached once, with the same footprints. Everything comes out in metres around the site centre: wire Point Cloud, Footprints and Domain into City Surface. Tree Crowns are read from the cloud's own vegetation returns (one closed mesh per cluster, for the Tree component); Trees, Barriers and Furniture are for looking at and for a render (round trees; with Roads on, OpenStreetMap fences, walls, hedges and street furniture); Layer Outlines, Layer Names, Layer Roughness and Flatten are OpenStreetMap land cover (ODbL) with its Davenport z0, in the footprints' frame — wire them into the City Surface inputs of the same names. Rivers, streams and canals mapped as lines come with them as water ribbons (the OpenStreetMap width tag, else river 20 m, canal 8 m, stream 3 m).

docs.title: Input
docs.text: Name Nickname Description Type Latitude Lat Site centre latitude (WGS84, degrees). Number Longitude Lon Site centre longitude (WGS84, degrees). Number Size Edge of the square the building footprints cover [m]. Number Terrain Size TSize Edge of the square the point cloud — the terrain — and the Domain cover [m]: make it cover the whole CFD domain floor. At least Size. Optional; 0 or unset = 2 x Size. Number Source Where the LiDAR comes from. Auto: AHN inside the Netherlands, swissSURFACE3D, Bavaria, IGN LiDAR HD, Scotland's National LiDAR Programme, Estonia, Denmark, Slovenia, Saxony, Luxembourg, Brussels, Navarra or Spain's PNOA where the site lies in one, else USGS 3DEP (its newest project over the site). Browse… picks one dataset: "3DEP " reads that project, "AHN " reads AHN. NOAA Digital Coast is asked for by name, never by Auto: county and city surveys on the US coasts and the Great Lakes, often newer and denser than 3DEP and with a building class ("NOAA " reads one dataset). Or type an http(s) URL of any LAS/LAZ file (metric coordinates): it is downloaded once into the cache and cropped around Cloud Centre. Or the full path of a LAS/LAZ (or x y z [class] text) file on this machine — your own survey: it is read in place and cropped the same way; press Re-run after replacing the file. Text Cache Folder Cache Where downloads are kept (default Eddy3D/LidarCache in the local app data folder: ~/Library/Application Support on macOS, %LOCALAPPDATA% on Windows). An AHN sheet is ~5 GB. Text Cloud Centre Centre URL or local file source only: the site centre in the FILE's coordinates (metres — UTM, a national grid), i.e. where Latitude/Longitude lie in the file. Points are returned relative to it. Point Roads Also fetch OpenStreetMap roads, paved surfaces and footpaths (highway centrelines buffered by their width or lane count, area:highway, car parks, paved plazas; footways and sidewalks, paths, cycleways and steps, 1.5-2.5 m where untagged) as three more Layer Outlines layers, 'roads', 'paved' and 'paths', that City Surface carries as their own triangle groups following the terrain. A path loses the ground a road or a paved area holds. Also one more query for the street's own objects — fences, walls and hedges (Barriers), benches, bus stops, hydrants and picnic tables (Furniture) — as simple solids on the ground. Boolean Ring Size Ring Edge of a larger square [m] filled with GEDTM30 ground (OpenGeoHub, 30 m, CC BY 4.0) outside the LiDAR terrain square, so the CFD domain floor can reach further than the tiles: the offset between the two models is measured at the seam (median over a band just inside the LiDAR edge) and the join is blended over that band. The Domain becomes this square. Must be larger than Terrain Size, at most 20000 m. Optional; 0 or unset = no ring. Number Run Fetch. Resets when the run starts; a wired toggle held true re-runs when the inputs change. Boolean

docs.title: Output
docs.text: Name Nickname Description Type Point Cloud Cloud The site's points as a LAS file in local metres: City Surface's Point Cloud. Text Footprints Bldg Building footprints in local metres: City Surface's Footprints. Curve Roof Hints Hints OpenStreetMap roof hints per footprint, aligned with Footprints — 'gable;4;90;across' (shape; roof height m; direction °; across), empty when untagged: City Surface's Roof Hints. Used only where the LiDAR has too few roof points to fit a roof. Text Domain The terrain square (Terrain Size, or Ring Size when a ring is on): City Surface's Domain. Curve Trees The trees as individual round crowns on short trunks, ONE mesh over Terrain Size: from the cloud's own vegetation returns where it classifies any, else from the satellite canopy map (Meta/WRI CHM v2, 1 m, CC BY 4.0; most 3DEP projects classify none). 3 m and taller, none inside a footprint, at most the 20,000 tallest. For looking at and for a render, not a solver: Tree Crowns are the porous zones the Tree component takes. The Report says where they came from. Mesh Tree Crowns Crowns Tree crowns from the cloud's own vegetation returns (classes 3-5; AHN's unclassified points beside its buildings), one closed mesh per cluster of 4 m columns from 0.41 x tree height to the top, none inside a footprint, over Size — the satellite canopy rules Site Context uses. Plug into the Tree component's Geometry, one Tree per crown. Mesh Layer Outlines Layer OpenStreetMap land-cover outlines over Terrain Size (water, grass, forest, built-up…), in the footprints' frame, smallest first so a pond in a park keeps its own class. City Surface's Layer Outlines. Curve Layer Names Names The Davenport class of each Layer Outlines curve (water, smooth, open, roughly_open, rough, very_rough, closed): City Surface's Layer Names. Text Layer Kinds Kinds What the ground of each Layer Outlines curve IS: water, sand, rock, grass, park, pitch, scrub, farmland, orchard, bare_soil, residential, industrial, forest, garden, and roads, paved, paths. Every kind lies inside one Davenport class, so Layer Roughness stays right for it. Wire it to the Layer Names input of City Surface INSTEAD of Layer Names to split and colour its layers by what the ground is rather than by roughness class (a result saved before this output holds the class names). Text Layer Roughness z0 Aerodynamic roughness length z0 [m] of each Layer Outlines curve (Davenport-Wieringa): City Surface's Layer Roughness. Number Flatten Flat True for a lake or pond: City Surface's Flatten, so it is one level. River and stream ribbons are false, they follow the ground. Boolean Barriers Fences, walls, retaining walls, hedges and city walls (OpenStreetMap barrier=*, ODbL) as ONE mesh of thin boxes, one per 2 m of line, standing on the ground under them at the height tagged or the kind's usual one. Needs Roads on. Over Terrain Size; the 20,000 boxes nearest the centre at most. For looking at and for a render, not a solver. The Report says what was found. Mesh Furniture Benches, bus stops, hydrants and picnic tables (OpenStreetMap, ODbL) as ONE mesh of a few boxes each, standing on the ground. Needs Roads on. Axis-aligned (OpenStreetMap gives a node no heading); the 5,000 nearest the centre at most. For looking at and for a render, not a solver. Mesh Frame How local metres relate to the world (RD New minus the centre, or the Eddy3D site frame). Text Report Sources (with licences), counts and notes. Text Origin Which dataset each layer came from (layer, features, dataset with licence): wire it into Site Report's Results for the Origin table. Generic Data

docs.title: Live Residuals - [source code]
docs.text: Draws a case's residual convergence directly on the Grasshopper canvas, with lightweight timed updates. Wire the case and toggle 'Live' to monitor a running simulation without an external plotter window. When a warm-up ramp is enabled the solver restarts mid-run and writes a separate residual file per phase; all phases are stitched into one continuous curve so you see the full history (warm-up + main), not just the latest phase. An Outdoor+ (UMF) case solves its air region to convergence inside each time step, so its curve counts fluid iterations and the strip reads 'step 3/24 · iter 51'.

docs.title: Input
docs.text: Name Nickname Description Type Case Case to monitor: a wind case (from the wind case component or Load Wind Case), an Outdoor+ case or an indoor case. Generic Data Live Set to true to enable timed live updates. Boolean

docs.title: Output
docs.text: Name Nickname Description Type File F Residuals file being monitored. Text

docs.title: Live Wind Tunnel - [source code]
docs.text: Sketch a site against the wind: a 2D lattice-Boltzmann wind tunnel that runs continuously and paints the flow into the viewport while you move buildings and probes. Nothing restarts when geometry moves. For an urban block, cut the buildings at pedestrian height (Cut Height ≈ 1.75 m) and wire the ABL Flow the wind studies use into ABL: the tunnel then runs in that profile's speed at the cut, in its first wind direction. A SKETCH tool: the site is a section through infinitely tall buildings (no flow over or under anything, no buoyancy), and the solver's viscosity floor runs it at a far lower Reynolds number than real air. Compare variants of a site layout with it, with Mean on (a single frame of a wake is gusty); take numbers you report from an OpenFOAM or LBM Case run.

docs.title: Input
docs.text: Name Nickname Description Type Context The surroundings that stay put: terrain, neighbouring buildings, walls, fences. Closed curves are filled, open curves are walls drawn as lines; Breps, extrusions and meshes are cut at Cut Height. A terrain (an open mesh that faces up) is the GROUND instead: it is not cut, every building is cut at Cut Height above its own base, and the flow is drawn at Cut Height above the terrain. Branches are flattened: the site is one scene. Geometry Buildings The buildings (or canopies, signs, pavilions) whose wind load you want. Each gets a live force arrow, and the Force and Cd outputs follow their order. Same geometry rules as Context. Geometry Probes Pts Points to read the flow at (speed, pressure, vorticity), labelled live in the viewport. Point Wind Speed Speed Inflow speed, m/s. Number Wind Direction Dir Direction the wind blows TOWARDS; only its horizontal part counts. Vector Cell Size Cell Lattice spacing in m. 0 = auto: about 120,000 cells, which steps at an interactive rate on a laptop CPU. Each halving quadruples the work. Number Cut Height Cut Height above the ground the buildings stand on at which Breps and meshes are cut into the 2D site section, m. With a terrain mesh in Context it is above the LOCAL terrain (each building from its own base, the flow drawn that high over the terrain); without, above the highest base among Context and Buildings. Pedestrian level (about 1.75 m) for an urban block; with ABL wired it is also the height the wind profile is read at. Number View What the viewport shows: Smoke (dye streaming in from the inflow faces), Speed, Pressure (gauge, against the outflow), Vorticity, or LIC (speed under a line integral convolution of sparse noise: thin white strands gliding along the flow, a picture of the recent pathlines). With Mean on, Smoke, Speed, Pressure, Vorticity and the LIC's colours and strands show their time-mean; compare layouts that way, a single frame of a wake is gusty. Text Live Run the tunnel. Off pauses it and keeps the flow; right-click → Restart flow starts it from rest. Boolean ABL Optional ABL Flow, the component the wind studies and LBM Case take. Wired, it replaces Wind Speed and Wind Direction: the inflow is the log-law profile's speed at Cut Height, blowing in the ABL's first wind direction. The tunnel is 2D, so it carries that one speed; the profile's gradient up the buildings is not modelled. Generic Data Average Avg Time-mean window in simulated seconds, for the Mean toggle. 0 = auto: ten flow-throughs of the site (its larger side over the wind speed). The mean starts once the flow has developed and restarts when the geometry or the wind direction changes or Mean is switched on; Status says how full it is. Number Engine Eng Where the lattice steps. Auto: the OpenCL GPU when one answers, else the CPU with a remark. GPU: the GPU, and a fallback to the CPU is reported loud, never silent. CPU: every core but one. Switching engines restarts the flow; the Status output names the engine that runs. Text Mean Show and output time-means instead of the instantaneous frame: Speed, Pressure and Vorticity averaged over the Average window; the Smoke view shows the time-mean concentration. The window fills from the moment Mean is switched on; the banner says how full it is. Boolean Forces Draw each building's wind-load arrow and label in the viewport. Off by default; the Force and Cd outputs are always computed. Boolean Tunnel Optional: the wind tunnel itself, as a rectangle, box or surface (its plan footprint). The flow is solved over exactly this area and it stays put while Context and Buildings change, so draw it large enough to hold the wake: wind enters on the upwind face and leaves on the downwind one. Unwired, the tunnel is sized around the geometry (three times its larger side). Geometry

docs.title: Output
docs.text: Name Nickname Description Type Field The tunnel's current frame as a vertex-coloured mesh in the selected View (bake to keep it). Mesh Speed V Speed at each probe, m/s (empty inside a wall); the time-mean with Mean on. Number Pressure P Gauge pressure at each probe, Pa; the time-mean with Mean on. Number Vorticity W Vorticity at each probe, 1/s (positive = anticlockwise); the time-mean with Mean on. Number Force F Wind load on each building per metre of height, N/m (the site is a section). Vector Cd Drag coefficient of each building: drag / (0.5 rho U² frontal width). Number Status S Lattice, speed and how far the run is from real air. Text

(2026), SSRN preprint 6401886, doi:10.2139/ssrn.6401886.

docs.title: MRT - [source code]
docs.text: Mean radiant temperature at each sensor, hour by hour. MRT = shortwave + longwave. SHORTWAVE — what the sensor absorbs from sun and sky. Either a direct raycast (default, pure C#) or the Radiance DDS chain (MRT Settings -> Radiance Reflections), which adds diffuse sky and interreflection off the surroundings. Radiance returns annual total and direct illuminance per sensor, which are mapped onto the probes' shortwave series. LONGWAVE — what the sensor exchanges with everything around it, weighted by view factors traced from each sensor against the scene and the sky dome. SURFACE TEMPERATURES come from ENERGYPLUS, not Radiance — Radiance is a light transport engine and computes no temperatures at all. With MRT Settings -> EnergyPlus Surfaces on, Eddy3D builds an epJSON from the polygons that actually matter to the sensors (those inside the cumulative view-factor percentile and above the small-face cutoff; everything else is demoted to a shading surface), runs EnergyPlus against the EPW, and maps the surface-specific temperatures out of the ESO back onto the geometry. With it off, every surrounding surface is simply assumed to sit at air temperature. SKY TEMPERATURE is always Clark-Allen from dew point, dry bulb, opaque cloud cover and relative humidity — it needs no engine. Method: Dogan, Kastner & Mermelstein (2021), Building and Environment 196:107762, doi:10.1016/j.buildenv.2021.107762; Kastner & Dogan (2022), Building and Environment 212:108639, doi:10.1016/j.buildenv.2021.108639.

docs.title: Input
docs.text: Name Nickname Description Type Working Directory Dir Root for everything this run writes. Used for the Radiance DDS run (only when reflections/diffuse radiation is enabled) and, with a Project, as its parent folder. Text Project Optional project name. This run's working files and result cache live under // instead of being mixed in with every other study — so one project's results can be found, copied or cleared on their own. Spaces and characters a folder name cannot hold are replaced (container mounts reject spaces). Leave it blank and a friendly name is generated the same way a wind case's is (e.g. "swift-otter-fjord-lantern"). It is saved with the document, so re-running writes to the same folder — and a wind case in the same file shares the name, so the two studies sit in same-named folders under their own roots. Text Surfaces S Tagged radiation surfaces (MRT Surface). Branches are flattened — everything wired here forms one scene. Generic Data Sensors P Sensor probes (MRT Sensors). Branches are flattened. Generic Data EPW W Path to the EPW weather file. Text Settings C MRT settings (optional). Leave unconnected for the fast pure-C# path — direct-raycast shortwave, ambient surface temperatures, no external engine. Connecting MRT Settings turns on the high-fidelity Radiance and EnergyPlus engines, which its own defaults enable and which take considerably longer. Generic Data Engine Run Radiance/EnergyPlus natively or via the bundled radiance-energyplus container image (Podman or Docker). Only relevant when MRT Settings enables Radiance Reflections or EnergyPlus Surfaces. Text Compute Comp Who runs the view-factor geometry and the per-hour longwave accumulation. Auto: the OpenCL GPU when one answers, else the CPU; a fallback is reported in the log and as a warning. CPU: the parallel loops. GPU: refuse to run silently on the CPU. Same answer either way. A GPU solve leaves the MRT field on the device, where UTCI (Simulation) reads it in place when Result is wired in. Text Run R Run the MRT analysis. Boolean

docs.title: Output
docs.text: Name Nickname Description Type Sky Dome D The generated sky dome, shaded from a deep zenith to a pale horizon as vertex colours. Cosmetic — it carries no result. EMPTY unless "Show sky dome" is enabled in the right-click menu: the dome encloses the whole model, so it is off by default and is not built at all while off. Mesh Probes X Solved probes (for UTCI component). Generic Data Result R The whole solved MRT field as ONE item — every probe's full year. Feed it to Deconstruct MRT for probe-specific statistics or a chosen hour's tree, and to UTCI (Simulation), which reads it without any tree being built. Generic Data

docs.title: MRT Dataset Curator - [source code]
docs.text: Export the solved MRT field as a machine-learning dataset: one row per sensor per hour with spatial features, hourly climate drivers and the MRT/UTCI targets.

docs.title: Input

Generic Data Buildings B Building Breps or meshes, used for the signed-distance and roof-height features. Leave unconnected to write those columns as NaN. Geometry UTCI U Optional UTCI tree from the UTCI (Simulation) component, {hour}(probes) or {probe}(hours). Branch order must match the Probes list. Unconnected writes NaN. Number EPW W Path to the EPW weather file — supplies the hourly climate columns (DNI, DHI, GHI, dry-bulb, RH, wind, sun position). Unconnected writes those columns as NaN. Text Folder F Output folder for the CSV parts. Created if it does not exist. Text Name N File-name stem; parts are written as {Name}_part0001.csv. Defaults to the folder name. Text Ground Level G Datum the relative height and roof height are measured from. Defaults to the lowest sensor. Pin it explicitly when curating several cases into one dataset, or the datum shifts with the sensor grid and the height features stop being comparable. Number Rows per File RPF Soft cap on data rows per CSV part (default 2,000,000). An hour is never split across parts, so a case with more sensors than this writes one hour per part. Integer Run R Write the dataset. Boolean

docs.text: Create comfort sensor probes from meshes (one probe per face center, facing the face normal) and/or points (facing corresponding Normals), mixed freely on one input.

Geometry Normal N Sensor normals for POINT inputs: one vector per point (for example, Vectors from Brep Grid Points), or one vector shared by every point. Default world Z. Mesh probes always face their face normal. Vector Height Offsets every sensor along its own normal by this many meters. Point sensors use their corresponding Normal input; mesh sensors use their face normal. Default 1.1 m places upward-facing ground sensors at pedestrian body height. Number

docs.title: MRT Settings - [source code]
docs.text: Configuration for the MRT + UTCI analysis. Method: Bourgeois et al. (2008), Building Research & Information 36(1):68-82, doi:10.1080/09613210701446325; Subramaniam (2017), Lawrence Berkeley National Laboratory, tutorial (Nov 2017 revision) Ch. 2, App. B, https://www.radiance-online.org/learning/tutorials/matrix-based-methods.

docs.title: Input
docs.text: Name Nickname Description Type Small Face Cutoff F Faces below this area (m²) are ignored by the thermal model. Number Radiance Reflections Rad High-fidelity shortwave via the Radiance DDS chain (true, default) vs the pure-C# raycast (false). Requires a Radiance install (or the containerized engine). Boolean EnergyPlus Surfaces EP Where the SURROUNDING surfaces' temperatures come from, which is what drives the longwave half of MRT. true (default): EnergyPlus. Eddy3D builds an epJSON from the polygons that matter to the sensors — those inside the cumulative view-factor percentile and above the Small Face Cutoff, with the rest demoted to shading surfaces — runs E+ against the EPW, and maps the surface-specific temperatures out of the ESO back onto the geometry. false: every surface is assumed to sit at air temperature. Note this is EnergyPlus, not Radiance: Radiance transports light and computes no temperatures. Requires an EnergyPlus install (or the containerized engine on the MRT component); a missing engine throws rather than silently falling back to ambient. Boolean Engine Timeout T Wall-clock cap in minutes for each external engine run (Radiance DDS, EnergyPlus). Raise for large urban scenes. Integer Radiance Quality Q Accuracy of the Radiance shortwave chain (ambient bounces and sampling). 0 Draft: sky and sun only, no interreflection — about 10% off Reference [-ab 1 -ad 512 -lw 0.0005 (sun -ad 256)] 1 Fast: one reflection, for iterating — about 4% off [-ab 2 -ad 1024 -lw 0.00025 (sun -ad 256)] 2 Standard: the historical default — about 2% off [-ab 3 -ad 2000 -lw 0.0001 (sun -ad 256)] 3 Accurate: street-canyon interreflection converging — about 1.4% off [-ab 5 -ad 4096 -lw 0.00006 (sun -ad 256)] 4 High: deep canyons and high-albedo facades — about 0.9% off [-ab 8 -ad 8192 -lw 0.00003 (sun -ad 512)] 5 Reference: validation runs — the yardstick the others are measured against [-ab 12 -ad 10000 -lw 0.000025 (sun -ad 1024)] Percentages are the measured departure from Reference on a triangulated 73k-polygon neighborhood. Total runtime barely moves between levels (1.10-1.14x end to end): the flags do scale the ray tracing 3.6x, but that is only 4-15% of the chain — the rest is the annual sky matrices. So choose on accuracy. Standard is the default and reproduces the flags used before this input existed. Only applies when Radiance Reflections is on. Text Parallelize Par How many processes the Radiance chain spreads its sensors over. Auto (default) decides from the chain. With Fast Matrices on (the default) the sun term is finished on the host and the container's multiplies are binary and quick, so Auto stays at ONE process: measured at 4,500 and 14,600 sensors, splitting changed the run time by less than its run-to-run noise. With Fast Matrices off (the ASCII chain), or with tree crowns (their sun multiply stays in the container), the annual multiplies (dctimestep + rmtxop) are most of the run at thousands of sensors and neither program has a threading flag, so Auto splits the sensors over up to the machine's physical cores minus two, never below 500 sensors a block — 4,500 ASCII sensors took 220 s in one process and 117 s in nine. Off is always one process; 2, 4, 8 or 16 processes are honoured as given, which is also the way to cap a shared machine. This never changes the answer: every sensor is traced by identical commands against identical octrees and sky matrices; only which file it was listed in differs. Only applies when Radiance Reflections is on. Text Run Period HOY Optional hours of the year (1-8760, e.g. from the HOY component) the study is about. EnergyPlus then simulates only the days spanning them, plus 3 lead-in days, instead of the whole year — its cost is close to linear in simulated hours, so a heat-wave week runs many times faster. The MRT result is still 8760 hours: outside the period the surrounding surfaces are assumed to sit at air temperature, exactly as with EnergyPlus Surfaces off, so read results only for the hours given here. A selection that wraps the new year runs (nearly) the whole year. Empty (default) = full year. Only applies when EnergyPlus Surfaces is on. The Radiance chain works on annual sky matrices and is not shortened by this. Integer Fast Matrices Fast true (default): the Radiance chain moves its annual matrices as binary files and the sun term is finished as a sparse product on the host — several times quicker on large sensor grids, a quarter of the disk, and free of the three-digit rounding ASCII sky matrices carry (up to 0.5 % of the beam in an hour). false: the ASCII chain Eddy3D shipped before this input existed, kept as the control and the way back. For Two-Phase DDS the two agree to float rounding apart from that rounding. Two-Phase (preview) reads its beam straight from the sampled ray-traced coefficients, which the ASCII chain does not reproduce from run to run (about 0.7 % of the annual total, and more in single hours); the binary chain does. Only applies when Radiance Reflections is on. Boolean Shortwave Method Meth Which Two-Phase (daylight-coefficient) method the Radiance chain runs. Two-Phase DDS (default): the sun is traced separately, one source per fine sky bin (Bourgeois, Reinhart and Ward 2008), so shadows have close to the sun's own edges. Two-Phase (preview): the sun is read off the 145-patch sky, spread over the four patches nearest it, so shadow edges are blurred by several degrees and hourly beam and dMRT at sun altitudes below about 8 degrees are approximate. It skips the sun trace: about twice as quick on a grid of a few hundred sensors or more (five times on a handful). Reflected and diffuse light are the same; the annual total stayed within 2-3 % of Two-Phase DDS on the test cube and can differ more in a street canyon. For choosing a layout, not for a result. Scenes with tree crowns always run Two-Phase DDS. Only applies when Radiance Reflections is on. Text Sun Resolution Sun How finely the sky is divided for the traced sun of Two-Phase DDS (the Reinhart subdivision). MF:4 (default): 2,305 suns, bins about 3 degrees across. MF:6: 5,185 suns, about 2 degrees: the traced sun lands closer to the real one (the hourly error of the beam against an exact solar position fell by about a fifth in the check this setting was added with), for about twice the sun-coefficient trace and twice the disk of the transfer matrix. Ignored by Two-Phase (preview) and by scenes with tree crowns. Only applies when Radiance Reflections is on. Text

docs.text: Name Nickname Description Type Settings S MRT settings for the MRT component. Generic Data

docs.title: MRT Solve - [source code]
docs.text: Solves MRT on a prepared VF Model: shortwave (direct raycast, or Radiance DDS when MRT Settings enables reflections) + view-factor longwave. Wire the VF Model straight from MRT View Factors for ambient/FFT surface temperatures, or through SurfaceTemp (EnergyPlus) for E+ temperatures. Result feeds Deconstruct MRT and UTCI. Method: Dogan, Kastner & Mermelstein (2021), Building and Environment 196:107762, doi:10.1016/j.buildenv.2021.107762; Kastner & Dogan (2022), Building and Environment 212:108639, doi:10.1016/j.buildenv.2021.108639.

docs.title: Input
docs.text: Name Nickname Description Type Working Directory Dir Folder the Radiance case is written to. Only needed when MRT Settings enables Radiance Reflections. Text VF Model VF Solved model from MRT View Factors, optionally enriched by SurfaceTemp (EnergyPlus). Generic Data EPW W Path to the EPW weather file. Text Settings C Optional MRT Settings. Unconnected = fast pure-C# path (raycast shortwave). Generic Data Engine Run Radiance natively or via the bundled container image. Only relevant when MRT Settings enables Radiance Reflections. Text Compute Comp Who runs the view-factor-weighted longwave accumulation (probes x polygons x 8760 h). Auto: the OpenCL GPU when one answers, else the CPU; a fallback is reported in the log and as a warning. CPU: the parallel loop. GPU: refuse to run silently on the CPU. The GPU's rows are bit-identical to the CPU's. A model with tree crowns always runs on the CPU. Text Run R Solve MRT. Boolean

docs.title: Output
docs.text: Name Nickname Description Type Probes X Solved probes (for UTCI component). Generic Data Result R The complete MRT solve as one item — feed to Deconstruct MRT and UTCI. Generic Data Log The run's full log, one line per item — stages, sizes, engine choice, timings. Text

docs.title: MRT Surface - [source code]
docs.text: Tags Breps or Meshes as a radiation surface for an MRT analysis. Breps are meshed at Patch Size; Meshes are used face-for-face as given. Tree surfaces are tree CROWNS that transmit part of the radiation (SOLWEIG canopy, Lindberg & Grimmond 2011: 3 % of the beam in leaf, 50 % out of leaf, leaf season from the site latitude, leaves at air temperature for longwave) unless Tree Settings says otherwise; model them as closed crown volumes. Documents saved before canopy transmittance keep their opaque crowns (right-click).

docs.title: Input
docs.text: Name Nickname Description Type Geometry G Surface geometry: Breps (meshed at Patch Size) or Meshes (used as given — their faces ARE the view-factor patches, so refine coarse meshes upstream). Geometry Type T Surface type. Drives the default reflectance, the EnergyPlus construction, and the type-specific view-factor totals. Text Simulated S True if the surface temperature is solved; false treats it as ambient. Boolean Patch Size P Target mesh patch edge length (m) for view-factor resolution. Number Material Mat Optional material from an Outdoor+ Building / Terrain Material component or an MRT Surface / Vegetation / Tree Settings component. UMF thermal properties are reused directly; MRT optical properties override the default reflectance. Generic Data Temperature Tsrf Optional surface temperature (°C) for longwave MRT. Connect SurfaceTemp directly: both {hour}(surface points) and {surface point}(hours) trees are accepted. A single value or one shared 8760-hour series is also supported. Overrides Simulated. Number Temperature Points TempPts Optional points used to calculate SurfaceTemp. When their count differs from the MRT mesh polygon count, each polygon uses its nearest temperature sample. Point

docs.title: Output
docs.text: Name Nickname Description Type Surface S Tagged radiation surface for the MRT component. Generic Data Mesh M The meshed surface (preview). Mesh

docs.title: MRT View Factors - [source code]
docs.text: Assembles tagged surfaces + sensors into a radiation model, builds the sky dome, and solves probe-to-polygon view factors. Feed the VF Model to SurfaceTemp (EnergyPlus) and/or MRT Solve. The sweep is the expensive part of an MRT run — solving it once here lets the downstream stages re-run without repeating it. Method: Dogan, Kastner & Mermelstein (2021), Building and Environment 196:107762, doi:10.1016/j.buildenv.2021.107762.

docs.title: Input
docs.text: Name Nickname Description Type Surfaces S Tagged radiation surfaces (MRT Surface). Branches are flattened — everything wired here forms one scene. Generic Data Sensors P Sensor probes (MRT Sensors). Branches are flattened. Generic Data Sky Dome Subdivisions SkyDiv Resolution of the internal MRT sky hemisphere, as a SUBDIVISION LEVEL: the dome has 6 x 4^level faces, half of them above the horizon. Higher levels smooth the view factors but cost time on every probe; 5 (3072 patches) is ample for MRT. Text Fidelity Fid How much of the occlusion raycasting to spend. Balanced (default): polygons whose view factor is below 5e-5 are assumed visible instead of raycast — each such polygon can shift the normalized result by less than that, and the sweep runs several times faster. Fast: same idea at 2e-4, and the sky dome is capped at 768 patches (level 4) — the dome only refines the probe-specific sky view fraction, which 768 patches already pin to ±0.02 of the 3072-patch answer. Quick iteration on big models. Reference: every contribution above the 1e-5 floor is raycast (the original behavior). Use for the final run when publishing numbers. Sky patches are always raycast at every fidelity. Text Engine Eng Who does the heavy lifting of the sweep: the occlusion rays (and the raycast shortwave in MRT Solve) AND the view-factor geometry of every probe x polygon pair (the cos·area/r² term) ahead of them. Auto: rays on Embree when its natives load, else the OpenCL GPU when a device answers, else the managed BVH; geometry on the GPU when one answers, else the CPU. GPU: rays and geometry on the OpenCL GPU even where Embree loads, which pays off on the sweep's large ray batches; a fallback to the CPU is reported in the log and as a warning, never silent. Embree: Embree rays, geometry on the CPU. BVH: the managed BVH and CPU geometry — the same answer on every machine. GPU geometry is float; measured within 2e-6 per view factor of the CPU's at Reference fidelity. Text Run R Solve the view factors. Boolean

docs.title: Output
docs.text: Name Nickname Description Type VF Model VF The assembled radiation model with solved view factors. Feed to SurfaceTemp (EnergyPlus) and MRT Solve. Generic Data Sky Dome D The sky dome mesh (preview). Mesh Log The run's full log, one line per item — stages, sizes, engine choice, timings. Text

docs.title: Manual Inflow Profile - [source code]
docs.text: Define inflow boundary conditions from a manually entered vertical profile (z/zR, U/UR, k/UR^2) instead of the parametric ABL log-law. Writes fixedProfile inlet conditions for U, k and epsilon. epsilon is derived from the profile as epsilon(z) = Cmu^0.5 * k(z) * d(U)/dz.

docs.title: Input
docs.text: Name Nickname Description Type Wind Directions Dirs Wind directions as meteorological degrees (wind-from, clockwise from north, e.g. 0, 45, 90) or flow vectors. One solver case is created per direction; the profile magnitudes are rotated to each direction. Optional; default is flow toward +X. Generic Data Normalized Height (z/zR) z/zR List of normalized heights z/zR (z = height above ground, zR = boundary layer height). Number Normalized Velocity (U/UR) U/UR List of normalized streamwise velocities U/UR at each height (UR = reference velocity at zR). Number Normalized TKE (k/UR^2) k/UR^2 List of normalized turbulent kinetic energies k/UR^2 at each height. docs.title: Morph Settings - [source code]
docs.text: Engine settings for Morph Weather: the method (Future Weather Generator or the World Bank CCKP anomalies), climate products, spatial interpolation, uncertainty case and solar methods. Every value left empty stays on the Future Weather Generator's own default; the CCKP methods ignore the generator-only settings.

docs.title: Input
docs.text: Name Nickname Description Type Models M Climate products (GCMs for the CMIP6 Global build, GCM-RCM pairs for CORDEX) named as the distribution names them — see Morph Weather's Available output. Empty uses the distribution's full model set. Text Ensemble E Also produce the multi-model ensemble mean. This is the file most studies report. Boolean Interpolation I How the monthly climate signal is interpolated from the model grid to the site: IDW (inverse distance over four valid points), NP (nearest point), AVG4P (four-point mean), BI (bilinear), SCI/SGBI/STBI (structured-grid variants). Text Uncertainty U Which case of the model spread to take: CENTRAL, the sigma shifts, or the WARM_DRY / WARM_HUMID / HIGH_SOLAR / LOW_SOLAR corners. Text Sigma s Sigma multiplier for the sigma-based uncertainty variants. Number Winter Shift Ws Extra winter dry-bulb spread in K, on top of the morphed signal. 0 leaves it alone. Number Summer Shift Ss Extra summer dry-bulb spread in K, on top of the morphed signal. 0 leaves it alone. Number Decomposition D Solar decomposition model used to rebuild the direct/diffuse split, e.g. MULTIMODEL_CONSTRAINED_ENSEMBLE. Your jar's help lists the installed set. Text Illuminance L Illuminance model used to recompute the lux columns, e.g. PEREZ_1990. Text Present Day P Also write the present-day control file, processed through the same chain — the honest baseline to compare a future file against. Boolean Threads N Worker threads for the morphing engine. Empty or 0 leaves the count to the engine. Integer Method Which engine morphs the file. Future Weather Generator: the Java application you install (needs its jar). CCKP median / 10th / 90th percentile: the World Bank Climate Change Knowledge Portal's CMIP6 ensemble at 0.25° — monthly anomalies of temperature, humidity, wind, solar and longwave radiation read for the site's grid cell, applied to the file as monthly shifts and stretches. No key, no Java; pressure, cloud cover, wind direction and rain stay as in the present-day file. The percentiles are taken per variable and month, so the 10th and 90th are the ends of the model spread, not two coherent climates. Text

docs.title: Morph Weather - [source code]
docs.text: Morph a present-day EPW into future-climate EPWs with the Future Weather Generator (future-weather-generator.adai.pt), then feed the result to any Eddy3D workflow. Needs Java 17+ and the generator's .jar, which Eddy3D does not ship: download the distribution you need (CMIP6 Global, CORDEX-CMIP5 Europe, …) into ~/Eddy3D/FWG. The tool is licensed CC BY-NC-SA 4.0 — noncommercial use, attribution required. Alternatively set Morph Settings' Method to a CCKP entry: the World Bank Climate Change Knowledge Portal's CMIP6 ensemble (0.25°, no key, no Java, no jar) is read for the site's grid cell and applied to the file as monthly shifts and stretches.

docs.title: Noise Run - [source code]
docs.text: Road-traffic noise after CNOSSOS-EU (Directive 2015/996, 2021/1226 coefficients): the emission of every road and the propagation to every receiver — divergence, air absorption, the ground effect on the mean plane, diffraction over roofs and crests — summed per octave band and period into Lday, Levening, Lnight and Lden. Lden (L_den) is the day-evening-night level of the EU Environmental Noise Directive 2002/49/EC: the long-term A-weighted level in dB(A) over a whole day, with the 4 h evening counted +5 dB and the 8 h night +10 dB (the day is 12 h), so night and evening noise weigh more than their hours. PROTOTYPE LIMITS: homogeneous atmospheric conditions only (no favourable-propagation share, so distant levels run a little low); no facade reflections; no path around a corner (a receiver behind a block gets the over-the-roof path only, which reads low); one ground factor for the whole site; no rail, aircraft or industry. Not a compliance calculation. Method: CNOSSOS-EU, Commission Directive (EU) 2015/996 Annex II (road emission §2.2, propagation §2.5), coefficients per Delegated Directive (EU) 2021/1226, https://eur-lex.europa.eu/eli/dir/2015/996/oj — pinned against NoiseModelling (Université Gustave Eiffel) on the ISO/TR 17534-4 cases.

Generic Data Receivers The receiver set from Noise Receivers. Generic Data Buildings Bldgs Building solids or meshes: what blocks and diffracts the sound. Branches are flattened. Geometry Terrain Terrain meshes or surfaces. Flat at the lowest building base (z = 0 with no buildings) when unwired. Branches are flattened. Geometry Ground CNOSSOS ground factor of the whole site: hard (asphalt, paving, water — a city centre), mixed, or soft (grass, soil — a park). Soft ground lowers mid-frequency levels at distance; hard ground is the conservative choice. Text Cell Size Cell Raster cell of the scene heightfield, m. 5 m is a quick look on a large site; 1 m resolves ordinary buildings. A wall thinner than a cell is not seen. Number Engine Eng Auto: the OpenCL GPU when one answers, else the CPU. GPU: the GPU, and a fallback to the CPU is reported, never silent. CPU: every core. Same CNOSSOS terms either way; the GPU hands the rare section it cannot decide in single precision back to the CPU. Text Run Solve the map. Works as an inline button or as a wired toggle — with a wire held true, the run relaunches whenever the inputs change. Boolean

Text Case Wind case; plug into the Wind Run and post-processing components. Generic Data Domain Resolved simulation domain (box, or domain mesh for cylindrical cases). Generic Data Refinement Box Refine Refinement box derived from the case. Brep Buildings Bldgs Building meshes from the case. docs.title: PALM Case - [source code]
docs.text: Write the PALM-4U case: the static driver (terrain, buildings, tree canopies and the ground surface mosaic, rasterized onto the domain grid) and the _p3d namelist that runs it. Geometry inputs take trees of meshes/Breps; branches are flattened — everything wired belongs to ONE scene. Ground not covered by any input takes the Ground Cover class. The viewport shows the domain, its boundary conditions and the rasterized surface the solver will actually see.

docs.title: Input
docs.text: Name Nickname Description Type Case Name Case The case folder under Working Directory. Empty mints a session name shared by every PALM component on this document. Text Working Directory Dir The root the case folder sits under; empty uses ~/Eddy3D/PALM. Text Domain D The PALM Domain to rasterize onto. Generic Data Buildings B Building solids, roof surfaces or meshes; each item, and each separate piece of a joined mesh, becomes one building id. Branches are flattened. Geometry Trees Tr Tree crown volumes (closed meshes/Breps); each, and each separate piece of a joined mesh, becomes leaf area density between its bottom and top. Branches are flattened. Geometry Terrain T Terrain surface (mesh or Brep). Branches are flattened. Empty means flat ground. Geometry Vegetation V Ground painted as vegetation, using the Vegetation Type. Branches are flattened. Geometry Pavement P Ground painted as pavement (streets, plazas). Branches are flattened. Geometry Water W Ground painted as water. Branches are flattened. Geometry Land Cover LC PALM Land Cover patches (OSM). Painted below the explicit geometry above. Generic Data Building Type BT PALM building_type for every building: construction era and use drive the wall, roof and window properties the urban surface model applies. Text Vegetation Type VT Class for ground wired into Vegetation. Text Pavement Type PT Class for ground wired into Pavement. Text Water Type WT Class for ground wired into Water. Text Ground Cover G What UNCLAIMED ground becomes — always a vegetation class, because unpainted urban ground is far more often grass than asphalt; paint pavement, never assume it. Text Soil Type ST PALM soil_type under every vegetation and pavement cell — drives the soil column's heat and moisture transport. Text Leaf Area Density LAD Leaf area density written inside tree crowns (m² m⁻³). 1–2 is a typical broadleaf canopy. Number Settings S PALM Settings — duration, wind, temperature, outputs. Written into the _p3d beside the driver, so a settings change needs a re-Write before it can reach a run. Empty writes the defaults (2 h, 3 m/s westerly, comfort on). Generic Data Write Wr Rasterize and write the static driver and the _p3d namelist into the case's INPUT folder. Boolean Clear Cl Delete this case's PALM artifacts — the JOBS tree (driver, namelist, results, monitoring), the live-run tmp tree and the launch script. The case folder itself and anything else in it are left alone. Refused while a run looks active. Boolean

docs.title: Output
docs.text: Name Nickname Description Type Driver Dr The written case (driver path + namelist + contents summary). Feed to PALM Run. Generic Data Path P Where the driver was written. Text Report R What was rasterized: cell counts per class, terrain shift, the boundary conditions and the forcing, and anything skipped. Text Namelist Nl The _p3d this case writes, as text — the same string that goes to disk on Write. Text Domain Box Box The simulation domain as a box in model space. Box

docs.title: PALM Domain - [source code]
docs.text: Define the PALM-4U grid: cells, spacing and the site's latitude/longitude. The domain's lower-left corner sits at the Origin point in the Rhino model (world origin by default), with y pointing north. Feed the output to PALM Case and PALM Run.

docs.title: Input
docs.text: Name Nickname Description Type Latitude Lat Latitude of the domain's lower-left (south-west) corner, decimal degrees. Drives the sun position for radiation and comfort. Number Longitude Lon Longitude of the domain's lower-left corner, decimal degrees east. Number Cell Size dx Horizontal grid spacing in metres. PALM-4U urban runs use square cells (dx = dy); 2 m resolves streets and courtyards, 4–10 m a district. Number Cells X nx Number of cells across the domain in x (east). Integer Cells Y ny Number of cells across the domain in y (north). Integer Cells Z nz Number of vertical levels. The domain top should clear the tallest building by a factor of 3 or more. Integer Vertical Spacing dz Vertical grid spacing in metres. Empty follows Cell Size, which is what a street-resolving run wants. Number Origin O Rhino model point of the domain's lower-left corner. Default 0,0,0. Point

docs.title: Output
docs.text: Name Nickname Description Type Domain D The PALM domain. Feed to PALM Case, which rasterizes the scene onto it and writes the run. Generic Data Boundary B The domain footprint as a rectangle in model space — what the static driver will rasterize. Curve Summary S Grid, extent and anchor, one line each. Text

docs.title: Input

docs.title: Input
