docs.title: PALM Results - [source code]
docs.text: Read a PALM output field: one variable, one time frame, as values and a colored mesh over the domain. Variables and times available in the case are listed on every solve.

docs.title: Input
docs.text: Name Nickname Description Type Case Folder Dir The case folder — PALM Run's Case Folder output. Empty uses the document's session case. Text File F Which output file to read. Averaged fields are the ones a comfort map wants. Text Variable V The PALM variable to read — pick from the catalog, type any name, or check the Variables output for what the file actually offers. Empty picks the first biometeorology variable present, else the first variable. Text Frame T Time frame index; -1 is the last frame written so far. Integer Domain D The PALM Domain OR the Static Driver's Driver output, to place the mesh in model space. Unwired, the mesh sits at the world origin — the spacing always comes from the file itself. Generic Data

docs.title: Output
docs.text: Name Nickname Description Type Mesh M The field as a colored mesh at z = 0 (blue low to red high). Mesh Values Val The field row-major, south-west first — one value per mesh face. Number Variables Vars Every data variable the file carries. Text Times Ti The simulated seconds of each frame in the file. Number Info I File, variable, frame and range. Text

docs.title: PALM Run - [source code]
docs.text: Run PALM-4U. Writes a launch script into the case PALM Case wrote, then starts the published PALM container. The script and command are always shown, even before you run, so a failing run can be reproduced by hand.

docs.title: Input
docs.text: Name Nickname Description Type Driver Dr PALM Case's Driver output. It carries the case folder, the grid and the settings the case was written with — one wire, nothing to keep consistent. Generic Data Engine E Which backend runs PALM. Container (Docker or Podman) is the only backend in this release, on every platform. Text Image Img Container image. Auto uses the published Eddy3D PALM image matching this machine's architecture; pull it from the Eddy3D Setup window. A custom image can be typed or wired in. Text Run R Write the launch script and start the container against the case PALM Case wrote. Boolean

docs.title: Output
docs.text: Name Nickname Description Type Namelist Nl The _p3d this run will read, as it sits on disk. PALM Case writes it; empty means it is not there yet. Text Script Sc The generated run script. Text Command C The command that launches it, as it would be typed. Text Status St Engine, files, and what happened. Text Case Folder Out The resolved case folder. Feed to PALM Progress and PALM Results. Text

docs.title: PALM Settings - [source code]
docs.text: Steer the PALM-4U run: duration, wind, temperature and outputs. Forcing is idealized (constant wind, cyclic boundaries). Comfort switches on radiation and the biometeorology module, whose PET/UTCI/MRT maps are PALM-4U's point.

docs.title: Input
docs.text: Name Nickname Description Type Duration T Simulated hours after spin-up. Two hours settles a street-resolving flow field; a diurnal comfort study wants 24. Number Spinup Sp Wall and soil spin-up in hours before the atmosphere starts. 0.5 is a floor for surface temperatures worth reading. Number Output Interval Oi Minutes between outputs; also the averaging window for the _av fields. Number Wind Speed U Driving wind speed (m/s), applied as a constant geostrophic wind. Number Wind Direction Dir Meteorological wind direction in degrees (wind FROM; 270 = westerly). Number Air Temperature Ta Near-surface air temperature (°C). Number Humidity q Near-surface specific humidity (kg water per kg air). 0.008 is a mild mid-latitude day. Number Date Time Dt Simulation start, 'YYYY-MM-DD hhss +zz'. Drives the sun. Text Slice Height H Height above ground of the horizontal result slices (m). 2 m is pedestrian level. Number Output Variables Out PALM data_output names, one per item — pick from the catalog or type any name PALM knows. Empty uses the default set: pedestrian-level u/v/w/theta, surface temperature, and PET/UTCI/MRT when Comfort is on. Text Comfort C Run radiation and biometeorology (PET, UTCI, MRT maps). Off makes a plain LES — faster, wind only. Boolean Cores N MPI ranks for the run. Empty picks them automatically at launch: the container daemon's CPU count (on macOS and Docker Desktop the VM's allotment is the real ceiling), capped so every rank owns a worthwhile patch of the grid. Integer

docs.title: Output
docs.text: Name Nickname Description Type Settings S The run settings. Feed to PALM Run. Generic Data Summary Su What will run, one line each. Text

docs.title: PET (Simulation) - [source code]
docs.text: Compute annual probe-specific PET (Höppe) from simulation outputs: MRT and wind-speed data trees, plus air temperature, relative humidity and the person. Solves in the background; cancel from the right-click menu. For a single point, use "Thermal Comfort".

docs.title: Input
docs.text: Name Nickname Description Type MRT M The MRT component's Result (preferred), or a DataTree of annual MRT values — {probe}(8760) or {hour}(probes), both accepted. Generic Data Wind Speed V Wind speed as an AnnualWindField (the VAF component's Wind Speed output — fed by CFD probe vectors or the ML Wind Predictor alike), one spatial list (one value per probe, held for all hours), or a {probe}(hours) / {hour}(probes) tree. An AnnualWindField on a different grid than the MRT sensors is resampled by nearest neighbor when both carry points. PET takes the wind AT the body, so pedestrian-height speeds are used as they are (UTCI lifts them to 10 m; PET does not). Defaults to calm (0.5 m/s) when unconnected. Generic Data Air Temperature T Annual hourly ambient air temperature (8760 values, °C). Number Relative Humidity RH Annual hourly relative humidity (8760 values, %). Number Pressure Press Air pressure [hPa]. Number Age Age [years]. Integer Sex Male, Female, or Average. Text Height Body height [m]. Number Weight Body weight [kg]. Number Body Position Pos Standing, Sitting, or Crouching. Text Clothing Insulation Icl Clothing insulation [clo]. Number Metabolic Rate MET Metabolic rate [W]. Number Climate Type Climate Assessment scale: Temperate (Matzarakis & Mayer) or Humid (Lin & Matzarakis, shifted +8..+10 °C). Changes only how PET is classified as comfortable, never the PET value. Text Transpose Orientation of the PET tree output. Hours × Probes (default): one branch per hour, each holding every probe's value. Probes × Hours: one branch per probe, each holding that probe's year. Text Run R Start the annual PET solve. Boolean

docs.title: Output
docs.text: Name Nickname Description Type PET PET data tree. Default: {hour}(probes). With Transpose off: {probe}(hours). Only built while this output is WIRED: for a few thousand probes the full year is tens of millions of values on the canvas, and constructing them — not the PET model — is the wait. Prefer the Result output with Deconstruct UTCI. Number Comfort Hours H No-thermal-stress hours per probe on the chosen climate's PET scale. Integer Comfort % % Comfort percentage per probe. Number Result The complete annual PET solve as ONE item — feed to Deconstruct UTCI for statistics, comfort hours/% over any hour selection, or straight into the Thermal Comfort Legend for a map (its PET bands follow the Climate Type). Carries the MRT probes' positions when the MRT input was a Result. Generic Data

docs.title: Input

docs.title: Output
docs.text: Name Nickname Description Type Log Summary Summary Summary of log parsing results. Text Errors Errors found in log files. Text Warnings Warnings found in log files. Text

docs.title: Pedestrian Wind Comfort - [source code]
docs.text: Classifies pedestrian wind comfort per point from an annual hourly wind-speed series (the Wind Speed output of the Velocity Amplification Factors (VAF) component) against a comfort criterion (Lawson, Davenport, NEN8100). Returns the comfort category, class letter, and activity description for each point. Within about 1.5 building heights leeward of a building a steady-RANS comfort or safety verdict is OPTIMISTIC (too calm): on AIJ Cases A and B the solver reattaches at 1.3–1.5 H (Case B 3.27 H) against the tunnel's 0.38–0.75 H (Case B 1.88–2.62 H) and reads the 88 wake points at 0.30 U_H against the measured 0.451 (FB +0.29; above the roof +0.06). SST URANS and DES do not fix it (0.286 and 0.292 U_H).

docs.title: Input
docs.text: Name Nickname Description Type Wind Speed U Annual wind field from the Velocity Amplification Factors (VAF) component (its Wind Speed output): a single object holding every point's 8760-hour wind-speed series. Passed as an object so the millions of values skip the Grasshopper data tree. Generic Data Comfort Metric Metric Comfort criterion: Lawson General, Lawson LDDC, Lawson 2001, Davenport, NEN8100 Comfort, NEN8100 Safety, or Wellington (NZ; its safety class reads the 3-second gust); or a planning-authority preset — City Lawson (City of London 2019: worse of mean and GEM, comfort in the worst season, 15 m/s safety annually), Melbourne DDO10, Boston BPDA (effective gust = mean + 1.5σ), San Francisco §148 (equivalent wind speed) or Toronto (GEM, 06:00-23:00, worst season). The authority presets read the gust series — wire Gust Speed for a TKE-based gust. A wired integer 0-11 still selects by index. A Criteria object wired below overrides this pick. Text Color Scheme Scheme Categorical palette for the comfort classes: Classic (green through red, the standard wind-comfort plot), Colorblind Safe (Okabe-Ito derived), Muted (desaturated, for underlays), or City of London — the colour code the City of London Wind Microclimate Guidelines (2019) ask planning submissions to use: Frequent Sitting grey, Occasional Sitting blue, Standing green, Walking yellow, Uncomfortable and/or Unsafe red (so any red zone is unacceptable or unsafe). Made for the City Lawson criterion; on another one it is applied by class position, and the component says so. Text Size S Marker half-size in model units for the comfort mesh (one quad per point). Number Period Slice of the year to classify: Year (default), a season, or a single month. The exceedance criteria then apply to that period's hours only — winter comfort is usually worse than annual. Seasons are named by their months (Winter = Dec-Feb), so southern-hemisphere EPWs read unambiguously. Text Gust Speed Gust Optional annual gust field — the Gust Speed output of Velocity Amplification Factors (needs its TKE input). Read by gust-referenced classes only (Wellington's 20 m/s annual maximum 3-second gust). Without it those classes fall back to mean × Gust Factor. Generic Data Gust Factor G 3-second gust / hourly mean ratio used for gust-referenced classes when no Gust Speed field is wired. 1.85 is the ratio New Zealand planning practice writes down (Auckland Unitary Plan: gust equivalent mean = 3-s gust / 1.85), i.e. GEM at ~24% turbulence intensity with g = 3.5. Ignored when Gust Speed is wired. Number Criteria Optional criteria object from the Wind Comfort Criteria component — a jurisdiction's own class table. When wired it replaces the Comfort Metric pick. Generic Data Wind Climate Climate Optional long-term wind climate from the Wind Climate component. When wired, the classification is PROBABILISTIC: Wind Speed must then be VAF's Speed Ratios output (per-probe speed / inlet reference speed per direction), and P(U > u) = Σ p·exp(−(u/(r·c))^k) over the climate's sectors replaces the hour count — the City of London Annex A procedure, with no hourly series formed. Period may also read "Worst season" (comfort rows per season, safety rows annual). Gust-referenced classes use VAF's TKE-based gust ratios or the Gust Factor. Generic Data Engine Eng Engine for the annual classification sweep. Auto: the OpenCL GPU when one answers, else the CPU — a fallback is reported, never silent. GPU: the same exceedance tallies on the GPU (identical classes). CPU: every core. Text

docs.title: Output
docs.text: Name Nickname Description Type Comfort Rank Rank Comfort category number per point (1 = most comfortable; higher = worse). Integer Class Letter Letter Comfort class letter per point (A, B, ... ; S = unsafe). Text Comfort Class Class Comfort activity description per point (e.g. Sitting, Walking). Text Mesh M Comfort mesh: one colored quad per probe point, class-colored by the selected scheme. Needs points inside the Wind Speed object — wire the probe points into the VAF component's Points input. Mesh Colors C Class color per point, aligned with the input series — for coloring custom geometry. Colour Legend Colors LC One color per class of the selected metric, best-to-worst — pairs with Legend Labels for annotation. Colour Legend Labels LL One label per class of the selected metric ("A — Sitting" style), aligned with Legend Colors. Text

docs.title: Planting Suitability - [source code]
docs.text: Nursery-label planting suitability from a Sun Hours study: Sunny (6 h or more of direct sun a day), Part sun (4-6 h), Partial shade (2-4 h) or Shade (under 2 h) per point, flagged morning sun or afternoon sun when more than 70 % of it falls on one side of solar noon. Thresholds are editable: there is no accredited standard and some extension services draw the shade edge at 4 h. Method: Grenfell (2025), UC Master Gardeners of Placer County, University of California Agriculture and Natural Resources, https://ucanr.edu/site/uc-master-gardeners-placer-county/article/definitions-light-requirements.

docs.title: Input
docs.text: Name Nickname Description Type Morning Hours AM Direct-sun hours before solar noon at each point — Sun Hours' Morning Hours output. Number Afternoon Hours PM Direct-sun hours after solar noon at each point — Sun Hours' Afternoon Hours output. Number Sunny Hours Sun Direct sun at or above this is Sunny (full sun). Number Part Sun Hours Part At or above this, below Sunny Hours: Part sun. Number Partial Shade Hours PShade At or above this, below Part Sun Hours: Partial shade. Below it: Shade. Number Lopsided Fraction Lop Share of a point's direct sun that must fall on one side of solar noon before it is flagged morning sun or afternoon sun (strictly more than this; 0.5-1). Number

docs.title: Output
docs.text: Name Nickname Description Type Category Cat Per point: Sunny, Part sun, Partial shade or Shade, with ' · morning sun' or ' · afternoon sun' appended when the split is lopsided. Text Colors Col One colour per point by category — amber, yellow, leaf green, deep green from sun to shade — for a mesh or point preview. Colour Legend L One line per band with the thresholds in use, plus the timing rule. Text Summary S Points per category and per timing. Text

docs.title: Plot Residuals - [source code]
docs.text: Open the web-based residual plotter for a wind case's convergence history (one trace per direction).

docs.title: Input
docs.text: Name Nickname Description Type Case Wind case (from the wind case component or Load Wind Case). Generic Data Plot Set to true to open the residual plotter in your browser. Boolean

docs.title: Output
docs.text: None

docs.title: Pollutant Source - [source code]
docs.text: Define a pollutant emission source for the wind study: a closed volume (stack tip, traffic corridor box, exhaust vent) releasing a named species at a mass rate. Wire into the Eddy3D Case component's Sources input; the species is transported as a passive scalar with turbulent diffusivity (Sct) on every direction case, and the concentration field (kg/m3) is read back by probing the species name.

docs.title: Input
docs.text: Name Nickname Description Type Geometry Geo Closed mesh of the emitting volume, in metres. Thinner than the local mesh cells selects no cells — thicken it or refine around it. Mesh Species Field name of the emitted species — pick a common one from the dropdown or type any OpenFOAM word. Sources sharing a name solve as ONE concentration field; distinct names each add a transport solve per iteration. Text Rate kg/s Total emission of this source in kg/s. The transport is linear, so results rescale to any other rate without re-running. Number Schmidt Sct Turbulent Schmidt number of the species (default 0.7, standard for atmospheric dispersion). Lower spreads the plume faster. Number

docs.title: Output
docs.text: Name Nickname Description Type Source Src The source object for the Eddy3D Case component's Sources input. Generic Data

docs.title: Ponding Report - [source code]
docs.text: One row per puddle: where it is, how much water, how deep, when it peaked and how long it took to drain — against the capacity of the hollow it sits in, so an overflowing depression is visible as such.

docs.title: Input
docs.text: Name Nickname Description Type Result A run from Stormwater Run. Needs a Full run — a Fast one has no water in it, only the capacity of the hollows. Generic Data Minimum Depth MinDepth Depth in MILLIMETRES a depression must reach to be reported. 25 mm is about where a puddle stops being a wet patch. Number Minimum Volume MinVol Volume in m³ a depression must reach to be reported. Keeps a report about the site from being a report about its raster. Number CSV Path CSV Optional file path to write the table to. The folder must exist. Text Write Write the CSV to the path above. Boolean

docs.title: Output
docs.text: Name Nickname Description Type Locations Pts Deepest point of each pond, at the water surface. Point Volumes Vol Water held at peak (m³). Number Areas Area Wetted area at peak (m²). Number Depths Depth Peak depth (mm). Number Drain Times Drain Minutes until the pond fell below the reporting depth. Empty where it never did — which means the water has nowhere to go within the simulated period. Number Table The whole report as CSV text. Text

docs.title: Prediction Confidence - [source code]
docs.text: Score an ML wind prediction per point: red outside the model's training window, where a feature lies outside the training envelope, or where models disagree by more than 25 %; amber near the window edge, in the envelope's outer 10 %, or where models differ by more than 10 %; green otherwise. The envelope is measured from Dataset Curator CSVs or Verify Prediction logs — none is shipped for the bundled models, because none is published. ML screening prediction, not CFD: use it to compare options, then confirm anything that matters with a Wind Study (planning authorities do not accept surrogate results).

docs.title: Input
docs.text: Name Nickname Description Type Points The points the prediction was made at (absolute Z). Point Buildings Building geometry, to measure SDF / Bldg_height / Z_relative for the envelope test (as the predictor does). Geometry Boundary Conditions BC The study's boundary conditions (reference height for U/U_ref). Generic Data Pedestrian Level PedLevel Pedestrian mounting height [m], as given to the predictor. Number Envelope Training-envelope sources: Dataset Curator CSVs and/or Verify Prediction logs. Text Ensemble Optional: the same direction predicted by two or more models, one branch per model, one value per point. Number Edge Margin Margin Distance [m] from the training window's edge counted as 'near'. Number

docs.title: Output
docs.text: Name Nickname Description Type Level 0 green, 1 amber, 2 red, per point. Integer Reasons Why each point got its level. Text Colors Traffic-light colour per point. Colour Summary Counts per level and what was (and was not) checked. Text

docs.title: Probe - [source code]
docs.text: Sample fields at points on a solved case, post-hoc. With Run it writes a probes function and runs postProcess on the requested Time (latest by default), then reads the results; without Run it reads existing results. Works on a wind case (one sub-result per direction) or a loaded case.

docs.title: Input
docs.text: Name Nickname Description Type Case What to probe: a solved case (wind / loaded / UMF / indoor), or the Case output of LBM Case / LBM Run for either lattice-Boltzmann engine — OpenLB (its final time-averaged field, U only) or FluidX3D (its VTK export, resolved automatically). Generic Data Points Pts Probe points in model space. Required when Run is true. Point Field Field to sample. The dropdown lists the fields the solved case holds (the common OpenFOAM fields before a solve); a multi-region case lists them as region/field, e.g. air/UMean. Type or wire any other field name; a bare name on a multi-region case goes to the region that holds it. For a FluidX3D VTK directory: "rho"/"density" → density, otherwise velocity. Text Probe Name Name Name of the probe set. Optional — if left blank, a unique name is generated automatically (adjective-animal-place-noun, e.g. swift-otter-fjord-lantern). Text Time Result time to probe — the dropdown lists every time written on disk: latestTime (default) = latest written time, a number = that written time, all = every written time still on disk (empty, as before the dropdown, reads every probed time). Times that were purged (Keep Time Steps) cannot be probed. FluidX3D results also accept avg (mean over every written time) and avg:START-END (mean over a window in seconds, e.g. avg:120-360 to skip the spin-up transient). Text Run True: run postProcess to sample the requested time (Time input), then read. False: read existing results only. Boolean

docs.title: Output
docs.text: Name Nickname Description Type Values Probe values (numbers or vectors); branch = {sub-result, field, time}, items = one per point. Generic Data Time Steps Times Sampled time steps; branch = {sub-result, field}. Text Sub-Results Subs Sub-result labels matching the first branch index (e.g. wind direction case names). Text Points Pts The probe points actually written and sampled — the input points minus the culled ones. Values items line up with this list, one per point. Point

docs.text: Read cell connectivity and cell zones for a region. OutdoorPlus

docs.title: Input
docs.text: Name Nickname Description Type Case UMF case containing the region data. Generic Data Region Region name to read. Text Chunk Size Chunk Chunk size for reading owner/neighbour files. Optional; default is 500. Integer Chunk Offset Offset Chunk offset for reading owner/neighbour files. Optional; default is 0. Integer

docs.title: Output
docs.text: Name Nickname Description Type Cells by Face Indices Cells Tree of cells containing face indices. Generic Data Cell Zone Names Zones Cell zone names. Text Cell Zone Indices ZoneIndices Indices for each cell zone. Generic Data

docs.title: Read Results - [source code]
docs.text: Read what a case's function objects wrote under postProcessing/ — forces, force coefficients, y+, flow rates, volume/surface field values, probe histories, sampled profiles — as columns of numbers, with per-column statistics. One grammar reads every tabular file OpenFOAM writes there, including function objects Eddy3D has never heard of. Restart slices of a time series are stitched with the later run winning; a sampled profile is one snapshot per time.

docs.title: Input
docs.text: Name Nickname Description Type Case A written case: a wind study (one sub-result per direction), a loaded study, a UMF case, an indoor case, or a path to a case folder. Generic Data Dataset Which output to read, as function/file (e.g. forces/force.dat, probes/U, air/probes/T for a region-nested UMF case) or just the function name when it writes one file. Leave empty to read the only dataset present; the Datasets output always lists what is available. Text Time For a sampled PROFILE (a file whose first column is distance, not time): which snapshot to read — empty or latest = the latest start time, a number = that start time. Ignored for a time series, whose restart slices are always stitched. Text Refresh Re-read the files now. Momentary. Results are read off the solution thread and cached until the inputs or the files change; a solve still writing to the case needs this to pick up new rows. Boolean

docs.title: Output
docs.text: Name Nickname Description Type Values The numbers: branch = {sub-result, column}, items = one per row. Column 0 (time or distance) is on the Times output, not here. Number Names Column names in Values order, taken from the file's own header — OpenFOAM's names where it writes them (total_x), component suffixes (U_x) where it does not, probe coordinates folded in. Text Times The independent variable per sub-result: solver time for a series, distance for a profile. Number Stats One line per column: last value, tail mean (final fifth — what a report quotes), min, max, sample count, and for a time series whether it has SETTLED by the KPSS stationarity test over the trailing half, with the two-fifths drift as a reading aid. Text Datasets Every tabular dataset found under postProcessing/, as function/file keys. Text Log What was read, from where, and anything that was dropped, replaced or skipped. Text

docs.title: Run Settings - [source code]
docs.text: Configure solver run controls for Eddy3D. PIMPLE (transient) writes Co below 1, three pressure correctors, turbulence on every outer corrector and unbounded convection. Method: Wolf Dynamics (2021), OpenFOAM advanced training, online session, July 2021 GT-79, GT-97, GT-100, https://www.wolfdynamics.com/training/turbulence/OF2021/turbulence_20221_OF8_guided_tutorials.pdf.

docs.title: Input
docs.text: Name Nickname Description Type Iterations Iter Total solver iterations (endTime). Optional; default is 1000. Integer Write Interval WriteInt Write interval in iterations. Optional; default is 20. Integer Keep Time Steps Keep Number of time directories to keep (purgeWrite). Optional; default is 3. Integer Turbulence Model Turb RANS turbulence model (OpenFOAM 12). The four best for urban wind: Realizable k-ε (default; AIJ/COST732 best practice for pedestrian wind), Standard k-ε (ABL baseline), RNG k-ε (high-strain / recirculation), and SST k-ω (separation, near-wall). All run on the template's existing fields. Text CPU Count CPU Number of CPUs/subdomains for parallel runs. -1 (default) = auto: the machine's physical cores minus two. Optional. Integer Solver Algorithm Algo Pressure-velocity coupling for the steady solver. SIMPLE (default) is the robust, conservatively under-relaxed baseline. SIMPLEC adds the consistent correction so it tolerates much higher relaxation (p 0.7, U/turbulence 0.9), which usually converges in fewer iterations on a good urban mesh — try it for speed, fall back to SIMPLE if a hard case stalls or oscillates. Optional; default is SIMPLE. Text Age of Air Age Solve the mean age of air (OpenFOAM 'age' function object) during the run. Age [s] is the time since the air at each point entered the domain — the urban ventilation/stagnation map (low = well flushed, high = trapped in canyons/courtyards). Adds a cheap scalar transport solved alongside the flow at every iteration (turbulent diffusion on) and written with the other fields; the 'age' field is then viewable in ParaView or probe-able. Optional; default is false. Boolean Numerics Num Numerics as a point on the Accuracy / Robustness / Speed triangle. It sets the convection and gradient schemes, the under-relaxation, the non-orthogonal correctors, the laplacian correction (unless Laplacian Scheme overrides it), the linear-solver relTol and the auto warm-up length together. Accuracy corner: second-order convection, high relaxation, full laplacian correction — captures wakes and eddies but needs a good mesh and warms up first. Robustness corner: first-order upwind, heavy relaxation, three correctors — always converges, smears wakes by numerical diffusion. Speed corner: first-order upwind, one corrector, loose relTol, short warm-up. The old 1-5 levels are named points (right-click, or the picker's buttons); the default is level 4, the shipped baseline, so nothing changes until the dot moves. Accepts a wired "4" or "a,r,s". Standards note: the ASCE/SEI CWE Prestandard's AC 4-3 needs second-order convection — the Accuracy side (levels 1-3); the Robustness/Speed side is first-order upwind. Text Potential Foam Init PotFoam Initialise velocity/pressure with a quick potentialFoam (potential-flow Laplace) solve before simpleFoam, so the run starts from a developed, divergence-free field instead of a uniform one. Removes the first-iteration velocity overshoot of a cold start and shortens convergence. Complements the Warm-up Iterations ramp (potentialFoam seeds the field; the ramp damps the first iterations with first-order upwind + heavy turbulence relaxation). Optional; default is off (shipped behaviour). Boolean Warm-up Iterations Warmup Run this many initial iterations with robust 1st-order upwind + heavy turbulence under-relaxation, then ramp up to the numerics dial for the rest of the run. Tames the cold-start velocity overshoot without losing final accuracy. -1 (default) = automatic: scales with the robustness dial (robust levels 4-5 warm up, accurate levels 1-2 do not). 0 = force off. >0 = explicit count. Integer Field Monitors Monitors Write the domain min/max-magnitude and volume-average of the solved fields (U, p, k, ε/ω, νt) each write-time, and the domain max |U| every iteration. Cheap convergence + stability monitor — a max |U| climbing past any physical value is the earliest sign of a cold-start overshoot or divergence. Default on. Boolean Pedestrian Average PedAvg Write the area-average of U on a horizontal plane at the Pedestrian Height (default 1.75 m) each write — the comfort-relevant mean wind speed, sampled from the live mesh (no topoSet). Default off. Boolean Pressure Coefficient Cp Write the surface pressure coefficient (Cp) field each write, computed from the ABL wind speed at building height (dynamic pressure reference). View it on the building surfaces in ParaView. Default off. Method: Dogan & Kastner (2021), Building Simulation 14(4):1189-1200, doi:10.1007/s12273-020-0727-x; Dogan & Kastner (2018), IBPC 2018, Syracuse NY 1139-1144, doi:10.14305/ibpc.2018.ms-5.05. Boolean Convergence Conv Auto-stop tolerance: the solver stops once the p, U and k initial residuals (plus omega for k-omega models; never epsilon, whose residual cannot reach a tolerance) all drop below this value (SIMPLE residualControl) — typically 30-60 % faster than running the full iteration count. Default 1e-4; 0 disables auto-stop (always runs all iterations). Number Auto-stop on Plateau AutoStop Watches the live residuals while the run is going; once every field's residual has been flat for about 100 iterations after any warm-up ramp, writes stopAt=writeNow — exactly what the manual right-click 'Stop Simulation Gracefully' action does — so the solver finishes its current iteration, writes the latest fields, and exits cleanly instead of grinding out the rest of the iteration count. Requires a Live Residuals component monitoring the case. Optional; default is off. Boolean Duration Dur PIMPLE only: how long to simulate, in SECONDS of physical time (the steady solver's Iterations input is ignored). Size it from the domain flow-through time L/U - the statistics need several flow-throughs before they settle, and a run that is too short produces a confident-looking mean of the start-up transient. 0 or blank defaults to 600 s and says so on the component. Optional. Number Time Step dt PIMPLE only: initial time step in seconds. This is only a SEED - the run uses adjustTimeStep, so the step is re-derived every iteration from the Max Courant limit and climbs away from this value within a few steps. Leave at 0 for the default (0.01 s), which is small enough never to start a run unstable. Optional. Number Max Courant Co PIMPLE only: Courant number cap that sets the time step. 0 defaults to 1: PIMPLE's outer correctors keep Co > 1 stable, not time-accurate, and a wake's shedding needs Co below 1 (Wolf Dynamics, GT-100). Raising it buys wall-clock at the cost of time accuracy; lower it if the run goes unstable. Optional. Number Averaging Window Win PIMPLE only: averaging time constant in SECONDS. A transient run's U is an instantaneous, gusty snapshot, so the case also writes UMean/pMean (plus UPrime2Mean, the resolved variance) - read THOSE downstream, not U. The window damps the start-up transient exponentially, weighting a contribution by about exp(-age/window); it does NOT hard-cut it, because OpenFOAM 12's fieldAverage has no timeStart. So keep the run long relative to the window. 0 or blank uses half the Duration. Optional. Number Pressure Solver pSolver Linear solver for the pressure equation. GAMG (default): algebraic multigrid, GaussSeidel smoother — measured 4× faster wall time than PCG on a 311k-cell urban mesh at 8 ranks, same iteration count, same field. PCG/DIC is the template's original and stays available for comparison. Text Laplacian Scheme Laplacian Non-orthogonal correction of the laplacian terms. 'limited 0.5' (the standard snappyHexMesh choice: half the explicit correction, bounded) or 'corrected' (full correction, the template's original). The default is the one that measured better on two urban configurations — see the Run Settings log for what was written. Text Mesh Quality Preset MeshQ What the mesh's own checkMesh verdict does to the numerics before Simulate. checkMesh runs as the last step of Mesh; Simulate reads its 06_checkMesh.txt (after checking it describes the mesh on disk) and presets the numerics PATH: 'auto' (default) — a failed check, or max skewness > 4 / non-orthogonality > 70° (checkMesh's own limits) solves on the 'robust' path (p 0.3 / U 0.5 / turbulence 0.25, three correctors, a longer warm-up); skewness ≥ 10, non-orthogonality ≥ 80° or inverted cells on 'hardened' (that path plus a potentialFoam start and a doubled warm-up). A mesh that passes changes nothing. 'off' keeps the Numerics above whatever the mesh looks like; 'robust' / 'hardened' apply that preset unconditionally. The convection, gradient and laplacian schemes and the convergence criterion are never touched, so the answer is the one the Numerics input asks for — only the route to it moves. Run All applies it too: unless this is 'off' it meshes in its own window and opens Simulate once the new mesh is built and checked. The Wind Run component says what was applied. Optional. Text Pedestrian Height PedH The study's pedestrian (comfort sampling) height above ground, m. Where Pedestrian Average samples, and recorded in the case (controlDict marker + eddy3d-study.json) so Study Report can print it and check it against an authority — the City of London guideline asks for 1.5 m — and ParaView's pedestrian slice follows it. Default 1.75 m, the value used before this was a setting, so existing studies are unchanged. It declares the height; place your probe points at it. Number Guideline Guide The planning guideline this study is set up for. City of London (2019): SETS the pedestrian height to 1.5 m (unless Pedestrian Height is wired or changed) and prism layers that put three cells below 1.5 m (absolute sizes: 0.3 m first layer, ratio 1.2); RECORDS itself, so Study Report checks against it without its Authority input; and WARNS — on this component and on Outdoor Case — about what it cannot set for you: 36 directions at 10°, 400 m of modelled context, the Harris & Deaves inlet (ABL → Inlet Profile), cell sizes, a turbulence model it advises against. None (the default) changes nothing. Text Concurrent Directions Concurrent How many wind directions Run All solves AT ONCE (Docker / WSL). CPU Count is the budget they share: 4 directions on 16 CPUs run on 4 ranks each, which beats 16 ranks one after another once MPI scaling flattens (about 1M cells). Each direction logs to its own run_concurrent.txt; one failed direction fails the run. blueCFD stays sequential. 1 (the default) = one at a time. Integer Empty Domain Check EmptyDomain The ASCE/SEI CWE prestandard's two-step process (PO 4-1 / AC 5-9): every direction gets an EMPTY twin (empty_NNN on mesh*_empty) — the same domain, mesh settings, inlet and numerics without the buildings, their volume refined in their place — meshed and solved with it, sampled on the vertical through the site centre. The Study Report's ABL self-sustainment verdict then reads the twin (the incident location proper) instead of the building run's approach station. Costs one extra mesh and solve per direction. Off by default. Boolean

docs.title: Runoff Zones - [source code]
docs.text: Assigns a surface MATERIAL to an area of the site. The material's runoff coefficient is the share of the rain landing there that enters the surface flow, and it brings an overland Manning's n — change the material and both swap. Wire the zones into Stormwater Grid's Zones for the ground, or its Roof Zones for roofs; a zone with no Areas is the Default for every cell no other zone covers (or, as a roof zone, every roof). Manning's n here is the OVERLAND FLOW value, several times the channel value for the same material — at the millimetre depths of sheet flow the surface texture is the whole channel, and using a channel roughness makes runoff arrive far too fast. A Curve Number (1–100) replaces the coefficient with losses that grow through a storm as the ground wets up. A Soil replaces both with Green-Ampt infiltration: all the rain reaches the ground and the soil takes water from whatever stands on it — run-on from upslope included, and ponds after the rain has stopped — at a rate that falls from unlimited toward the soil's saturated conductivity as it wets. Solved on the CPU. Overland Manning's n after Engman (1986), J. Irrig. Drain. Eng. 112(1):39-53. Green-Ampt soil parameters as tabulated in the HEC-RAS 2D User's Manual, ported with the source study's workflow. Method: DIN 1986-100:2016-12 (2016), DIN Media, Berlin Table 9, doi:10.31030/2586228; Green & Ampt (1911), Journal of Agricultural Science 4(1):1-24, doi:10.1017/S0021859600001441; Shrestha et al. (2026), Urban Systems Lab, urban-flood-modeling-workflows, https://github.com/UrbanSystemsLab/urban-flood-modeling-workflows.

docs.title: Input
docs.text: Name Nickname Description Type Areas Closed curves outlining where this surface type applies, in plan. Curves are projected to the world XY plane, and a cell belongs to a zone when its CENTRE does. Leave unwired for a zone with no outline: in Stormwater Grid's Zones it is the Default material for every cell no drawn zone covers; in Roof Zones it covers every roof. Curve Surface The surface material. Its runoff coefficient (DIN 1986-100 Table 9, mean Cm) is the share of the rain on this area that enters the surface flow, and it brings an overland Manning's n. Changing the material swaps both. Pick Custom to set the Runoff Coefficient yourself; set a Curve Number to use the SCS loss model instead. Text Curve Number CN SCS Curve Number, 1–100. Higher sheds more: 98 is sealed paving, 61 a healthy lawn on an average soil, 55 mature woodland. Unlike a flat coefficient it makes runoff GROW through a storm as the ground wets up, which is why it suits a design event. 0 (the default) uses the material's runoff coefficient instead. Number Runoff Coefficient C Fraction of rainfall that becomes runoff, 0–1, for the Custom surface only — every material carries its own. Ignored when a Curve Number is set. Number Manning's n n Overland-flow roughness (s/m^⅓). A positive value overrides the material's. Typical: 0.012 smooth paving, 0.05 gravel, 0.24 short grass, 0.40 woodland litter. Number Initial Abstraction Ratio Ia/S Fraction of the soil's storage absorbed before ANY runoff starts. 0.05 is the default and the value re-analysis of the original gauge data supports for small, largely impervious urban catchments; the textbook TR-55 figure of 0.2 was fitted to agricultural watersheds and under-predicts urban runoff. Pass 0.2 to reproduce it. Number Soil A soil texture to infiltrate by Green-Ampt instead of the runoff coefficient or Curve Number. All the rain then reaches the ground, and the soil takes water from whatever stands on it — run-on from upslope included, and ponds after the rain has stopped — at a rate that falls from unlimited on dry soil toward its saturated conductivity Ks as the wetting front deepens: Ks 223 mm/h for sand, 13 for loam, 0.6 for clay. The material still brings its Manning's n. None (the default) keeps the material's coefficient, or the Curve Number when one is set; a Soil and a Curve Number together are refused. Solved on the CPU solver only. Text Initial Saturation Sat How wet the soil is when the storm starts, as an effective saturation: 0 at its residual water content, 1 saturated. Wetter soil leaves less room behind the wetting front and takes less. 0.44 is the source study's default. Green-Ampt (Soil) only. Number

docs.title: Scalar Field Viewer - [source code]
docs.text: Visualize a probed scalar field — CO2, temperature, age of air, Cp, pressure — as a colored point cloud, a heatmap mesh, or a translucent volumetric cloud. Feed the Probe component's points and one value per point. For velocity, use the Vector Field Viewer.

docs.title: Input
docs.text: Name Nickname Description Type Values V One scalar per point, in whatever unit the field is in — the Probe component's Values output for a single scalar field (CO2, T, age, Cp, p, k). Number Points P Sample points (e.g. the probe points). Empty with a Mesh wired uses the mesh's samples: its vertices when it has one per value (the WRF Probe's Mesh) or its face centres when it has one face per value (the square probe markers of Deconstruct MRT and Deconstruct Wind), in Values order — so mesh-only wiring is complete. Point Display Mode M How to render the field: Point Cloud (colored samples, filtered to the Min/Max band), Heatmap Mesh (colors a supplied mesh from the samples on each face), or Volumetric Cloud (translucent points, more opaque the higher the value — for reading a plume in 3D). Text Color Map CM Color ramp — pick the same map as the Flex Legend so the legend matches what is drawn. Text Min Value Min Lower end of the color range / filter. Empty = data minimum. Number Max Value Max Upper end of the color range / filter. Empty = data maximum. Number Mesh Msh Surface to color for Heatmap Mesh mode. A mesh with faces is subdivided to the samples' spacing and each vertex is read from the samples that lie on its own face, so a wall is not blended from the ground and the roof; faces that meet at a crease keep separate colours. A mesh of bare vertices takes the nearest sample. Ignored in the other modes. Mesh Size S Point Cloud and Volumetric Cloud: drawn point size in pixels. Heatmap Mesh with Fit = Size: the width of each square probe marker, in model units. Number Fit Heatmap Mesh over a square-per-probe mesh (Deconstruct MRT / Wind's Mesh): Gapless grows every square to the probe spacing so the squares touch; Size draws each one Size wide. Any other mesh is left as wired. Text Units U Unit label for the component's readout only (e.g. ppm, K, s, Pa). The field carries no unit of its own, so nothing can infer it: probing CO2 returns a mass fraction, age of air returns seconds, and both are just numbers by the time they reach here. Text

docs.title: Shadow - [source code]
docs.text: Lit or shaded at each analysis point for one or more sun instants — the shadow's position, not accumulated sun hours.

docs.title: Input
docs.text: Name Nickname Description Type Context C Shading geometry: buildings, terrain, canopies. Geometry Points P Analysis points. Point Normals N Optional per-point normals. A sun below a point's own horizon counts as shaded without tracing — a floor cannot be lit from beneath. Vector Weather W Weather record from Download Weather or Open Weather. The sun's position for each evaluated hour comes from this file. Generic Data HOY H Hours of the year to evaluate [1-8760], one result branch per hour — wire the Hour Of Year component to name a date and time. Left empty, every DAYLIGHT hour of the year is evaluated, which on a large grid is a long run. Integer Offset O Distance to lift each point off its surface before tracing. Number North Nth Counter-clockwise degrees from the model's +Y axis to true north (Ladybug's convention). The sun is rotated, not the model. Number Engine Eng Who traces the rays. docs.title: Share Bundle - [source code]
docs.text: Write results as files anyone can open without Rhino: ONE self-contained HTML viewer (top-down map with pan/zoom and an orbiting 3D view, sets and layers, legend, hover readout, KPI tables, wind rose, swipe and difference comparison between sets, print to PDF — works offline from the file), glTF binaries (.glb, one per layer, for web/VR/AR viewers), float32 GeoTIFFs (UTM when the site latitude/longitude is given), a PDF report and slide-ready PNGs. Wire one Values branch per layer over the Points (or a Mesh with per-vertex or per-face values). Every file states that the results were computed by the solver and that Eddy3D is the front end.

docs.title: Input
docs.text: Name Nickname Description Type Folder Dir Output folder. Empty with a Study wired: the bundle goes to /share. Text Title T Title of the bundle; also names the files. Left at the default with a Study wired: " — results". Text Points P Sample points (e.g. the pedestrian grid). Each value branch with one value per point is a point layer. Point Mesh M Result surface instead of points: a branch with one value per mesh VERTEX or per mesh FACE is a mesh layer. Mesh Values V One branch per layer (e.g. a comfort class, a speed, one branch per wind direction). NaN = no data. Number Layer Names N One name per branch (or one for all). Default: Layer 1, Layer 2, … Text Sets S One set name per branch (or one for all): switchable groups such as directions, seasons, or "Existing" / "Proposed". Two sets holding layers of the same name get the viewer's swipe and difference comparison. Text Units U Unit per branch (or one for all), e.g. m/s, °C. Text Classes C Class table for categorical layers: a Wind Comfort Criteria object, a metric name ("Lawson LDDC", "Davenport" …) or class labels best first. Applied to every branch whose values are category numbers (1..n; 0 = no data, as Pedestrian Wind Comfort's Rank). Generic Data Context Ctx Buildings, terrain, trees, ground layers, in the site's clay look. A mesh from City Surface, LiDAR Site, Site Look or Site Context is drawn as what it is (trees green, water blue …); any other mesh as a building. Empty with a wind Study wired: the building and terrain surfaces the study was meshed from. Mesh Latitude Lat Latitude of the model origin (0,0), +Y north. With Longitude, GeoTIFFs are written in UTM and the viewer reads out latitude/longitude. Empty: the Study's wind-climate site, if any. Number Longitude Lon Longitude of the model origin (0,0). Number Study The case the results came from: a Wind Study (or its folder), or any case a Probe accepts. Fills every input left empty — Folder (/share), Title, site, Context — and adds the origin (engine, directions, Eddy3D version, the study report, the wind climate as a wind rose). A Wind Conditions record may be wired too (the wind rose). Generic Data Formats F Which files: a choice, or a list such as "html,glb,tif,pdf,png". Text Write W Write the bundle. docs.title: Site Context - [source code]
docs.text: One click from a location to the site's context: buildings with heights, bare-earth terrain, tree crowns, land-cover ground zones with their roughness, and the inlet z0 per wind direction — fetched in the background from open data and placed in a local frame centred on the location (Rhino model units). Sources: OpenStreetMap buildings (ODbL; height from the height tag or building:levels x 3 m, else the Fallback Height — never guessed silently: every building's height KIND is in the report), GEDTM30 bare-earth DTM (CC BY 4.0), the Meta/WRI 1 m canopy height map plus OSM street trees (CC BY 4.0 / ODbL), and ESA WorldCover 2021 (CC BY 4.0). Buildings come from GlobalBuildingAtlas LoD1 (TUM, CC BY-NC 4.0 — heights PREDICTED by a model, every one labelled so) or from OpenStreetMap (ODbL — the height tag or building:levels x 3 m, else the Fallback Height), chosen on Building Source. Results are cached on disk, so a reopened document shows its context without a new fetch; pressing Fetch again, or Refresh from the sources on the right-click menu, downloads anew.

docs.title: Input
docs.text: Name Nickname Description Type Latitude Lat Latitude of the SITE, decimal degrees WGS84. Optional: with neither Latitude nor Longitude wired, the document's Earth Anchor Point is used (and its model point and north become the Anchor). Not an EPW header's latitude — that is the weather station. Number Longitude Lon Longitude of the SITE, decimal degrees WGS84, east positive. Optional, as Latitude. Number Radius R Half-size (m) of the square the buildings, trees and ground zones cover. Buildings straddling the edge are clipped to it. Optional; default 500, at most 3000. Number Terrain Radius TR Half-size (m) of the terrain (and of the ground zones on it). Make it cover the whole CFD domain floor; the inlet z0 is read over the 3 km BEYOND it. Optional; 0 or unset = 2 x Radius. Number Anchor Plane Model plane the location maps to (X = east, Y = north). Optional; default the Earth Anchor Point's plane when the site comes from it, else the world XY origin. Plane Fallback Height Hf Height (m) given to a building whose source states no height or storeys. Such buildings are labelled 'fallback' in the report and on the mesh. 0 = leave them out. Optional; default 9 (three storeys). Number Wind Directions Dirs Wind directions (meteorological degrees, wind FROM, clockwise from north) to report the upstream z0 for. Wire the same list into ABL's Wind Directions. Optional; default the eight compass points. Number Building Source Src Where the buildings come from. Global Building Atlas: LoD1 footprints worldwide with heights PREDICTED by a model (RMSE 1.5-8.9 m; TUM, CC BY-NC 4.0 — non-commercial use), read straight from the published tiles. OpenStreetMap: mapped footprints with the height tag or building:levels x 3 m, else the Fallback Height (ODbL; via the public Overpass mirrors, which can queue for minutes). Overture Maps: the newest release's building footprints (conflated from OpenStreetMap, Microsoft ML Buildings, Esri Community Maps, Google Open Buildings and others), with the height it states or num_floors x 3 m, else the Fallback Height - many buildings carry neither, so check Height Sources (ODbL-1.0 for the theme; the contributing datasets keep their own terms, Esri and Google CC BY 4.0; credit: (c) OpenStreetMap contributors, Overture Maps Foundation), read straight from the published files. The height KIND of every building is on its mesh and in the report. Text Terrain Source TSrc Where the ground comes from. GEDTM30: global bare-earth model, 30 m (CC BY 4.0) - the default. Auto: the regional bare-earth model that covers the site (Canada HRDEM, else USGS 3DEP), else GEDTM30. USGS 3DEP: the 1 m lidar DEM where a project covers the site, else ~10 m, then ~30 m, USA (public domain). Canada HRDEM: lidar DTM at 1 m, then 2 m, where flown, Canada (Open Government Licence - Canada). Copernicus GLO-30: global but a SURFACE model - buildings and trees are in the heights, so building massing seated on it stands too high (use only where nothing else covers the site). Each is read straight from its public bucket, no key. A source with no data at the site gives flat ground and says so in the Report. Optional; default GEDTM30. Text Fetch Press to fetch every selected layer in the background — the canvas stays live. One press is one attempt: a Fetch held true by a wired toggle does not retry a failed fetch on every recompute. A press on a site already in the cache downloads it anew (the cached answer stays on the outputs until the new one lands). Right-click to cancel, or to refresh from the sources. Boolean

docs.title: Output
docs.text: Name Nickname Description Type Buildings Bldg One closed mesh per building, seated on the terrain (roof = median ground + height; the base reaches 20 m below the lowest ground under it so it pierces the terrain, or stands on z = 0 without terrain). Each mesh carries its height, height kind and source id (OSM or Overture) as user strings. Plug into the wind case's Buildings. Mesh Building Heights H Height (m) above the median ground per building, index-aligned with Buildings. Number Height Sources HSrc Where each height came from, index-aligned with Buildings: predicted (Global Building Atlas), osm:height (a mapped height), osm:levels (storeys x 3 m), overture:height or overture:levels (Overture Maps: stated height, or num_floors x 3 m) or fallback (your Fallback Height). Text Terrain T Bare-earth terrain mesh (GEDTM30), elevation RELATIVE to the ground at the location. Empty when the Terrain layer is off or the DTM host was unreachable (then the report says so and everything stands on flat ground). Mesh Site Elevation Elev Absolute elevation (m above sea level) of the ground at the location — the terrain's z = 0. Number Tree Crowns Crowns Tree crown volumes, one mesh per cluster of the canopy map (4 m columns from 0.41 x tree height to the top) and one per mapped OSM tree the map has no crown over. Plug into the Tree component's Geometry, one Tree per crown. Mesh Tree Points TPts Every mapped OSM tree (natural=tree, and tree_row every 8 m) at its ground point, whether or not it got its own crown. Point Tree Heights TH Height (m) per tree point: the mapped height tag, else 10 m. Index-aligned with Tree Points. Number Ground Zones Zones The terrain split by land use (WorldCover), one mesh per region and class, coloured by z0 on the fixed Davenport scale. Inside Radius the ground is read by the RESOLVED table (built = the street between the meshed buildings, 0.03 m; tree = forest floor under a fetched crown, 0.1 m), beyond it by the upstream one. Wire with Roughness Lengths and Land Cover into Ground Roughness. Mesh Roughness Lengths z0 z0 (m) per ground zone, index-aligned with Ground Zones. Number Land Cover Class Zone name per ground zone (region_class, e.g. core_built, ring_water), index-aligned with Ground Zones — usable as Ground Roughness' Names. Text Wind Directions Dirs The directions z0 per Direction is aligned with. Number z0 per Direction z0 [m] Upstream z0 (m) per wind direction: the log-mean of the land cover over the 3 km the wind crosses before the terrain edge, ±15°. Wire into ABL's z0 per Direction. A sector with no classified land (off the WorldCover map) gets the log-mean of the other directions, with a Warning naming it — never a gap, which would shift every later direction's z0. Number Report Origin, as JSON: every source, licence, date, count, what was left out and why, and the building heights by KIND. Text Ground Zones GZones The land-cover zones as Ground Zone objects (mesh, roughness length z0, name): wire into Outdoor Case's Ground Roughness. Zones itself is plain meshes for display and carries no z0. Generic Data

The map window stays in front of Rhino and Grasshopper while it is open. Latitude and Longitude (WGS84 degrees) go into LiDAR Site, Site Context or any component that takes a site. The pick is saved with the document. The last 20 places you searched for or used are kept on this machine (~/Eddy3D/site-picker-recent.json): Recent in the map window, and "Recent sites" in this component's right-click menu sets one without opening the map. Imagery: Esri World Imagery; map: © OpenStreetMap contributors. Needs an internet connection.

docs.title: Site Report - [source code]
docs.text: Write a client-ready PDF site report from a weather file and the Rhino viewports: climate key statistics, wind rose and Weibull, climograph, psychrometric chart, hour-by-day year charts of solar radiation, wind speed and UTCI, the weather-only comfort scenarios (no sun / no wind / full protection), captured views, methodology and glossary, plus the natural-hazard record around the station (earthquakes from USGS, storms, floods, wildfires, volcanoes and landslides from NASA EONET, tsunami run-ups from NOAA NCEI; Hazards switches it off). Every sentence is assembled from the measured numbers by fixed rules. Results from other components that implement the report seam add their own chapters.

docs.title: Input
docs.text: Name Nickname Description Type Folder Dir Output folder. Default: ~/Eddy3D/Reports. Text Title T Report title, printed on the cover and in the footer. Text Weather W The weather year: an EPW file path (e.g. from Download Weather) or an Eddy3D Weather object. Generic Data Views V Rhino viewport names to capture ("Perspective", "Top", or a named view). The first capture is the cover picture; the rest fill the Site views chapter. Empty: the active view. Text Images Img PNG or JPEG files to include after the captures (a rendering, a site photo); the file name is the caption. Text Results R Optional results that add chapters: a Share Bundle (its Bundle output — one chapter of map pages with the share of area per class, per set), a site's Origin (LiDAR Site's Origin output — a table in the methodology of which dataset each layer came from) or an object implementing the report seam. Others are ignored with a remark. Generic Data Author A Author or firm, printed on the cover. Text Logo L PNG or JPEG logo for the cover's corner; empty for the Eddy3D wordmark. Text Future Fut Projected years to compare with the present one: EPW paths from Morph Weather (labelled from their scenario and horizon) or Weather objects. Adds the Future climate chapter. Generic Data Hazards Haz Add the Natural hazards section: events within 100 km of the station from three public catalogues (USGS earthquakes M ≥ 4.5 since 1970, NASA EONET storms / floods / wildfires / volcanoes / landslides since 2015, NOAA NCEI tsunami run-ups since 1900), cached for 30 days. False skips the three requests; offline, the lines read "no data". Boolean Write Go Write the report. Edge-triggered: a click, or a wired value turning true, writes once. Boolean

docs.title: Solar Irradiation - [source code]
docs.text: Cumulative incident solar energy per point in kWh/m² — beam plus isotropic sky plus ground reflection. An interactive preview, not a Radiance simulation.

docs.title: Stormwater Flowlines - [source code]
docs.text: Traces where the runoff goes, as curves over the graded surface. From a full run these are the solved velocity paths; from a fast run they are steepest-descent paths down the depression-filled terrain.

docs.title: Input
docs.text: Name Nickname Description Type Result A run from Stormwater Run. Generic Data Seed Spacing Spacing Distance in metres between the points flowlines are started from. Smaller is denser and slower. Number Minimum Catchment MinArea Terrain mode only: seed a line only where at least this much upslope area already drains through (m²). Raising it turns a hairball of sheet flow into the drainage NETWORK, which is usually what you want to look at. 0 seeds everywhere. Number Maximum Length MaxLen Give up on a line after this many metres, so a slow eddy cannot spin forever. Number Time Minutes from the storm's start. Full runs only — the velocity field at the nearest stored snapshot is traced. Leave at 0 to use the peak-velocity field. Number
