docs.title: Velocity Amplification Factors (VAF) - [source code]
docs.text: Compute Velocity Amplification Factors (VAF) and annual wind speed at probes from CFD or ML wind-prediction results and EPW weather data. VAF (the term used in the wind-engineering literature for what Eddy3D historically called "wind factors") is the local wind speed normalized by the reference speed. Method: Kastner & Dogan (2022), Building and Environment 212:108639, doi:10.1016/j.buildenv.2021.108639; Kastner & Dogan (2019), Building Simulation 2019, Rome 621-628, doi:10.26868/25222708.2019.210458.

docs.title: Input
docs.text: Name Nickname Description Type Boundary Conditions BC OutdoorBoundaryConditions object from the ABL or Uniform Flow component. Generic Data Wind Velocity U DataTree {direction}[probe] of velocity vectors from the CFD probe results, OR of scalar wind speeds (m/s) from the Wind Predictor's Values output — either engine feeds the same annual wind field. Generic Data EPW Path to the EPW weather file. Text Probe Height Height Probing/pedestrian height in meters. Number Interpolate Interp How each weather hour's direction is mapped onto the simulated directions — for any number of them. Interpolate blends the two BRACKETING directions by angular proximity; Nearest snaps to the closest simulated direction. A wired boolean from an older document still works: True means Interpolate, False means Nearest. Text Points P Optional probe points in the same order as the Wind Velocity tree's branches. Embedded into the Wind Speed output so downstream components — the Pedestrian Wind Comfort mesh — know where each series lives without extra wiring. Point Factors What the Velocity Amplification Factors output carries. Annual (per hour) — the default: {hour}(probes), 8760 branches, each hour's factor resolved from the EPW's wind direction through the Interpolate setting; needs the EPW and is built only while the output is wired (prefer the one-item Annual VAF output into Deconstruct Wind). Spatial (per direction): {direction}(probes), one branch per simulated direction. Text TKE k Optional turbulent kinetic energy k (m²/s²) at the probes, one branch per simulated direction like Wind Velocity (the probe's k field). With the EPW it yields the Gust Speed output: U + g·√(2k/3), the Gust Equivalent Mean the ML predictor uses, scaled per hour by (EPW speed / reference speed)². Needed by gust-referenced criteria such as Wellington's 20 m/s safety class. Generic Data Peak Factor g Gust peak factor g in U_gust = U + g·σ_u. 3.5 is the 3-second gust used by the Lawson family and Wellington; 3.0 is common for NEN 8100 / Davenport. Number Wind Conditions WC Optional Wind Conditions record (from the Wind Conditions component). When it carries a station-to-site transfer, the EPW's hourly speeds are scaled by the SAME factor the inlet speeds were, so the annual field is consistent with the CFD reference. Without it the EPW speeds are used as recorded at the station. Generic Data

docs.title: Output
docs.text: Name Nickname Description Type Wind Speed Wind Annual wind field object (every point's 8760-hour wind-speed series) for the Pedestrian Wind Comfort component. A single object rather than a data tree, so a few thousand probes stay fast. Generic Data Velocity Amplification Factors VAF Velocity Amplification Factors (VAF) — local wind speed normalized by the reference (undisturbed) speed at probe height of each direction's own inlet (its own z0 when the ABL has z0 per Direction). Indexing follows the Factors setting: {direction}(probes) per simulated direction (default), or {hour}(probes) across all 8760 weather hours when Factors is set to Annual. Number Annual VAF AVAF The direction-mapped Velocity Amplification Factor at every probe for every weather hour, carried as ONE object (probes × 8760, dimensionless) — wire it into Deconstruct Wind for statistics, a colored mesh and per-hour values. Needs the EPW; empty until it is connected. This is the fast path: the tree output above materializes the same numbers as millions of items on the canvas. Generic Data Gust Speed Gust Annual 3-second gust field (probes × 8760, m/s) from the TKE input: U + g·√(2k/3). Wire it into Pedestrian Wind Comfort's Gust Speed input for a gust-referenced criterion (Wellington WIND-S1). Empty until TKE and the EPW are connected. Generic Data Speed Ratios Ratios Per-probe speed / inlet reference speed for every simulated direction, as one object (probes × directions, no hours; with TKE wired, the 3-second gust ratio too). Feed it to Pedestrian Wind Comfort's Wind Speed together with a Wind Climate for the probabilistic classification. Needs no EPW. Generic Data

docs.title: Ventilation & Comfort Report - [source code]
docs.text: One page per room: thermal comfort (EN ISO 7730 / EN 16798-1 category shares, ASHRAE 55, draught, stratification, ADPI), ventilation effectiveness (age of air, air change effectiveness, contaminant removal) and airborne infection risk (Wells–Riley) with the ASHRAE 241 equivalent-clean-airflow check — each number beside the reference it is read against, and the caveats that belong to it. Always outputs the Markdown and HTML text; Write saves .md and a self-contained .html (no external assets) into the Folder. Sections left unwired are reported as not evaluated.

docs.title: Input
docs.text: Name Nickname Description Type Folder Dir Where Write saves the report. Text Room Name Room Room name for the title and the file names. Text Comfort Map Map Indoor Comfort Map's Comfort Map output. Generic Data Ventilation Vent Ventilation Effectiveness's Ventilation output. Generic Data Infection Risk Risk Infection Risk's Infection Risk output. Generic Data Notes Extra lines for the caveats (probe grid, solver mode, …). Text Write W Write the .md and .html files to the Folder. Boolean

docs.title: Output
docs.text: Name Nickname Description Type Markdown MD The report as Markdown. Text HTML The report as a self-contained HTML page. Text Files Paths written by the last Write. Text

docs.title: Ventilation Effectiveness - [source code]
docs.text: How well the supply reaches the occupants, from a solved Indoor case. Turn on Age of Air on the Indoor Case, probe 'age' (seconds) at the occupied points, give the room volume, and wire what the case wrote under postProcessing/ through Read Results: the flow it carried (Dataset exhaustFlow, m³/s on both the isothermal and the buoyant path), the flux-weighted exhaust age (exhaustAge) and, for a tracer, its flux-weighted exhaust value (exhaustCO2 / exhaustViral). Returns the nominal time constant τn = V/Q, the local air-change index εp = τref/τp per point, the air-change efficiency εa = τref/(2⟨τ⟩) (50 % mixing, 100 % piston; REHVA Guidebook 2, Mundt et al. 2004), ASHRAE 129's air change effectiveness E = τref/⟨τ⟩ over the breathing zone, and — from a probed tracer (CO2, viral) with its exhaust value — the contaminant removal effectiveness εc = (Ce − Cs)/(⟨C⟩ − Cs). τref is the exhaust age τe when it is wired, else τn: the Indoor case keeps the age function object's turbulent diffusion on (without it the ages follow the mesh), and with age fixed at 0 on the supply age can diffuse out through the supply opening. The isothermal case derives its supply turbulence from the opening and balances (τe/τn 0.999); the buoyant path keeps the template's fixed supply turbulence and leaks — every age reads low, τe/τn 0.891 on the 300 W reference room, 0.797 on the isothermal room at 0.15 m/s with that turbulence. τe carries the same leak, so the indices referenced to it land within a few percent of a leak-free supply (measured down to τe/τn 0.745), where V/Q-referenced ones read 27–32 % high at 0.797 (enough to move E across 1). The Exhaust Check output is τe/τn: 1.00 for pure advection, below 1 by the leak; outside the range a converged field with the case's volume and carried flow can give, E, εa and εp are WITHHELD (an Error names why) — referenced to τe they would look plausible whatever state the age field is in. Point means are volume means only on a uniform grid.

docs.title: Input
docs.text: Name Nickname Description Type Room Volume V Air volume of the room (m³). Number Supply Flow Q The airflow the case CARRIED, as a VOLUME flow in m³/s — not a kg/s mass flow, which nothing here can tell from a volume flow and which reads about 15 % low (ρ ≈ 1.2). The case writes it in m³/s on the isothermal AND the buoyant path: Read Results with Dataset 'exhaustFlow' (postProcessing/exhaustFlow), its Values wired straight in — the LAST value, the final written time, is used. Typed by hand, a design flow in L/s is divided by 1000. The Indoor case imposes each supply as a flow rate, so this is the supply as designed (0.5 m³/s on the reference room); in a case built before 2026-09-30 the inlet was a velocity on the MESHED opening and carried less (0.370 m³/s of a nominal 0.5). The inlet's supplyFlow (negative — OpenFOAM sums inflow — and read as its magnitude) works too, but prefer exhaustFlow: on the buoyant path the supply is the colder, denser air and carries a smaller volume than leaves (0.5000 against 0.5008 m³/s at 300 W; about 2 % at a 3 kW heater, estimated). An air-change rate no room has (1000 /h or more — cleanrooms run 200–600 /h — or below 0.01 /h) is warned as the L/s ↔ m³/s slip it is and the indices are withheld, unless a solved Exhaust Age passes the Exhaust Check (which a flow off by 1000 cannot); so is an εa above 100 %, the piston-flow bound. Number Age of Air Age Probed local mean age of air at the occupied points (s — OpenFOAM's 'age'). Generic Data Breathing Zone BZ Which of the points are in the breathing zone (one per point). Unwired: all of them. Boolean Exhaust Age AgeE The FLUX-weighted mean age of the air leaving the room (s), as the Indoor case writes it when Age of Air is on: Read Results with Dataset 'exhaustAge' (postProcessing/exhaustAge), its Values wired here — the LAST value, the final written time, is used (0 there means the case is not solved yet: a Warning, and τn meanwhile). Wire a FINISHED solve: nothing here can tell a mid-run refresh from a converged one. Wired, the indices are referenced to it (τref = τe); unwired, to τn = V/Q. Not a probed point: one point is not the mean of the exhaust, and even an area average is not the flux-weighted one. Number Tracer C Probed tracer (CO2, viral) at the same points. Generic Data Exhaust Tracer Ce The FLUX-weighted mean of the tracer in the air leaving the room, as the Indoor Case writes it for every CO2/viral emitter: Read Results with Dataset 'exhaustCO2' or 'exhaustViral' (postProcessing/exhaustCO2, …), its Values wired here — the LAST value, the final written time, is used (0 there means the case is not solved yet: a Warning, and no εc). Not a point probed at the outlet: the exhaust carries the flux-weighted mean (the viral balance closes at 1.000 with it, 0.983 with the area average). The Indoor Species Case writes no exhaustCO2 — its CO2 is a mass fraction of a multicomponent mixture, not this tracer. Number Supply Tracer Cs Tracer in the supply air (0 for the Indoor Case's CO2/viral tracers, whose inlet is fixed at 0). Number Tracer Name Name Label for the report. Text

docs.title: Output
docs.text: Name Nickname Description Type Nominal Time Constant τn τn = V/Q (s) — reported whatever the indices are referenced to. Number Local Air-Change Index εp τref/τp per point (1 = as good as mixing); τref = the exhaust age τe when wired, else τn. Withheld when the Exhaust Check fails. Number Air-Change Efficiency εa τref/(2⟨τ⟩) (%) — 50 mixing, 100 piston. Withheld when the Exhaust Check fails. Number Air Change Effectiveness E ASHRAE 129: τref/⟨τ⟩ over the breathing zone. Withheld when the Exhaust Check fails. Number Exhaust Check τe/τn Exhaust age over τn — the mass-balance check: 1.00 for pure advection of age, below 1 under the buoyant Indoor setup (age leaks out through the supply; about 0.89), 0.999 on the isothermal one, and E, εa, εp withheld above 1.02 or below 0.50. Number Removal Effectiveness εc Contaminant removal effectiveness over all points. Number Breathing Zone Removal εc,bz Contaminant removal effectiveness over the breathing zone. Number Local Removal εc,p Local contaminant removal index per point. Number Summary Sum Readable summary. Text Ventilation Vent The assessment, for the Ventilation & Comfort Report. Generic Data

docs.title: Verify Prediction - [source code]
docs.text: Compare an ML wind prediction with a CFD result at the same points: VDI 3783-9 hit rate (D = 0.25, W = 0.05·U_ref; ≥ 0.66 passes), FAC2, Willmott's index of agreement, R, bias, MAE and RMSE per direction and overall, plus the per-point deviation. Write appends the compared points to a verification log (Dataset Curator columns + U_pred + U_cfd) that is retraining data and a training envelope for Prediction Confidence. ML screening prediction, not CFD: use it to compare options, then confirm anything that matters with a Wind Study (planning authorities do not accept surrogate results).

docs.title: Input
docs.text: Name Nickname Description Type Points The points both results were sampled at (absolute Z). Point Predicted ML wind speeds [m/s], one branch per wind direction (the Wind Predictor's Values output). Number CFD CFD wind speeds [m/s] at the same points, one branch per direction in the same order (e.g. Probe |U|). Number Boundary Conditions BC The study's boundary conditions: U_ref sets the hit rate's absolute tolerance W = 0.05·U_ref and the log's normalised columns; the wind directions label the branches. Generic Data Buildings Optional: building geometry, so the log carries SDF / Bldg_height exactly as the Dataset Curator writes them. Geometry Pedestrian Level PedLevel Pedestrian mounting height [m] for the log's features. Number Log Verification log CSV to append to (created with its header when new). Text Case A name for this comparison in the log. Text Write Append the compared points to the log. Fires once per set of inputs, also when wired. Boolean

docs.title: Output
docs.text: Name Nickname Description Type Metrics Agreement metrics: overall first, then one block per direction. Text Hit Rate HitRate VDI 3783-9 hit rate per direction (then overall, last). Number Passes Hit rate ≥ 0.66 per direction (then overall, last). Boolean Deviation Dev Predicted − CFD [m/s] per point, one branch per direction. Number Colors Per point: green within the hit-rate tolerance, blue over-predicted, red under-predicted. Colour

docs.title: Vertical Sky Component - [source code]
docs.text: Vertical Sky Component per point, in percent: the diffuse illuminance a vertical plane receives directly from a CIE standard overcast sky, over the illuminance an unobstructed horizontal plane would receive under the same sky. Geometry only — no weather, no orientation, no time of year. An unobstructed vertical plane reads 39.6%; BRE BR 209 reads 27% as the guideline for conventional window design.

docs.title: Input
docs.text: Name Nickname Description Type Context C Obstructing geometry: buildings, terrain, canopies. Obstructions are treated as perfectly black — VSC counts direct skylight only, so nothing here reflects. Geometry Points P Analysis points, on the plane whose sky access is wanted. Wire Facade Grid for a facade map, or place points at window centres for the BR 209 assessment. Point Normals N Outward normal at each point — REQUIRED. VSC is a property of a plane, not of a location: the same point facing two ways has two different VSCs. Facade Grid emits these alongside its points. Vector Offset O Distance to lift each point along its normal before tracing, so the plane it sits on does not occlude itself. Number Sky Bands SB Sky subdivision from zenith to horizon; cell count is about 4πN²/3, so the default 24 is ~2,400 cells. Raise it for a smoother map at proportionally more cost — 24 already sits within 0.02 points of the analytic answer for an open plane. Integer Engine Eng Who traces the sky rays. Auto: the OpenCL GPU when there is one, else the CPU occlusion engine (Embree, or the managed BVH). GPU: the OpenCL GPU; a fallback to the CPU is reported, never silent. CPU: Embree / the managed BVH. Text

docs.title: Output
docs.text: Name Nickname Description Type VSC Vertical Sky Component per point, PERCENT. 39.6 is a fully open vertical plane. Number Colors Col Per-point colours on BR 209's own bands — under 5%, 5-15%, 15-27%, 27% and over — so the guideline reads off the map rather than out of a legend. Colour Report R Range, band counts, rays and the assumptions used. Text

docs.title: ViewFactors - [source code]
docs.text: Configure the view-factor discretization for radiation modeling. OutdoorPlus

docs.title: Input
docs.text: Name Nickname Description Type Domain Sides Coarse Faces SideFaces Number of faces in the coarsest level for domain side walls. Integer Domain Top Coarse Faces TopFaces Number of faces in the coarsest level for the domain top. Integer Terrain Coarse Faces TerrainFaces Number of faces in the coarsest level for terrain. Integer Building Coarse Faces BuildingFaces Number of faces in the coarsest level for buildings. Integer Vegetation Coarse Faces VegFaces Number of faces in the coarsest level for vegetation. Integer

docs.title: Output
docs.text: Name Nickname Description Type View Factor Settings ViewFactors View-factor settings. Generic Data

docs.title: View Target - [source code]
docs.text: Fraction of a target's surface each observer point can see — which seats see the park, which units see the water. The target is sampled by area; rays are blocked by the context and by the target's own body.

docs.title: Input
docs.text: Name Nickname Description Type Context C Obstructing geometry between the observers and the target. Branches are flattened into one scene. The target itself must NOT be wired here. Optional — with nothing wired, only the target's own body occludes (a pure massing/self-occlusion study). Geometry Points P Observer points. Point Target T The geometry whose visibility is being rated. Branches are flattened into one target; it occludes itself, so a solid target's far side reads as hidden. Geometry Target Samples S Points the target is reduced to, allocated by area. More samples resolve partial views more finely; cost is linear per observer. Integer Offset O Clearance around ray endpoints, so observers and samples sitting ON geometry do not block themselves. Number Max Distance D Optional cap in metres — target samples farther than this count as not visible. Number Color Scheme Ramp Colour ramp for the Colors output. Viridis is perceptually uniform and colourblind-safe (use it in a figure); Grayscale suits a monochrome print. Text Engine Eng Who traces the rays. Auto: the OpenCL GPU when there is one, else the CPU. GPU: the OpenCL GPU; a fallback to the CPU is reported, never silent. CPU: the SIMD BVH on every core. Text

docs.title: Output
docs.text: Name Nickname Description Type Visibility V Fraction of the target's samples each observer can see, 0-1. Number Colors Col Point-specific colour ramp over visibility, for a mesh or point preview. Colour Target Points TP The area-weighted sample points the target was reduced to — preview these to judge whether Target Samples is enough. Point Report R Rays traced, samples, and elapsed time. Text

docs.title: Viewshed - [source code]
docs.text: Visual openness by ray casting: the unobstructed fraction of a view cone around each point's normal. A design-orientation tool for seats, windows and routes — how open does it FEEL here — not a daylight metric.

docs.title: Input
docs.text: Name Nickname Description Type Context C Obstructing geometry: buildings, terrain, walls. Meshes, Breps and Surfaces are accepted; branches are flattened into one scene. Geometry Points P Observer points. Point Normals N Optional per-point view directions — the cone axis (e.g. a facade normal, or a seat's facing). Default is straight up, the plan-view openness question. Vector Cone Half-Angle A Half-angle of the view cone in degrees. 60 approximates the human comfortable field of view; 90 is the full hemisphere around the axis. Number Rays R Rays traced per cone. More rays, smoother numbers; cost is linear. Integer Offset O Distance to lift each point along its axis before tracing, so a point sitting ON geometry does not see only itself. Number Max Distance D Optional view distance cap in metres — geometry beyond it counts as OPEN, turning the answer into "openness within this range". Number Color Scheme Ramp Colour ramp for the Colors output. Viridis is perceptually uniform and colourblind-safe (use it in a figure); Grayscale suits a monochrome print. Text Engine Eng Who traces the rays. Auto: the OpenCL GPU when there is one, else the CPU. GPU: the OpenCL GPU; a fallback to the CPU is reported, never silent. CPU: the SIMD BVH on every core. Text

docs.title: Output
docs.text: Name Nickname Description Type Openness Op Unobstructed fraction of each point's view cone, 0-1. Number Colors Col Point-specific colour ramp over openness, for a mesh or point preview. Colour Report R Rays traced, cone directions, and elapsed time. Text Cones VC All view cones joined into ONE mesh (a mesh per point made the canvas crawl), each sector coloured by its point's openness — the axis actually used (including the straight-up fallback for an unusable normal) and the half-angle actually sampled. The surface is TRUNCATED by the context: each direction is drawn to the first building it hits, so the shape shows what the rays saw. Unobstructed directions reach Max Distance when one is set, and otherwise the context's bounding-box diagonal, which is a display length and not a traced distance; the Report says which was used. Mesh

docs.title: Viral Emitter - [source code]
docs.text: An airborne-pathogen passive-scalar source box for an indoor ventilation case. Method: De Simone, Kastner & Dogan (2021), Building Simulation 2021, Bruges, doi:10.26868/25222708.2021.30632.

docs.title: Input
docs.text: Name Nickname Description Type Zone Z Box zone occupied by the viral source. Box Injection Rate IR Viral tracer injection rate, SPECIFIC: per m³ of the zone per second (1/s). The case injects it into the cells whose CENTRES the box contains, so the tracer emitted is rate × the MESHED zone volume, not the drawn box — the case writes that volume (Read Results → viralSourceVolume_0, one per emitter). Number

docs.title: Output
docs.text: Name Nickname Description Type Source S Viral source for the Indoor Case component. Generic Data

docs.title: WRF ABL - [source code]
docs.text: Build an atmospheric boundary layer from a WRF site series. The output plugs into the same socket as Outdoor's ABL, so it drives the wind study, Outdoor+, FluidX3D and LBM alike. Note this is uniform in plan: one log-law profile at the site, not a spatially varying inflow.

docs.title: Input
docs.text: Name Nickname Description Type Series S The site series from WRF Weather. Generic Data Terrain T Aerodynamic roughness of the ground upwind of the site, as a Davenport class. WRF cannot supply this: its own land use describes cells kilometres across, while the CFD domain needs the roughness of the specific approach. Choose Custom to set z0 directly. Text Roughness z0 Aerodynamic roughness length in metres. Used only when Terrain is Custom. Number Ground Height zG Displacement height of the ABL profile, in metres. Number Mode M Average gives one boundary for the whole run — note the direction is a VECTOR mean, since averaging bearings arithmetically makes 350 and 10 degrees come out as 180. Sectors gives one per direction that actually occurred, which is what a multi-direction wind study wants. Hourly gives one per history frame. Text Sectors N How many direction sectors to bin into. Used only in sector mode. Integer

docs.title: Output
docs.text: Name Nickname Description Type Boundary Conditions BC The ABL boundary. Wire to a wind study, Outdoor+, FluidX3D or LBM. Generic Data Wind Vectors V Unit vectors the wind blows TOWARD, one per boundary. Vector Speed U Reference speed at 10 m, one per boundary, m/s. Number Report R One line per boundary. Text

docs.title: WRF Animate - [source code]
docs.text: Loop through a WRF run's history frames while Play is on. Wire Frame into the WRF Probe's Frame input; each tick advances one frame and recomputes the display.

docs.title: Input
docs.text: Name Nickname Description Type Case Folder Dir The case folder — WRF Run's Case Folder output; run_wrf is derived from it (a run_wrf path wired directly still works). Empty uses the document's session case. Text Domain d Which nest's frames to count: 1 for d01, 2 for d02. Integer Play P Loop through the frames while on. Boolean Seconds per Frame s How long each frame stays on screen. Number

docs.title: Output
docs.text: Name Nickname Description Type Frame i The current frame index. Wire into WRF Probe's Frame input. Integer Instant T The current frame's instant, UTC. Text

docs.title: WRF Domain - [source code]
docs.text: Define a WRF domain and the parent grids nested around it. Domains are specified INNERMOST-FIRST: the grid you set here is the finest one, and each nest ratio adds a coarser parent around it. Outputs the project the WRF Namelist component writes, and the domain extents as rectangles centred on the innermost domain.

docs.title: Input
docs.text: Name Nickname Description Type Latitude Lat Latitude of the innermost domain's centre, in decimal degrees (north positive). Number Longitude Lon Longitude of the innermost domain's centre, in decimal degrees (east positive). Number Projection Proj Map projection for the whole domain stack. Lambert conformal suits mid latitudes, Mercator the tropics, Polar the high latitudes, and Lat-Lon is a plain geographic grid whose cell size is in DEGREES rather than metres. Text Cell Size dx Grid spacing of the innermost domain, in metres (or degrees for a Lat-Lon grid). Each parent is this multiplied by the nest ratios. Number Grid X nx Number of cells across the innermost domain in x. May be rounded UP so the grid spans a whole number of parent cells. Integer Grid Y ny Number of cells across the innermost domain in y. May be rounded UP so the grid spans a whole number of parent cells. Integer Nest Ratios R One parent grid per entry, innermost parent first. Each value is how many of the child's cells fit across one of this parent's — WPS supports odd ratios only in practice, and 3 is the usual choice. Clear it for a single domain. Integer Nest Padding P How many of its OWN cells each parent extends beyond its child, on all four sides. One value applies to every parent; a list gives one per parent. Default 5. Integer True Lat 1 T1 First standard parallel, in degrees. Used by Lambert, Mercator and Polar; ignored by Lat-Lon. Number True Lat 2 T2 Second standard parallel, in degrees. Lambert only. Setting it equal to True Lat 1 gives a tangent cone. Number Stand Lon SL Longitude the projection is centred on, in degrees. Leave unwired to follow the domain centre, which is what a single-site study wants. Number Geog Data Res G geog_data_res per domain, innermost-first — the WPS static dataset resolution geogrid reads. One value applies to every domain. Defaults to 'lowres', which is what WRF Geo Data's default download installs; asking for '30s' against a low-res tree fails inside geogrid, minutes into a run. Text

docs.title: Output
docs.text: Name Nickname Description Type Project P The WRF project. Feed this to the WRF Namelist component. Generic Data Domains D Domain extents as rectangles, outermost-first (d01 first, matching the namelist). Drawn in metres about the innermost domain's centre, so the innermost rectangle is centred on the Rhino origin. For a Lat-Lon grid the units are degrees. Curve Summary S One line per domain, d01-first: grid size, spacing, extent and centre. Text

docs.title: WRF Geo Data - [source code]
docs.text: Check and download the WPS static geographical data geogrid needs. Reports what is installed against the mandatory field list, and fetches the bundle that closes the gap.

docs.title: Input
docs.text: Name Nickname Description Type Geog Folder Dir Where the WPS geographical data lives (the WPS_GEOG tree). This is what geog_data_path in namelist.wps points at. Empty uses the shared tree every Eddy3D WRF project reads, so it matches WRF Namelist's Geog Data Path with nothing wired. Text Resolution Res The geog_data_res your namelist uses — 'lowres' or a resolution such as '30s'. Decides which mandatory field list is checked. 'default' means the highest resolution installed. Any other GEOGRID.TBL selector can be typed or wired in. Text Download Get Which archive to fetch. The three bundles carry everything geogrid needs at a given resolution; the individual datasets are extras — NLCD and NUDAPT are the ones worth having for a US urban study. Text Fetch F Download and extract the selected archive. Runs in the background; the canvas stays usable. Boolean

docs.title: Output
docs.text: Name Nickname Description Type Geog Path P The folder, to wire into WRF Namelist's Geog Data Path. Text Ready R True when every mandatory field for the chosen resolution is present. Boolean Status S What is installed, what is missing, and what to download. Text

docs.title: WRF Map - [source code]
docs.text: Lat/lon graticule with labels, the run's own coastline from LANDMASK, and a site marker — in the same plane as the WRF Probe points and WRF Domain rectangles. Wire Labels + Label Points (and Site Label + Site Point) to a Text Tag to draw the annotations.

docs.title: Input
docs.text: Name Nickname Description Type Case Folder Dir The case folder — WRF Run's Case Folder output; run_wrf is derived from it (a run_wrf path wired directly still works). Empty uses the document's session case. Text Domain d Which nest to map: 1 for d01, 2 for d02. Integer Graticule G Spacing of the lat/lon grid in degrees. Empty or 0 picks a round spacing that gives the domain a handful of lines; negative disables the graticule. Number Site Name S Label for the site marker. Empty uses the case folder's name. Text Site Latitude Lat Site latitude in degrees. Defaults to the domain centre. Number Site Longitude Lon Site longitude in degrees. Defaults to the domain centre. Number Z Height Z Height the map lines and labels are drawn at, in metres, so they print above the results underneath. Empty or 0 picks a height from the domain size. Number Line Weight LW Pixel width of the self-drawn border and urban lines; the graticule stays one pixel thinner. The curve outputs are unstyled — weight applies to the viewport drawing. Integer Label Style LS How the labels draw in the viewport. Text is plain 3d text that bakes and exports the way it looks; Bubbles are the classic screen-sized text dots. Text

docs.title: Output
docs.text: Name Nickname Description Type Graticule G Lat/lon grid lines clipped to the domain. Curve Labels L Graticule labels, e.g. 34N or 84.5W, one per label point. Text Label Points LP Anchor for each graticule label, on the domain edge. Point Coastline C The run's own land/water boundary: LANDMASK contoured at 0.5. Curve Site Point SP The site marker position. Point Site Label SL The site marker text. Text Borders B Country and state borders inside the domain, from the embedded Natural Earth base map. Curve Urban Areas U Urban-area outlines inside the domain (Natural Earth 10m urban areas) — the metro footprint, not an administrative city limit. Curve Water W Lakes and ocean coastline inside the domain, from the base map. Curve

docs.title: WRF Met Data - [source code]
docs.text: Download the meteorological GRIB files that drive a WRF run. The file list and the Vtable are shown before you fetch anything, so a window can be checked first.

docs.title: Input
docs.text: Name Nickname Description Type GRIB Folder Dir Where to put the downloaded GRIB files. Wire this to WRF Run's GRIB Folder. Empty uses the grib folder under the resolved case (Working Directory + Case Name), which is where WRF Run looks with nothing wired. Text Source Src Where to fetch from. NOMADS needs no account but keeps only about ten days; AWS Open Data needs no account and holds every GFS cycle from 2021-01-01 (0.25 degree files of 300-550 MB each); RDA has the older archive and needs a free account. Text Start S First instant the run needs, UTC. e.g. 2024-01-15_00:00:00. Defaults to the most recent GFS cycle that has finished posting. Text End E Last instant the run needs, UTC. Defaults to a day after Start. Text Interval I Hours between boundary files. 6 is the usual GFS spacing; 3 gives a smoother forcing and twice the download. Integer Resolution R GFS grid spacing. 0p25 is a quarter degree — the operational default and what you want unless the download is a problem. Text Credential Cr For RDA only. Give the PATH of a file containing your API token, or the NAME of an environment variable holding it — never the value itself. Grasshopper saves a component's text inputs into the .gh document in plain text, so a literal would be published with the definition. Text Working Directory WD The root the case folder sits under when GRIB Folder is empty. Empty uses ~/Eddy3D/WRF. Text Case Name Case The case folder under Working Directory when GRIB Folder is empty. Empty uses the document's session case name — the one WRF Run mints. Text Fetch F Download the files listed above. Runs in the background. Boolean

docs.title: Output
docs.text: Name Nickname Description Type GRIB Folder P The folder, to wire into WRF Run. Text Vtable V The ungrib variable table this product needs. Wire to WRF Run's Vtable. Text Files Fs The files that make up this window. Text Status St What will be fetched, and what happened. Text

docs.title: WRF Namelist - [source code]
docs.text: Write namelist.wps for a WRF project. The text is produced on every solve; the Write toggle saves it to /run_wps/namelist.wps.

docs.title: Input
docs.text: Name Nickname Description Type Working Directory Dir The root the case folder sits under; namelist.wps is written to //run_wps/. Empty uses ~/Eddy3D/WRF and the document's session case name — the same folder WRF Run resolves, so the two agree with nothing wired. A full project path with an empty Case Name is used as-is. Text Project P The WRF project from the WRF Domain component. Generic Data Geog Data Path G Folder holding the WPS static geographical data (the WPS_GEOG extract). Defaults to the shared tree WRF Geo Data downloads into. Clear it and the namelist carries a placeholder path that geogrid will reject — deliberately, so an unconfigured run fails at once rather than halfway through. Text Start S Start of the simulated period, UTC. Accepts '2024-01-15_00:00:00', '2024-01-15 00:00' or '2024-01-15'. Defaults to the most recent GFS cycle that has finished posting — the same default WRF Met Data uses. Text End E End of the simulated period, UTC. Same formats as Start. Defaults to a day after Start. Text Interval I Seconds between the driving meteorological files. 21600 (6 h) matches GFS and most reanalyses; 10800 (3 h) matches the higher-frequency products. Integer Case Name Case The case folder under Working Directory. Empty uses the document's session case name — the one WRF Run mints. Text Write W Write namelist.wps to disk. Resets itself after one write. Boolean

docs.title: Output
docs.text: Name Nickname Description Type Namelist N The generated namelist.wps. Text Path Pa Where the namelist was written, or would be written. Text

docs.title: WRF Probe - [source code]
docs.text: Sample a surface field of a WRF run over the whole domain, one point per grid cell. Points are in metres about the domain centre, matching the WRF Domain rectangles. Wire Points + Values into the Scalar Field Viewer, or Points + Vectors into the Vector Field Viewer, for the display.

docs.title: Input
docs.text: Name Nickname Description Type Case Folder Dir The case folder — WRF Run's Case Folder output; run_wrf is derived from it (a run_wrf path wired directly still works). Empty uses the document's session case. Text Domain d Which nest to sample: 1 for d01, 2 for d02. Integer Field F What to sample at every cell. Wind also fills the Vectors output; the temperatures are converted from Kelvin; rain is RAINC + RAINNC since the run start. Custom reads the Variable input as a raw wrfout dataset name. Text Variable V Raw wrfout dataset name, used only when Field is Custom. It must be a 2-D surface field (south_north x west_east). Text Frame i Which history frame to sample: 0 for the first, -1 for the last. Integer

docs.title: Output
docs.text: Name Nickname Description Type Points P One point per grid cell centre, metres about the domain centre, z = 0. Point Values N The sampled field, one value per point, in the field's stated unit. Number Vectors V 10 m wind vectors, one per point, m/s — only for the wind field. Vector Report R What was sampled: file, frame instant, grid size, and the value range. Text Mesh M A quad mesh over the grid, one vertex per cell centre in the same order as Points and Values — color it by Values (or let Flex Legend do it) for a heatmap. Mesh

docs.title: WRF Progress - [source code]
docs.text: Progress of the WRF pipeline in the working directory, with an expected time to completion once wrf.exe is stepping. Toggle Live to re-poll once a second.

docs.title: Input
docs.text: Name Nickname Description Type Case Folder Dir The case folder — WRF Run's Case Folder output, the one holding run_wps and run_wrf. Empty uses the document's session case, the same folder WRF Run resolves. Text Live L Re-poll the run once a second while on. Boolean

docs.title: Output
docs.text: Name Nickname Description Type Progress P 0 to 1 across the whole pipeline, weighted so wrf.exe owns 80 % of the bar. Number Phase Ph The step currently running: geogrid, ungrib, metgrid, real, wrf, done or failed. Text Done D True once SUCCESS COMPLETE WRF is in the log and wrfout files exist. Boolean Status St One line: phase, percentage, and the expected time to completion when known. Text

docs.title: WRF Run - [source code]
docs.text: Run the WRF pipeline in the two launches it needs: the WPS half (geogrid, ungrib, metgrid), then run_wrf/namelist.input, built from that output, then the WRF half (real, wrf). Writes one script per launch into the project folder. The scripts and commands are always shown, even before you run, so a failing run can be reproduced by hand.

docs.title: Input
docs.text: Name Nickname Description Type Working Directory Dir The root the case folder sits under; the case itself is /. Empty uses ~/Eddy3D/WRF. A full project path with an empty Case Name is used as-is, which is what older definitions wire. Text WRF Distribution WRF Folder the WRF distribution is unpacked into — its main/ holds real.exe and wrf.exe. Leave empty on the Container engine: the published image carries its own, and a folder given here is mounted OVER it. Text WPS Distribution WPS Folder the WPS distribution is unpacked into. Leave empty on the Container engine — the published image carries its own. Text GRIB Folder G Folder of GRIB files to link as GRIBFILE.AAA, AAB, ... for ungrib. Auto uses the grib folder under the case — where WRF Met Data downloads with nothing wired. Clear it if they are already linked, or if you are running the WRF half only. Text Vtable V The ungrib variable table for your meteorological product. The list is every table the shipped WPS carries; a table you added yourself can be typed or wired in. Vtable.GFS is what WRF Met Data downloads for. Text Engine E Which backend runs WRF. Auto picks the first that works here, preferring WSL. Native needs the WRF-CMake Windows build and MS-MPI. Container runs the published Eddy3D image through Docker or Podman, and is the only backend on macOS. Text Image Img Container image, when the engine is Container. Auto uses the published Eddy3D image matching this machine's architecture; pull it from the Eddy3D Setup window. A third-party image can be typed or wired in — one without Eddy3D's version marker keeps the mount-the-host-distributions behaviour. Text Ranks N MPI ranks for wrf.exe. Only wrf.exe uses more than one: ungrib has no MPI build, and geogrid, metgrid and real are pinned to a single rank because their netCDF-4 output is not reliable in parallel. Integer Steps S Which half to run. Everything runs the WPS half, builds run_wrf/namelist.input from its output (WRF's own physics kept), then runs the WRF half. WPS output does not change unless the domains or the met data do, so re-running the WRF half alone is the normal edit-and-retry loop: it uses the namelist.input in run_wrf exactly as you left it (time step, physics, run length), and only builds one when there is none. Time Step and History Interval, when set, are the exception: they are written into that file. Text Case Name Case The case folder under Working Directory. Empty mints a friendly session name once per document — the same name every other WRF component resolves — and keeps it with the saved document. Text Time Step Step Model time step [s], written to namelist.input as time_step (1 to 3600). 0 or empty derives it from the grid: 6 s per km of the outermost domain's spacing, divided by the largest map factor when that exceeds 1. WRF stops with a CFL error on a step the grid cannot take, so pin a shorter one to retry. With Steps set to WRF only, the value is also written into the run_wrf/namelist.input already there; with 0 that file is used exactly as you left it. Integer History Interval History Minutes between history frames [min], one wrfout file per frame, written as history_interval for every domain (1 to 1440). 0 or empty keeps the base namelist's, which is hourly in WRF's own example. With Steps set to WRF only, the value is also written into the run_wrf/namelist.input already there; with 0 that file is used exactly as you left it. Integer Run R Launch the run. The script is written and shown regardless. Boolean

docs.title: Output
docs.text: Name Nickname Description Type Script Sc The generated run script. Text Command C The command that launches it, as it would be typed. Text Status St What the engine is, what it will run, and what happened. Text Case Folder Out The resolved case folder. Feed to WRF Weather, Probe, Map, Animate and Progress — each derives its run_wrf from it. Text

docs.title: WRF Weather - [source code]
docs.text: Read a WRF run at a site and build the weather an Eddy3D case needs. Feed the Weather output to Timing Parameters and urbanMicroclimateFoam runs on WRF instead of an EPW. Start HOY and Duration describe the window the run actually covers — wire them too, because every hour outside it is deliberately NaN and will stop OpenFOAM rather than quietly simulate a day of 0 degC.

docs.title: Input
docs.text: Name Nickname Description Type Case Folder Dir The case folder — WRF Run's Case Folder output; run_wrf is derived from it (a run_wrf path wired directly still works). Empty uses the document's session case. Text Domain d Which nest to read: 1 for d01, 2 for d02. The innermost domain that covers your site is usually the one you want. Integer Latitude Lat Site latitude in decimal degrees. The nearest WRF cell centre answers. Number Longitude Lon Site longitude in decimal degrees. Number Time Zone TZ Standard-time offset from UTC, in hours. Leave unwired to derive it from longitude, which is right to within an hour almost everywhere and wrong at every political zone boundary. WRF writes UTC; this is only used to place the hours in the year. Number Solar Split Sp How to split WRF's global horizontal irradiance into beam and diffuse. This is a MODELLING CHOICE, not a conversion: urbanMicroclimateFoam consumes IDN and Idif separately and they drive surface temperatures differently. Erbs (1982) is the standard hourly correlation. WRF's own diagnostics are exact but exist only when the run enabled them; the component falls back to Erbs and says so. Text Cloud Cover Cl How to obtain sky cover for 0/air/cloudCover. The clearness index inverts Kasten-Czeplak on the ratio of WRF's SWDOWN to a clear sky — it works with the fields every run writes but is blind at night, where the nearest daylight value is carried across. CLDFRA is available only when the run wrote it. Text

docs.title: Output
docs.text: Name Nickname Description Type Weather W The weather. Wire this to Timing Parameters' Weather input. Generic Data Start HOY H Hour of year of the run's first hour. Wire to Timing Parameters' Hour of Year. Integer Duration D How many hours the run covers. Wire to Timing Parameters' Duration. Integer Series S The extracted site series. Feed to WRF ABL, or deconstruct it. Generic Data Report R What was read, which cell answered, and which methods actually ran. Text

docs.title: Water Surface - [source code]
docs.text: Coupled evaporating water surface for urbanMicroclimateFoam. The water geometry becomes a named air patch that exchanges sensible heat and moisture with the air; water motion and a moving free surface are not solved. Requires an UMF build that includes the simpleWater model.

docs.title: Input
docs.text: Name Nickname Description Type Water Surface Surface Planar or meshed water surface. It should coincide with an exposed terrain/ground boundary; model terrain with an opening beneath the water when possible. Geometry Mixed Depth Depth Effective thermally mixed water depth in metres. Number Albedo Short-wave reflectivity of the water surface (0–1). Number Emissivity Long-wave emissivity of the water surface (0–1). Number Aerodynamic Resistance Resistance Surface aerodynamic resistance in s/m. Use -1 to derive it from local wind speed. Number Refinement Level Refine SnappyHexMesh refinement level at the water surface. Integer

docs.title: Output
docs.text: Name Nickname Description Type Water Settings Water Connect directly to the Water Surface input on Outdoor+ Case. Generic Data

docs.title: Watertight - [source code]
docs.text: Combine a multi-part building mesh into a single watertight, CFD-ready solid via the bundled Python mesh service (trimesh/manifold3d/pymeshfix). The server auto-starts locally on the first run (uv-managed Python environment; first start installs it, 1-2 minutes) and is reused afterwards.

docs.title: Input
docs.text: Name Nickname Description Type Mesh M Input meshes (merged and combined into one solid). Mesh Min Length L Vertex weld tolerance in model units. Two vertices closer than this are merged. Default 0.1 (10 cm for meter-unit models). Number API URL URL MetaBlock API base URL. Text Run Process the mesh — auto-starts the local server on first run. Resets when the result arrives. Boolean

docs.title: Output
docs.text: Name Nickname Description Type Combined M Combined watertight CFD-ready solid mesh. Mesh Status S Status message. Text

docs.title: Weather - [source code]
docs.text: Read an EPW file and create a Weather object for the simulation. OutdoorPlus

docs.title: Input
docs.text: Name Nickname Description Type EPW File Path Path Full path to the EPW weather file. Text

docs.title: Output
docs.text: Name Nickname Description Type Weather Weather object containing EPW data. Generic Data

docs.title: Wind Climate - [source code]
docs.text: Long-term directional wind statistics for pedestrian comfort: for every direction sector (36 × 10° by default) and season (year + Dec-Feb, Mar-May, Jun-Aug, Sep-Nov, named for the hemisphere), the sector probability, the calm share and a Weibull c, k fitted by maximum likelihood to the non-calm hours of a MULTI-YEAR record — ERA5 via Open-Meteo (any coordinate, no key), the nearest NOAA ISD or GHCNh station, local EPW files or a CSV — or the City of London Annex A table. A typical year cannot carry a safety criterion: Lawson's 15 m/s for 0.022 % of the year is about two hours, and a TMY holds two hours of one composite year. Wire the Wind Climate output into Pedestrian Wind Comfort (with VAF's Speed Ratios) to classify from P(U > u) = Σ p·exp(−(u/(r·c))^k); the report says whether the record is long enough to measure the safety tail. Downloads run off the canvas and are cached per year in WeatherCache/WindRecords inside the Eddy3D folder of your local app data.Sources: ERA5 (Hersbach et al. 2020, Copernicus C3S) via Open-Meteo; NOAA NCEI Integrated Surface Database (ISD-Lite) and its successor GHCNh; City of London Wind Microclimate Guidelines (2019), Annex A.

docs.title: Input
docs.text: Name Nickname Description Type Source Src Where the wind comes from. ERA5 (Open-Meteo): hourly 10 m reanalysis for the 0.25° cell at Latitude/Longitude, open-terrain exposure. ISD station (NOAA): the nearest station within 100 km covering half the years (or the one named in Station); NOAA stopped updating ISD-Lite in August 2025. GHCNh station (NOAA): its successor, current to the day before, for 2000 onward — the nearest station within 100 km that measures wind (screened on the last year), or the one named in Station; 12-34 MB a station-year, read once and kept as a small file. EPW files / CSV file: the paths in Files. City of London Annex A: the guideline's published table (c at 120 m, terrain-corrected for the City — not valid elsewhere). Global Wind Atlas (.lib file): a generalized wind climate you downloaded from globalwindatlas.info, path in Files — the class nearest Source Terrain's roughness length, at Reference Height (between the file's heights, linear in ln z; outside them it refuses). It is the wind over FLAT terrain of that roughness, not the local wind, and it has no seasons. Text Latitude Lat Site latitude (°). Optional when Location carries one. Number Longitude Lon Site longitude (°). Optional when Location carries one. Number Location Loc Optional: a Wind Conditions record (its site, else its station, gives the coordinates; its EPW is used for the EPW source) or an EPW path (its header's coordinates). Generic Data Files EPW paths (each file is one year-block) for the EPW source, or one CSV path for the CSV source: UTC time (ISO 8601), speed m/s, direction ° from north, optional gust. Text Years Years to fetch for ERA5 / ISD / GHCNh (GHCNh from 2000), as "1995-2024" or one year. 20-30 years is the usual record for a safety tail; each year is one request, cached on disk. Text Station Stn ISD: pin a station by USAF-WBAN (e.g. 037720-99999, London Heathrow). GHCNh: its 11-character GHCN id (e.g. USW00014739, Boston Logan) or an ISD id with a WBAN number. Empty = nearest. Text Sectors N Direction sectors, centred on north: 36 = 10° (City of London / ESDU), 16 = 22.5°. Integer Calm Threshold Calm Speeds below this (m/s) are calm — their own category, never a sector (an EPW or ISD calm carries direction 0, which would otherwise spike the north sector). The Weibull fits are truncated here. Number Source Terrain SrcTerr EN 1991-1-4 category the SOURCE speeds stand for. II (open country) for ERA5 — ECMWF brings its 10 m wind down with a short-grass roughness of 0.03 m — and for a WMO-sited anemometer. Change it when the station is known to stand elsewhere. Text Site Terrain SiteTerr EN 1991-1-4 category around the SITE: every speed is transferred by c_r,site/c_r,source at the Reference Height (the same factor Wind Conditions applies). 'None' keeps the source's speeds — then the ABL inlet should also be the source's terrain. Text Reference Height Zref Height (m) of the transfer, and the height the climate's speeds then describe — the ABL reference height, 10 m for a standard anemometer. The comfort classifier re-references the CFD ratios to it. Number Fetch Download the years not yet cached (ERA5 / ISD / GHCNh). Local files and fully cached records build without it; a failed fetch stays reported until you press Fetch again or change the location. Boolean

docs.title: Output
docs.text: Name Nickname Description Type Wind Climate Climate The climate object — for Pedestrian Wind Comfort's Wind Climate input and the CLI (its JSON is what E3D wind-climate --out writes). Generic Data Directions Dir Sector centres (° from north, wind FROM). Number Probabilities p Annual share of all hours per sector (%); with the calm share they sum to 100. Number Weibull c c Annual Weibull scale per sector (m/s, after any transfer). Number Weibull k k Annual Weibull shape per sector. Number Calm Annual calm share (%). Number Sector Table Table The annual sector table as Markdown (p, hours, mean, max, c, k, fit). Text Report Origin, per-year completeness, exposure, transfer, every season's table, and whether the record is long enough to measure a 0.022 % safety tail. Text Rose Frequencies Rose Wind-rose petals: {sector}[speed band] annual frequency (%) from the fitted Weibulls, bands as in Rose Bands. Number Rose Bands Bands Speed-band labels for Rose Frequencies (m/s). Text

docs.title: Wind Comfort Compare - [source code]
docs.text: Compares pedestrian wind comfort between schemes — existing (baseline), proposed and optionally mitigated — at the same probe points: per-probe class transition, change in exceedance hours, suitability for the intended use, the City of London significance grade (on-site / off-site receptor tables: negligible, moderate or major, beneficial or adverse, and whether mitigation is required), Wellington WIND-S2 (no increase in hours at or above 2.5 m/s against the existing scheme), and count- or area-weighted summaries. Probes are matched by position; the Comparison output feeds Study Report.

docs.title: Input
docs.text: Name Nickname Description Type Existing Ex Baseline scheme's annual Wind Speed field (Velocity Amplification Factors) — the existing site the others are compared against. Generic Data Proposed Pr Proposed scheme's annual Wind Speed field, at the same probe points. Generic Data Mitigated Mi Optional mitigated scheme's annual Wind Speed field. When wired, the significance and suitability outputs grade the mitigated scheme against the existing one. Generic Data Comfort Metric Metric Comfort criterion — the Pedestrian Wind Comfort vocabulary; City Lawson (CoL 2019) by default, whose significance tables the grading follows. Text Criteria Optional Wind Comfort Criteria object; replaces the Comfort Metric pick. Generic Data Intended Use Use Optional intended pedestrian use — one for every probe or one per existing probe. A named use of the criterion (City Lawson: frequent sitting, occasional sitting, standing / entrance / bus stop, walking / pavement, service, cyclist), or a class letter ('C' = at most class C). Needed for suitability and most significance grades. Text Receptor Rec Optional 'on-site' or 'off-site' (default) — one for every probe or one per existing probe. On-site receptors are graded against the intended use only; off-site against the existing scheme too (City of London Wind Microclimate Guidelines 2019). Text Weights Area Optional area per existing probe — makes the summaries area-weighted instead of counting probes. Number Existing Gust ExG Optional Gust Speed field of the existing scheme (VAF, needs TKE). Without it gust-derived classes use mean × Gust Factor. Generic Data Proposed Gust PrG Optional Gust Speed field of the proposed scheme. Generic Data Mitigated Gust MiG Optional Gust Speed field of the mitigated scheme. Generic Data Gust Factor G 3-second gust / hourly mean ratio used where no gust field is wired (default 1.85). Number Match Tolerance Tol Distance (model units) within which a probe of one scheme is the same receptor as a probe of the existing scheme. Identical point lists match by index; otherwise the nearest point within this distance, and probes with none are left out and counted. Number

docs.title: Output
docs.text: Name Nickname Description Type Class Change dC Per existing probe: compared class number minus existing class number (+ = windier by that many classes, 0 = same, - = calmer). 0 for probes left out. Integer Transition T Per probe, e.g. 'B → D (+2)'; empty for probes left out. Text Delta Hours dH Per probe: change in hours above the threshold of the intended use's class (the criterion's most lenient comfortable class when no use is given). Integer Suitable OK Per probe: whether the compared scheme is suitable for the intended use (safe and no windier than the use allows); false where no use was given. Boolean Significance Sig Per probe: City of London significance — Major/Moderate Beneficial, Negligible, Moderate/Major Adverse, or 'Not covered' / 'Not graded' where the tables say nothing. Text Mitigation Required Mit Per probe: the City of London tables require mitigation (on-site Moderate/Major Adverse, off-site Major Adverse). Boolean WIND-S2 S2 Per probe: Wellington WIND-S2 — the compared scheme does not increase the hours with hourly mean at or above 2.5 m/s against the existing one. Boolean Change Colors CC Per probe colour of the class change: greens calmer, grey unchanged, oranges to reds windier, dark red for a newly unsafe probe; light grey for probes left out. Colour Significance Colors SC Per probe colour of the significance grade. Colour Summary Sum Count- or area-weighted summary lines. Text Comparison Cmp The comparison object — wire it into Study Report. Generic Data

docs.title: Wind Comfort Criteria - [source code]
docs.text: Builds a pedestrian wind-comfort criterion from lists — one class per item, best (most comfortable) first — so a jurisdiction's own standard can be classified without shipping code. Each class is a speed threshold, the share of the year it may be exceeded, an operator (< comfort class achieved when exceeded LESS than the share; > / >= hazard class tripped when exceeded MORE), and whether it reads the hourly mean or the 3-second gust. Wire the Criteria output into Pedestrian Wind Comfort or Study Report. Pick a Preset to start from a shipped table (e.g. Wellington) and edit it.

docs.title: Input
docs.text: Name Nickname Description Type Preset Optional shipped criterion to start from. Its rows are used wherever the lists below are empty, and echoed on the Table output so they can be copied and edited. Text Name Name of the criterion, shown on the comfort component's banner and in reports. Text Speed U Speed threshold per class (m/s), best class first. Number Exceedance % Share of the period the threshold may be exceeded, per class, in PERCENT (5 = 5 %). 0 means never (an annual maximum). Number Activity Act Activity / class description per class ("Sitting", "Unsafe"). Text Letter L Class letter per class (A, B, …, S). Defaults to A, B, C… when empty. Text Operator Op Per class: < (comfort class, achieved when the exceedance stays BELOW the share), > or >= (hazard class, tripped when the exceedance is ABOVE the share). Defaults to <. Text Reference Ref Per class: Hourly mean (default) or Gust — the 3-second gust series from the comfort component's Gust Speed input or its Gust Factor fallback. Text Source Src Optional citation of the standard the table comes from. Text

docs.title: Output
docs.text: Name Nickname Description Type Criteria The criterion object for Pedestrian Wind Comfort / Study Report. Generic Data Table One line per class, for a panel. Text

docs.title: Wind Comfort Predictor (ML) - [source code]
docs.text: Calculate Pedestrian Wind Comfort using predicted wind fields from the ONNX model. ML screening prediction, not CFD: use it to compare options, then confirm anything that matters with a Wind Study (planning authorities do not accept surrogate results). Method: Kastner et al. (2026), SSRN preprint 6401886, doi:10.2139/ssrn.6401886.

docs.title: Input
docs.text: Name Nickname Description Type Points Pts Analysis points for mesh visualization. Point Wind Speeds U Predicted wind speeds (m/s) as a DataTree from WindPredictor. Number EPW Path EPW Path to the .epw weather file. Text Reference Height zRef Reference height for the simulations (m). Default = 10.0 Number Roughness Length (z0) z0 Roughness length (m). Default = 1.0 Number Metric Comfort metric to use. Text Interpolate Interp Interpolate between wind directions. Default = true Text Fast Mode (MoM) Fast Use Method of Moments for ultra-fast Weibull estimation. Default = true Text Boundary Conditions BC Optional simulation metadata to automate zRef, z0, and Uref (sim). Generic Data TKE k Turbulent kinetic energy (m²/s²) as a DataTree from WindPredictor. When provided, GEM (Gust Equivalent Mean) is used: GEM = U + g × √(2k/3). Peak factor g is auto-set per metric. Number Wind Speeds (Roof) Wroof Optional roof-level wind speeds (m/s) DataTree. Number TKE (Roof) kroof Optional roof-level TKE (m²/s²) DataTree. Number Buildings Optional list of Brep or Mesh objects representing buildings. Needed to elevate roof-level comfort meshes to correct heights. Geometry

docs.title: Output
docs.text: Name Nickname Description Type Comfort Rank Rank Wind comfort rank (integer). Number Class Letter Letter Wind comfort class letter (e.g., A, B, C). Text Class Wind comfort class description. Text Comfort Mesh M Colored mesh representing comfort levels. Mesh Legend Mesh LM Legend mesh for comfort categories. Mesh Legend Points LP Label points for the legend letters. Point Legend Letters LV Letters (A-S) for the legend. Text Metric Name MetricName The name of the currently active comfort/safety standard. Text Category Explanations Explanations Detailed descriptions for each class (e.g., A: Sitting Long). Text Comfort Rank (Roof) RankRoof Wind comfort rank (integer) for roof level. Number Class Letter (Roof) LetterRoof Wind comfort class letter for roof level. Text Class (Roof) ClassRoof Wind comfort class description for roof level. Text

docs.title: Wind Compass - [source code]
docs.text: Visualize a wind direction on a compass circle. Direction is meteorological degrees (0=N, 90=E, 180=S, 270=W); outputs the flow vector and the 16-point cardinal name.

docs.title: Input
docs.text: Name Nickname Description Type Wind Direction Dir Wind direction in degrees (0=N, 90=E, 180=S, 270=W). Number Radius Rad Radius of the compass circle. Number Base Point Pt Center of the compass. Point Color Col Display color. Colour Arrow Scale Scale Scale of the directional arrow. Number Weather Optional Eddy3D Weather object. When connected, replaces the direction arrow with a 16-sector wind rose over Start–End Month (whole year by default). Radial length is occurrence frequency and stacked colors are wind-speed ranges in m/s. Generic Data Start Month StartMonth First month [1-12] of the hours the wind rose counts. Integer End Month EndMonth Last month [1-12] of the hours the wind rose counts, inclusive. Earlier than Start Month wraps the year end: Start 11, End 2 is November to February. Integer

docs.title: Output
docs.text: Name Nickname Description Type Vector Vec Wind direction (flow) vector. Vector Direction Name Name 16-point cardinal name (e.g. NNE). Text

docs.title: Wind Conditions - [source code]
docs.text: Bin a year of EPW wind into direction sectors — frequency, speed histogram, mean speed and a Weibull fit per sector — with the station's origin (provider, id, period, coordinates, elevation) and the site's location in one record. Optionally transfers the station's speeds to the site's terrain per EN 1991-1-4 (the anemometer stands in open country; the site does not). Wire the record into the ABL component's Wind Directions: it supplies directions AND speeds, travels into the study manifest and the Study Report, and lets VAF scale the hourly series by the same factor.

docs.title: Input
docs.text: Name Nickname Description Type EPW Path to the EPW weather file (Download Weather's EPW output). Text Sectors N Direction sectors around the compass; 16 = 22.5° sectors centred on the compass points (N, NNE, …). 8 and 36 are the other common choices. Integer Solve Sectors Solve How many sectors to SIMULATE. 0 or ≥ Sectors solves every sector; a divisor of Sectors takes every k-th (8 of 16 = the 45° compass); anything else takes the most frequent. The Directions/Speeds outputs and the ABL follow this choice; the record keeps every sector for the report. Integer Calm Threshold Calm Speeds below this (m/s) are calm: no usable direction, excluded from the sectors and reported as the calm share. Number Site Terrain SiteTerr EN 1991-1-4 terrain category around the SITE. Set it to transfer the station's speeds to the site: every sector speed is multiplied by c_r,site(z)/c_r,station(z) at the reference height (§4.3: c_r = k_r·ln(z/z0), k_r = 0.19·(z0/0.05)^0.07). Category IV at 10 m is ×0.54 of open country — an urban inlet fed the raw station speed overstates every pedestrian wind by nearly two. 'None' keeps the station's speeds. Text Station Terrain StTerr EN 1991-1-4 Table 4.1 terrain category around the STATION's anemometer. WMO exposure is open country — category II — which is the default and the right answer for nearly every airport TMY. Only read when Site Terrain is set. Text Reference Height Zref Height (m) the transfer is evaluated at — the ABL reference height, 10 m for a standard anemometer. Number Site Latitude Lat Optional site latitude (°), recorded with the study and reported with the station distance. Number Site Longitude Lng Optional site longitude (°). Number Site Elevation Elev Optional site elevation above sea level (m). Recorded beside the station's so a reader can judge whether the station represents the site. Number Speed Ratios Ratios Optional: the Speed Ratios object a solved study emits (Velocity Amplification Factors). With it, Critical Sectors ranks the sectors by what the SITE exceeds under them; without it the ranking is the station's own (every ratio 1), the prior before any CFD has run. Generic Data Threshold Thresh Speed (m/s, hourly mean at the reference height) whose exceedance ranks the sectors — the comfort criterion's threshold, e.g. 5 (NEN 8100 / Lawson walking). Default 5. Number

docs.title: Output
docs.text: Name Nickname Description Type Wind Conditions WC The record — wire into the ABL component's Wind Directions (and into VAF's Wind Conditions when a transfer is applied). Generic Data Directions Dirs Solved sector directions (° from north, wind-from). Number Speeds U Mean speed per solved sector (m/s) at the reference height, after any transfer. Number Frequencies Freq Share of non-calm hours per solved sector (%). Number Weibull k k Weibull shape per solved sector (dimensionless; NaN when a sector had too few hours). Number Weibull λ λ Weibull scale per solved sector (m/s), after any transfer. Number Report The sector table and origin as Markdown. Text Critical Sectors Critical Every sector's direction (° from north), ranked by its share of the year the site spends above Threshold: sector frequency × P(site speed > Threshold | that sector), the term the probabilistic comfort classifier sums. The top of the list is where a scale-resolving (DES) solve earns its cost; the rest can stay steady RANS. Number Critical Shares Share Each ranked sector's share (0-1) of the total exceedance, in the order of Critical Sectors. Number

docs.title: Wind Flowlines - [source code]
docs.text: Record wind flowlines through an LBM case's velocity frames (or a steady Points + Vectors field), save the recording in the case folder, and play it back. Each emitter releases particles evenly in time; when the wind direction turns past the restart angle the lines start again from the emitters. Playback restyles with Range and Thickness without re-tracing.

docs.title: Input
docs.text: Name Nickname Description Type Case LBM case folder (OpenLB or FluidX3D). The recording is written here as flowlines.e3dflow, and played back from here. Text Emitters Points the flowlines start from. Divide a curve for an even rake. Point Points Optional steady field: sample points (e.g. an OpenFOAM result or LBM Field). Wired with Vectors, it replaces the case's VTK frames and records one frame. Point Vectors Velocity per point (m/s), pairing 1:1 with Points. Vector Time Step Step Seconds between particle releases (and integration step). Point spacing along a line is speed x step. Number Line Points Length Particles kept per line; a line spans Line Points x Time Step seconds of travel. Integer Restart Angle Restart Degrees the mean wind direction at the emitters must turn between frames before every line restarts from its emitter. Number Frame Recorded frame to show (0-based). While Play is on, playback starts here. Integer Play Loop through the recorded frames at 10 frames per second. Boolean Range Speed range (m/s) the colours span. Unset: the recording's own range. Domain Thickness Line thickness in the viewport, in pixels. Integer Record Trace the flowlines through every frame and save the recording. Playback needs no Record. Boolean

docs.title: Output
docs.text: Name Nickname Description Type Flowlines Lines The shown frame's flowlines. Curve Speeds Speed (m/s) at each flowline point, one branch per line. Number Frame Index of the shown frame. Integer Frame Count Count Frames in the recording. Integer Time Solver time of the shown frame (s); empty for a steady frame. Number Range Speed range used for the colours, for a legend. Domain File The recording file. Text

docs.title: Wind Predictor - [source code]
docs.text: Run ONNX wind-field prediction end-to-end. Computes SDF, building height, Zrelative, U/Uref, direction features from geometry, assembles the 8-channel input tensor, runs ONNX inference, and outputs predicted wind speeds. Supports legacy 1ch (U), 2ch (U + k) and new 4ch (U + k + Uroof + kroof) models. ML screening prediction, not CFD: use it to compare options, then confirm anything that matters with a Wind Study (planning authorities do not accept surrogate results). Check a result with Prediction Confidence and Verify Prediction. Method: Kastner et al. (2026), SSRN preprint 6401886, doi:10.2139/ssrn.6401886.

docs.title: Input
docs.text: Name Nickname Description Type Points List of 3D points. Each point's Z must be absolute elevation (m). Point Buildings List of Brep or Mesh objects representing buildings. Geometry Model Full file path to the ONNX model. Connect the FilePath output from the ML Model component. Text Boundary Conditions BC Boundary conditions from the ABL or Uniform Flow component. Uref, zRef, z0, wind directions, and EPW path are extracted automatically. Generic Data Pedestrian Level PedLevel Pedestrian mount height (m). Default = 1.8 Number Filter Margin FiltMargin Margin (in meters) to mask out from the outer perimeter of the prediction plane due to unstable boundary effects. Default = 100.0 Number Palette Color palette for visualization. Text Legend Domain Domain Optional custom domain [min, max] to lock the color bounds. If empty, the colors scale dynamically to the data. Domain Interpolate Interp Visualization style. Flat (pixelated) vs Smooth (interpolated colors). Text Field Field to visualize. Affects M, LM, LP, LV outputs. Text Level Visualization level. Roof Level only applies when a 4-channel model is loaded. Text Selection Points SelectPts Optional locations to output. The model still runs on all input Points; each selection receives the result of its nearest input sensor, in selection order. Point Radius Marker size (m): circle radius or square half-width. Number Legend Scale LegScale Uniform scale factor for the legend bar and label spacing. Number Mesh Type MeshType Prediction marker topology. Square uses one quad per point and is fastest; Circle uses a 16-sided n-gon. Text Engine Eng Who measures the SDF and building-height grid the model reads (not the inference provider — that is the right-click menu). Auto (the default): the OpenCL GPU when every building is a mesh or a Brep with only planar faces, where it measures exactly what Rhino does; the CPU otherwise (curved faces, or no GPU), and the Remark says which. GPU: the OpenCL GPU on every building, curved ones on their render mesh; a fallback to the CPU is reported, never silent. CPU: Rhino's Brep rule on every core, the one the model was trained on. Text Run Sticky on/off switch for the prediction (a toggle, not a momentary button). On: every input change re-runs inference. Off: inference is skipped and the last result stays on the outputs, so the canvas can be rewired without paying for a solve. A wired boolean works the same as the inline switch. Boolean

docs.title: Output
docs.text: Name Nickname Description Type Points Pts The location of each predicted value, in Values order, at the input points' own height: the input Points, or the Selection Points when those are wired. Point Values V Predicted field values at each valid input point. Outputs wind speed (m/s) or turbulent kinetic energy (m²/s²) depending on the Field input. Branches represent different wind directions. Number Grid Mesh M A fast-rendering contiguous coloured preview mesh of the predictions. Mesh Legend Mesh LM A colored mesh strip acting as a visual legend. Mesh Legend Points LP Locations for the legend text in the 3D viewport (Generic type to prevent red cross preview). Generic Data Legend Values LV Text values corresponding to the generated legend. Text Boundary Conditions BC Automated simulation boundary conditions metadata. Generic Data Values (Roof) Vroof Predicted roof-level field values at each valid input point. Outputs wind speed or TKE depending on the Field input. Branches represent different wind directions. Empty unless a 4-channel model is used. Number

docs.title: Wind Predictor (Cloud) - [source code]
docs.text: Predict a pedestrian wind-speed field from buildings without running CFD, using the hosted Eddy3D model (Yel 1.0, a 512x512 image GAN). Rasterizes the buildings and the analysis plane into the model's input image, sends it to the API, and returns the predicted wind speeds plus a colored result mesh. Runs on Eddy3D's server: needs internet, no GPU and no model download, and the free server may need a minute to wake up. For a local GPU run over arbitrary points and multiple wind directions, use Wind Predictor with a model from ML Model instead. ML screening prediction, not CFD: use it to compare options, then confirm anything that matters with a Wind Study (planning authorities do not accept surrogate results). Method: Kastner & Dogan (2023), Building and Environment 242:110384, doi:10.1016/j.buildenv.2023.110384.

docs.title: Input
docs.text: Name Nickname Description Type Buildings B Building meshes. Mesh Analysis Plane Pl Square analysis plane (defaults to a 512x512 box around the buildings). Rectangle Wind Direction Dir Wind direction in degrees (0=N, clockwise). Integer API URL URL Prediction API base URL. Text Voxel Size V Geometry rasterization voxel size (m). Number Color Size CS Distance (m) at which the input image's open-ground colour saturates: the model reads the distance to the nearest building as colour up to this far (default 100, what it was fed). Number Color Map CM Color map: Viridis, Turbo, or Inferno. Text Run Run the prediction. Momentary - resets when the result arrives. Boolean

docs.title: Output
docs.text: Name Nickname Description Type Wind Speed U Predicted pedestrian wind speeds. Number Result Mesh M Colored wind-speed result mesh. Mesh

docs.title: Wind Rose Cluster - [source code]
docs.text: Cluster annual wind conditions into a budget of representative directions using k-means over hourly wind vectors (speed x direction): frequent, strong conditions attract the budget, and each cluster reports an observed direction/speed pair plus its frequency. Without wired speeds, clusters directions alone (unit vectors). Method: Kastner & Dogan (2022), Building and Environment 212:108639, doi:10.1016/j.buildenv.2021.108639; Kastner & Dogan (2019), Building Simulation 2019, Rome 621-628, doi:10.26868/25222708.2019.210458.

docs.title: Input
docs.text: Name Nickname Description Type Directions Dirs Wind directions in degrees (e.g. hourly values from an EPW). Number Budget Maximum number of representative directions (clusters), e.g. 8 or 16. Integer Wind Speeds U Hourly wind speeds (m/s) paired with Directions (optional). When wired, the clustering runs over wind VECTORS (speed x direction), so speed and frequency both shape the representative set; calm hours (< 0.5 m/s) are excluded. Number

docs.title: Output
docs.text: Name Nickname Description Type Wind Directions Dirs Distinct representative wind directions in degrees, sorted ascending; plug into the ABL or Uniform Flow component's Wind Directions input. Number Wind Speeds U Representative wind speed (m/s) per cluster — the observed speed of the cluster's medoid hour, aligned with Wind Directions; plug into the ABL component's Wind Speed input. Requires wired input speeds. Number Frequencies Freq Fraction of (non-calm) hours in each cluster, aligned with Wind Directions — the per-direction weights for annual wind-comfort statistics. Sums to 1. Number

docs.title: Window Air Exchange - [source code]
docs.text: Air exchange through an open window (Maas 1995) and the steady-state CO2 it supports.

docs.title: Input
docs.text: Name Nickname Description Type Opening Area A Effective free opening area (m2). Number Wind Speed U Outdoor wind speed at 10 m (m/s). Number Sash Height H Height of the openable sash (m) — drives the buoyancy term. Number Temp Difference dT Indoor minus outdoor air temperature (K). Sign is ignored. Number Room Volume V Room volume (m3), for air changes per hour. Number CO2 Rate Q CO2 generation per occupant (L/s) — see the Occupant CO2 component. Number Occupants N Number of occupants. Integer

docs.title: Output
docs.text: Name Nickname Description Type Flow Fl Air exchange through the opening (m3/h). Number Air Changes ACH Air changes per hour. Number Steady CO2 C Steady-state indoor CO2 (ppm) at that flow and occupancy. Number

docs.title: Write Run Scripts - [source code]
docs.text: Writes meshing and simulation scripts (.bat / .sh) into a Scripts/ folder under the wind study, so the workflow can be launched manually outside Grasshopper. The scripts match what the Run component executes. Write the study to disk first (Wind Case 'Write').

docs.title: Input
docs.text: Name Nickname Description Type Case C The wind study to generate run scripts for (Wind Case output). Generic Data Parallel P Generate scripts that decompose and run in parallel (MPI). Boolean CPUs N Number of subdomains (MPI ranks) for parallel meshing and simulation. Leave unset (or <= 1) for automatic: the case's decomposeParDict count if > 1, else half the host cores. Integer Probe Name PName FALLBACK only: the post-process scripts are generated automatically for every probe setup the Probe component(s) have written into the cases, each under its own chosen name (05_PostProcess__). This input is used only when NO probe setup exists yet. Default 'probes'. Text Write W Set to true to (re)write the scripts into the study's Scripts/ folder. Boolean

docs.title: Output
docs.text: Name Nickname Description Type Scripts Folder F Path to the Scripts/ folder containing the generated batch/shell files. Text Logs L Names of the scripts that were written. Text
